children.title: Convex Piecewise-Linear Models
children.top_down_role: Epigraph and segment representations for convex piecewise-linear functions.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Piecewise-Linear Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraph representation of a convex polyhedral function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be the finite convex piecewise-linear function \[f(x)=\max_{r=1,\ldots,m}\{a_r^\top x+b_r\}.\] Its epigraph is represented exactly by the linear inequalities \[t\geq a_r^\top x+b_r\qquad(r=1,\ldots,m).\] Consequently, minimizing \(f(x)\) over any feasible set is equivalent to minimizing \(t\) subject to these inequalities and the original constraints. No integer variable is required because the maximum of affine pieces is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The epigraph of a convex piecewise-linear function is the intersection of linear halfspaces, so minimization needs no segment-selection binaries.
assumptions_latex: \(f(x)=\max_{r=1,\ldots,m}(a_r^\top x+b_r)\) is finite on its domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{epi}f=\{(x,t):t\geq a_r^\top x+b_r\text{ for all }r\}\).

notation.meaning: Slope vector and intercept of affine piece r.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The epigraph representation is correct for a finite convex piecewise-linear function expressed as a maximum of finitely many affine functions, and the representation kind fits the container. No source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Disjunctive Piecewise-Linear Geometry Family
children.top_down_role: Disjunctive representations of nonconvex or discontinuous graphs and epigraphs.

children.title: Nonconvex Piecewise-Linear Graphs
children.top_down_role: Piecewise-linear graph structures whose global geometry is nonconvex.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Piecewise-Linear Graphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact segment-selection model for a continuous univariate graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\xi_0<\cdots<\xi_m\), and let \(f\) be affine on every \([\xi_{s-1},\xi_s]\), with values \(f_i=f(\xi_i)\). Its graph is represented by \[x=\sum_{i=0}^m\xi_i\lambda_i,\quad t=\sum_{i=0}^mf_i\lambda_i,\quad \sum_{i=0}^m\lambda_i=1,\quad \sum_{s=1}^mz_s=1,\] where \(z_s\in\{0,1\}\), \(\lambda_i\geq0\), \(\lambda_0\leq z_1\), \(\lambda_m\leq z_m\), and \(\lambda_i\leq z_i+z_{i+1}\) for \(1\leq i<m\). Exactly two adjacent breakpoint weights can be positive, so \((x,t)\) lies on one graph segment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Selecting one segment and allowing weights only at its adjacent breakpoints exactly represents a continuous nonconvex piecewise-linear graph.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is continuous and affine on each breakpoint interval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The projection onto \((x,t)\) equals \(\{(x,f(x)):x\in[\xi_0,\xi_m]\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The segment-selection formulation exactly projects to the continuous univariate piecewise-linear graph and is appropriately classified as a representation. It lacks an inspectable source citation.

children.title: Discontinuous Piecewise-Linear Graphs
children.top_down_role: Piecewise-linear graph structures containing jumps or separated branches.

knowledge_statements.title: Discontinuous Piecewise-Linear Graphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Disaggregated union model allowing distinct one-sided endpoint values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For segments \(s=1,\ldots,m\), let the graph piece join \((\xi_{s-1},v_s^-)\) to \((\xi_s,v_s^+)\), without requiring adjacent endpoint values to agree. Introduce \(z_s\in\{0,1\}\) and \(\theta_s^-,\theta_s^+\geq0\) satisfying \[\theta_s^-+\theta_s^+=z_s,\qquad \sum_{s=1}^mz_s=1,\] \[x=\sum_{s=1}^m(\xi_{s-1}\theta_s^-+\xi_s\theta_s^+),\qquad t=\sum_{s=1}^m(v_s^-\theta_s^-+v_s^+\theta_s^+).\] The projection is exactly the union of the closed affine segments; if two pieces assign different values at a shared breakpoint, both graph points are retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Selecting one disaggregated segment exactly models a discontinuous piecewise-linear graph, including multiple values at shared breakpoints.
assumptions_latex: Each graph piece is the closed segment between its stated endpoints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The projection onto \((x,t)\) is the union of the specified affine graph segments.

notation.meaning: Endpoint values of graph segment s.
Disaggregated endpoint weights for segment s.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed disaggregated system exactly represents the stated union of closed affine segments. Because retaining both values at a shared breakpoint makes the object a potentially set-valued graph relation rather than the graph of a single-valued discontinuous function, an authoritative source with an explicit endpoint convention is required.

children.title: Nonconvex Epigraph Regimes
children.top_down_role: Epigraph representations requiring explicit treatment of nonconvex pieces.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Epigraph Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite polyhedral-cell representation and convexity classification of a piecewise-linear epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D=\bigcup_{r=1}^m P_r\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), where each \(P_r\) is a polyhedron, and suppose the affine formulas \(a_r^\top x+b_r\) agree on every overlap \(P_r\cap P_s\), thereby defining \(f:D\to\mathbb R\). Then
\[\operatorname{epi}_D(f)=\bigcup_{r=1}^m\{(x,t)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R:x\in P_r,\ t\ge a_r^\top x+b_r\}.\]
If \(D\) is convex, \(\operatorname{epi}_D(f)\) is convex if and only if \(f\) is convex on \(D\). Consequently, the epigraph is nonconvex whenever \(D\) is nonconvex, or whenever \(D\) is convex and \(f\) is nonconvex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The restricted epigraph is the union of the cellwise polyhedral epigraphs. It is nonconvex if the domain is nonconvex, and on a convex domain it is nonconvex exactly when the function is nonconvex.
assumptions_latex: The affine formulas agree on overlaps, so \(f\) is single-valued.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{epi}_D(f)=\bigcup_{r=1}^m\{(x,t)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R:x\in P_r,\ t\ge a_r^\top x+b_r\}\).

notation.meaning: Epigraph of f restricted to D.

children.title: Breakpoint-Transition Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Modeling distinctions at jumps, excluded intervals, or incompatible adjacent pieces.

knowledge_statements.title: Breakpoint-Transition Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility conditions at adjacent univariate piecewise-linear segments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let consecutive intervals be \(I_r=[\tau_{r-1},\tau_r]\) and \(I_{r+1}=[\tau_r,\tau_{r+1}]\), with affine pieces \(f_r(x)=a_rx+b_r\) and \(f_{r+1}(x)=a_{r+1}x+b_{r+1}\). The breakpoint \(\tau_r\) is a continuous transition precisely when
\[a_r\tau_r+b_r=a_{r+1}\tau_r+b_{r+1}.\]
If this equality fails, a single-valued model must assign \(\tau_r\) to one side or prescribe a separate breakpoint value. A formulation permitting both unequal endpoint values represents a set-valued or disjunctive graph rather than an ordinary function graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adjacent affine pieces meet continuously exactly when their endpoint values agree; otherwise endpoint ownership or an explicit breakpoint value is required.
assumptions_latex: Each affine formula applies on its stated interval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\text{ is continuous at }\tau_r\iff a_r\tau_r+b_r=a_{r+1}\tau_r+b_{r+1}\).

children.title: Separable Piecewise-Linear Models
children.top_down_role: Piecewise-linear structures decomposable into univariate component terms.

knowledge_statements.title: Separable Piecewise-Linear Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive coordinatewise separability on a Cartesian-product domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D=\prod_{i=1}^n D_i\subseteq\mathbb R^n\). A piecewise-linear function \(F:D\to\mathbb R\) is separable when there exist univariate piecewise-linear functions \(f_i:D_i\to\mathbb R\) and a constant \(c\) such that
\[F(x)=c+\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x_i)\qquad(x\in D).\]
Consequently, an epigraph model may introduce variables \(t_i\) satisfying \(t_i=f_i(x_i)\) or \(t_i\ge f_i(x_i)\), as appropriate, and aggregate them through \(t=c+\sum_i t_i\) or \(t\ge c+\sum_i t_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A piecewise-linear model is separable when its value is a constant plus a sum of univariate piecewise-linear component values.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is a Cartesian product of coordinate domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x)=c+\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x_i)\) for every \(x\in D\).

children.title: Nonseparable Piecewise-Linear Models
children.top_down_role: Piecewise-linear structures involving coupled multivariate arguments.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonseparable Piecewise-Linear Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of additive coordinatewise decomposition on a product domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D=\prod_{i=1}^n D_i\). A piecewise-linear function \(F:D\to\mathbb R\) is nonseparable when no constant \(c\) and univariate functions \(f_i:D_i\to\mathbb R\) satisfy
\[F(x)=c+\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x_i)\qquad\text{for every }x\in D.\]
Its affine pieces may therefore depend jointly on several coordinates, and an exact formulation generally requires cells in \(\mathbb R^n\), shared disjunctions, or auxiliary variables representing coupled affine expressions rather than independent coordinatewise segment selections.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A piecewise-linear function is nonseparable when it cannot be expressed as a constant plus independent univariate component functions.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is piecewise linear on a finite polyhedral subdivision of \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nexists(c,f_1,\ldots,f_n)\text{ such that }F(x)=c+\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x_i)\text{ for all }x\in D\).

children.title: Multivariate Polyhedral Complexes
children.top_down_role: Polyhedral subdivisions supporting multivariate piecewise-linear representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Multivariate Polyhedral Complexes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite cell complexes supporting multivariate piecewise-affine functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A finite family \(\mathcal P\) of polyhedra in \(\mathbb R^n\) is a polyhedral complex when every face of every \(P\in\mathcal P\) belongs to \(\mathcal P\), and for all \(P,Q\in\mathcal P\), the intersection \(P\cap Q\) is empty or a face of both. Its support is
\[|\mathcal P|=\bigcup_{P\in\mathcal P}P.\]
A function \(F:|\mathcal P|\to\mathbb R\) is piecewise affine over \(\mathcal P\) when its restriction to every maximal cell is affine, with coincident values on shared faces whenever \(F\) is required to be continuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedral complex is a face-closed family of compatible polyhedra; affine formulas on its maximal cells define a multivariate piecewise-affine function.
assumptions_latex: All cells lie in the common ambient space \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\mathcal P|=\bigcup_{P\in\mathcal P}P\) supports a cellwise-affine representation of \(F\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically standard and well formed, but the record has no citation. A targeted polyhedral-geometry source with a definition, section, or page locator is required.

children.title: Cross-Variable Coupling
children.top_down_role: Dependence among variables that prevents componentwise separation.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Variable Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A finite-difference witness for failure of additive separability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D=\prod_{k=1}^n D_k\) and \(F:D\to\mathbb R\). Cross-variable coupling between coordinates \(i\ne j\) is witnessed if there are fixed remaining coordinates and values \(u_i,v_i\in D_i\), \(u_j,v_j\in D_j\) such that all four resulting points lie in \(D\) and
\[F(u_i,u_j)+F(v_i,v_j)-F(u_i,v_j)-F(v_i,u_j)\ne0.\]
Any such witness rules out a representation \(F(x)=c+\sum_k f_k(x_k)\). For a piecewise-affine function, the witness can arise from a jointly dependent affine expression or from cell boundaries whose selection depends on multiple coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero rectangular mixed difference witnesses cross-variable coupling and disproves any additive coordinatewise decomposition.
assumptions_latex: The four evaluations use identical values for every coordinate other than \(i\) and \(j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(u_i,u_j)+F(v_i,v_j)\ne F(u_i,v_j)+F(v_i,u_j)\Rightarrow F\text{ is not additively separable}.\)

children.title: Piecewise-Linear Encoding Families

knowledge_statements.title: Piecewise-Linear Encoding Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Code-based embedded-union representation underlying piecewise-linear formulation families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S=\bigcup_{r=1}^m S_r\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), where each \(S_r\) is a polyhedron. Let \(H=\{h^1,\ldots,h^m\}\subseteq\mathbb Z^q\), and assume every \(h^r\) is a vertex of \(\operatorname{conv}(H)\). Define
\[Q=\operatorname{conv}\Bigl(\bigcup_{r=1}^m(S_r\times\{h^r\})\Bigr).\]
Then
\[\operatorname{proj}_x\{(x,y)\in Q:y\in H\}=\bigcup_{r=1}^m S_r.\]
Thus \((x,y)\in Q\) together with \(y\in H\) is an exact embedded-union representation. Convex-combination, disaggregated, incremental, logarithmic, and related piecewise-linear formulations use different extended variables and linking descriptions; each represents the intended union only when its own linking constraints are exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A code-based embedding represents a polyhedral union exactly when the allowed piece codes are vertices of their code hull; common piecewise-linear formulations differ in their extended variables and exact linking descriptions.
assumptions_latex: \(H=\{h^1,\ldots,h^m\}\subseteq\mathbb Z^q\), and every \(h^r\) is a vertex of \(\operatorname{conv}(H)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x\{(x,y)\in Q:y\in H\}=\bigcup_{r=1}^m S_r\).

notation.meaning: Polyhedron for piece or segment r.
Vertex code assigned to piece r.

children.title: Separable On–Off Perspectives
children.top_down_role: Perspective structures attached to individual activated components.

knowledge_statements.title: Separable On–Off Perspectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed convex-hull formulation for independently activated convex components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each \(i\), let \(X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{d_i}\) be closed and convex with \(0\in X_i\), and let \(f_i:X_i\to\mathbb R_+\) be proper, closed, and convex with \(f_i(0)=0\). The closed convex hull of the on–off epigraph alternatives \(z_i=0,x_i=0,t_i\ge0\) and \(z_i=1,x_i\in X_i,t_i\ge f_i(x_i)\) is
\[0\le z_i\le1,\qquad x_i\in z_iX_i,\qquad t_i\ge f_i^\pi(x_i,z_i),\]
where \(f_i^\pi(x_i,z_i)=z_i f_i(x_i/z_i)\) for \(z_i>0\) and is its closed extension at \(z_i=0\). Independent components are aggregated by summing their epigraph variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each independently activated convex component has a closed convex hull described by its perspective function and scaled domain.
assumptions_latex: \(X_i\) is closed and convex and contains \(0\).
\(f_i\) is proper, closed, convex, nonnegative, and satisfies \(f_i(0)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{clconv}(S_i^0\cup S_i^1)=\{(x_i,t_i,z_i):0\le z_i\le1,\ x_i\in z_iX_i,\ t_i\ge f_i^\pi(x_i,z_i)\}.\)

notation.meaning: Binary activation variable, relaxed in the hull.
Closed perspective of component function f_i.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: An authoritative perspective-hull source is required. As written, the closed-hull claim also needs a precise convention for the scaled domain at z_i=0 or stronger boundedness/recession hypotheses; for unbounded X_i, the closure can contain nonzero recession directions not captured by the ordinary set 0X_i={0}.

children.title: Group-Activation Perspectives
children.top_down_role: Perspective structures shared across groups or blocks of variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Group-Activation Perspectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perspective hull for a block controlled by one activation variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X_G\subseteq\mathbb R^{d_G}\) be closed and convex with \(0\in X_G\), and let \(f_G:X_G\to\mathbb R_+\) be proper, closed, and convex with \(f_G(0)=0\). For one binary variable \(z_G\) activating the entire block \(x_G\), the closed convex hull of the inactive and active epigraphs is
\[0\le z_G\le1,\qquad x_G\in z_GX_G,\qquad t_G\ge f_G^\pi(x_G,z_G).\]
Here \(f_G^\pi(x_G,z_G)=z_Gf_G(x_G/z_G)\) for \(z_G>0\), with its closed extension at zero. The shared \(z_G\) preserves coupling among all coordinates in the group.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block sharing one activation variable is convexified through the perspective of its joint convex function and its scaled joint domain.
assumptions_latex: \(X_G\) is closed and convex and contains \(0\).
\(f_G\) is proper, closed, convex, nonnegative, and satisfies \(f_G(0)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{clconv}(S_G^0\cup S_G^1)=\{(x_G,t_G,z_G):0\le z_G\le1,\ x_G\in z_GX_G,\ t_G\ge f_G^\pi(x_G,z_G)\}.\)

notation.meaning: Index set of the activated block.
Closed perspective of the joint block function.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The block-perspective structure fits the leaf, but the exact closed-hull theorem lacks evidence and does not specify how recession directions are handled at zero activation. A source and sufficient boundedness or recession-compatible hypotheses are required.

children.title: Perspective Realization Interface Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Modeling realizations of perspective-strengthened structures.

children.title: Linear Perspective Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Linear modeling realizations of perspective-strengthened structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Perspective Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact linear realization for polyhedral convex perspective epigraphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(X=\{x:Bx\le d\}\) contains \(0\) and
\[f(x)=\max_{k=1,\ldots,K}\{a_k^\top x+b_k\}\]
is a proper convex piecewise-linear function on \(X\). For \(z\ge0\), the perspective epigraph has the linear interface
\[Bx\le dz,\qquad t\ge a_k^\top x+b_kz\quad(k=1,\ldots,K).\]
For \(z>0\), these inequalities are equivalent to \(x/z\in X\) and \(t\ge zf(x/z)\). With the appropriate recession-compatible closure at \(z=0\), they describe the closed perspective epigraph and can be placed directly in an LP or MILP formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex piecewise-linear perspective is represented exactly by scaling its polyhedral domain and affine epigraph inequalities by the activation variable.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is the finite maximum of the stated affine functions on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{epi}(f^\pi)=\{(x,t,z):z\ge0,\ Bx\le dz,\ t\ge a_k^\top x+b_kz\ \forall k\}\), using the closed extension at \(z=0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The homogenized linear inequalities are plausible and correctly targeted to the linear-interface leaf, but the exact closed-perspective equality is a nontrivial representation claim with no cited source. An authoritative locator covering the zero-scaling closure is required.

children.title: Conic Perspective Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Conic modeling realizations preserving perspective structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Conic Perspective Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogenized conic representation of a perspective epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\) be a closed convex cone, and suppose a closed convex epigraph has the conic representation
\[f(x)\le t\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad Ax+bt+c\in K.\]
Its homogenized perspective interface is
\[Ax+bt+cz\in K,\qquad z\ge0.\]
For \(z>0\), conicity makes this equivalent to \(A(x/z)+b(t/z)+c\in K\), hence to \(t\ge zf(x/z)\). At \(z=0\), the same conic system supplies the recession closure. Additional conic constraints defining the domain of \(f\) must be homogenized by the same replacement of constant terms with multiples of \(z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conic epigraph is perspectivized by homogenizing every constant term with the activation variable, preserving an exact conic interface.
assumptions_latex: The displayed conic system represents the closed epigraph of a proper convex function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{epi}(f^\pi)=\{(x,t,z):z\ge0,\ Ax+bt+cz\in K\}\), including its recession closure.

notation.meaning: Data of the conic epigraph representation.

source_refs.locator: Subgradient based outer approximation for mixed integer second order cone programming p. 41

source_witnesses.locator: Subgradient based outer approximation for mixed integer second order cone programming p. 41

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited outer-approximation chapter does not clearly support the general exact conic homogenization theorem stated here. Full support is needed for the claim that the z=0 conic slice gives precisely the recession closure, including any required nonemptiness or representability hypotheses.

children.title: Outer-Approximation Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Interfaces exposing perspective structure through progressively refined linear approximations.

knowledge_statements.title: Outer-Approximation Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Supporting-hyperplane interface for differentiable convex perspectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) be closed and convex, and differentiable at \(\bar x\in\operatorname{ri}(D)\). For the perspective \(g(x,z)=zf(x/z)\) with \(z>0\), convexity yields the globally valid linear inequality
\[t\ge \nabla f(\bar x)^\top x+\bigl(f(\bar x)-\nabla f(\bar x)^\top\bar x\bigr)z.\]
An outer-approximation interface maintains a finite set of such cuts and adds a violated cut after evaluating a relaxation point with positive \(z\). The intersection of all cuts over supporting points, together with the scaled-domain constraints and the recession closure at \(z=0\), equals the closed perspective epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perspective outer approximation uses tangent inequalities parameterized by points in the original function domain and adds violated cuts as needed.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex on \(D\).
\(f\) is differentiable at each selected supporting point \(\bar x\).
Scaled-domain and zero-activation closure constraints are enforced separately.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t\ge \nabla f(\bar x)^\top x+\bigl(f(\bar x)-\nabla f(\bar x)^\top\bar x\bigr)z\) is valid for every selected \(\bar x\).

notation.meaning: Supporting point in the original domain.

source_refs.locator: Using interior-point methods within an outer approximation framework for mixed integer nonlinear programming p. 225

source_witnesses.locator: Using interior-point methods within an outer approximation framework for mixed integer nonlinear programming p. 225

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed tangent inequality is valid, but the cited general outer-approximation section does not establish the perspective-specific cut formula or the stronger assertion that all such differentiable-point cuts recover the entire closed perspective epigraph under the stated hypotheses. A targeted source or strengthened hypotheses are required.

children.title: Interface-Selection Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Representability distinctions affecting the choice among linear, conic, or approximation interfaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Interface-Selection Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundaries among exact linear, conic, and cutting-plane realizations of a closed convex perspective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, closed, and convex, and let \(f^\pi(x,z)\) denote its closed perspective for \(z\ge 0\). A finite linear interface is exact only when \(\operatorname{epi} f^\pi\) is polyhedral. A conic interface is exact when this epigraph has an available finite representation by the solver's supported closed convex cones. Otherwise, outer approximation is valid when a separation oracle supplies globally valid supporting inequalities for \(\operatorname{epi} f^\pi\), but it is generally not a finite exact formulation unless the cutting process terminates finitely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use linear constraints for polyhedral perspectives, supported cones for conic-representable perspectives, and outer approximation when only valid separation is available.
assumptions_latex: \(z\ge 0\), with the closed perspective convention at \(z=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{epi} f^\pi\) determines whether the interface is finitely linear, finitely conic, or requires iterative outer approximation.

notation.meaning: Closed perspective of the convex function.

children.title: Factorable Expression Reformulations
children.top_down_role: Decomposition of composite nonlinear expressions into elemental relations.

knowledge_statements.title: Factorable Expression Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact extended representation obtained from an acyclic decomposition into elemental operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), and let \(F:D\to\mathbb R\) be represented by a finite directed acyclic expression graph. Its leaves are components of \(x\in D\) or constants, and each internal node \(k\) computes \(v_k=\phi_k(v_{p_1(k)},\ldots,v_{p_{r_k}(k)})\). Let \(r\) be the root node and define \(S_{\mathrm{lift}}\) by all leaf assignments and internal-node equations, with \(t=v_r\). If every elemental relation is imposed exactly on its stated domain, then \(\operatorname{proj}_{x,t}(S_{\mathrm{lift}})=\{(x,t):x\in D,\ t=F(x)\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assign an auxiliary variable to every internal node of a finite acyclic expression graph and impose each elemental relation exactly; projecting onto the inputs and root output recovers the graph of the original expression.
assumptions_latex: \(F:D\to\mathbb R\) has a finite acyclic expression graph.
Every elemental relation is imposed exactly on its stated domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_{x,t}(S_{\mathrm{lift}})=\{(x,t):x\in D,\ t=F(x)\}\).

notation.meaning: Auxiliary value assigned to expression-graph node k.
Elemental function at internal node k.
Root node of the expression graph.

children.title: Block-Separable Reformulations
children.top_down_role: Reorganization of nonlinear structure into weakly coupled blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Separable Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact lifting that isolates block-local mappings and retains their explicit coupling relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(b=1,\ldots,B\), let \(X_b\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_b}\), let \(T_b:X_b\to\mathbb R^{p_b}\), let \(A_b\in\mathbb R^{q\times p_b}\), and let \(a\in\mathbb R^q\). Define \(S_{\mathrm{original}}=\{x=(x^1,\ldots,x^B):x^b\in X_b,\ \sum_{b=1}^B A_bT_b(x^b)=a\}\). Introduce \(u^b\in\mathbb R^{p_b}\) and the exact block relation \(S_b=\{(x^b,u^b):x^b\in X_b,\ u^b=T_b(x^b)\}\). Then \(\operatorname{proj}_x\{(x,u):(x^b,u^b)\in S_b\ \text{for all }b,\ \sum_{b=1}^B A_bu^b=a\}=S_{\mathrm{original}}\). Integrality restrictions may be included in the sets \(X_b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Represent each block-local mapping by an exact lifted relation and couple the exported block variables explicitly; projection then recovers the original block-separable feasible set.
assumptions_latex: Each \(S_b\) is the exact graph of \(T_b\) over \(X_b\).
The displayed coupling equation contains every cross-block relation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x\{(x,u):(x^b,u^b)\in S_b\ \forall b,\ \sum_{b=1}^B A_bu^b=a\}=S_{\mathrm{original}}\).

notation.meaning: Feasible domain of block b, including any block-local integrality restrictions.
Block-local mapping exported to the coupling relation.
Lifted interface variable for block b.
Exact graph of the block-local mapping.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Interaction-graph lifting of MINLP functions into block terms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines coupling sets for a partition and the resulting auxiliary-variable function representation. The extract does not specify the consistency constraints needed for a complete equivalent reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let J_1,\ldots,J_p be a partition of the vertex set V, and for k=1,\ldots,p define
R_k=\left\{i\in\bigcup_{l=k+1}^{p}J_l\mid (i,j)\in E_{\mathrm{sparse}}\text{ for some }j\in J_k\right\}.
Then there exist functions \widetilde h_{i,k}:\mathbb R^{|J_k|}\times\mathbb R^{|R_k|}\to\mathbb R such that
h_i(x)=\sum_{k=1}^{p}\widetilde h_{i,k}(x_{J_k},x_{R_k}),\qquad i=0,\ldots,m.
Replacing x_{R_k} by y_k\in\mathbb R^{|R_k|} defines
\widetilde h_i(x,y_1,\ldots,y_p)=\sum_{k=1}^{p}\widetilde h_{i,k}(x_{J_k},y_k).
If the original problem is block-separable with respect to the blocks J_k, then R_k=\varnothing for every k; if it is not block-separable, at least one R_k is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an arbitrary partition of the sparse interaction graph, each block's coupling set contains later-block vertices adjacent to that block. The model functions can be expressed as sums of terms involving a block and its coupling variables, after which auxiliary copies of those coupling variables define a blockwise function representation. Every coupling set is empty in the already block-separable case, whereas a nonseparable formulation has at least one nonempty coupling set. The displayed extract does not give the consistency constraints required for a complete equivalent lifted model.
assumptions_latex: R_k=\left\{i\in\bigcup_{l=k+1}^{p}J_l\mid (i,j)\in E_{\mathrm{sparse}}\text{ for some }j\in J_k\right\},\quad k=1,\ldots,p.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\,\widetilde h_{i,k}:\mathbb R^{|J_k|}\times\mathbb R^{|R_k|}\to\mathbb R:\quad h_i(x)=\sum_{k=1}^{p}\widetilde h_{i,k}(x_{J_k},x_{R_k}),\quad \widetilde h_i(x,y_1,\ldots,y_p)=\sum_{k=1}^{p}\widetilde h_{i,k}(x_{J_k},y_k);\quad \bigl[\text{block-separable}\Rightarrow R_k=\varnothing\ \forall k\bigr],\ \bigl[\text{not block-separable}\Rightarrow\exists k:R_k\ne\varnothing\bigr].

children.title: Quadratic Liftings
children.top_down_role: Lifted representations for quadratic interaction structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Liftings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact matrix lifting of quadratic forms, distinguished from its convex rank relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), introduce a symmetric matrix \(X\in\mathbb S^n\) and impose \(X=xx^\top\). Then every quadratic expression satisfies \(x^\top Qx+q^\top x+c=\langle Q,X\rangle+q^\top x+c\). Equivalently, the lifting relation is \(\begin{pmatrix}1&x^\top\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\) together with rank one. Dropping the rank condition gives a convex semidefinite relaxation rather than an exact reformulation. Any original integrality restrictions on components of \(x\) remain unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace quadratic products by a matrix variable equal to the outer product; omitting the rank-one condition yields only a relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X=xx^\top\Rightarrow x^\top Qx=\langle Q,X\rangle\), while positive semidefiniteness alone is generally inexact.

notation.meaning: Lifted matrix representing the outer product of x.
Trace inner product of symmetric matrices.

children.title: Polynomial Liftings

knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial Liftings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite lifting of selected monomials by variables and multiplicative consistency equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p(x)=\sum_{\alpha\in A}c_\alpha x^\alpha\) be a polynomial with finite exponent set \(A\subset\mathbb Z_+^n\). Introduce \(y_\alpha\) for each required monomial and impose \(y_0=1\), \(y_{e_i}=x_i\), and sufficient multiplication identities \(y_{\alpha+\beta}=y_\alpha y_\beta\) to construct every \(\alpha\in A\). Then \(p(x)=\sum_{\alpha\in A}c_\alpha y_\alpha\). With all identities exact, projection recovers the polynomial graph; relaxing any identities generally enlarges it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Represent each needed monomial by an auxiliary variable and enforce a complete set of multiplication identities to obtain an exact polynomial lifting.
assumptions_latex: The multiplication identities generate every monomial indexed by \(A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_\alpha=x^\alpha\) for every \(\alpha\in A\), hence \(p(x)=\sum_{\alpha\in A}c_\alpha y_\alpha\).

notation.meaning: Finite set of polynomial exponent vectors.
Lifted variable for monomial indexed by alpha.

children.title: Bilinear Interaction Liftings
children.top_down_role: Auxiliary representations exposing pairwise product structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Bilinear Interaction Liftings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact product lifting and its bounded convex-hull relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For bounded variables \(x\in[\ell_x,u_x]\) and \(y\in[\ell_y,u_y]\), replace each occurrence of \(xy\) by \(w\) and impose \(w=xy\) for an exact lifting. The convex hull of this bilinear graph over the rectangle is described by the four McCormick inequalities: \(w\ge \ell_xy+\ell_yx-\ell_x\ell_y\), \(w\ge u_xy+u_yx-u_xu_y\), \(w\le u_xy+\ell_yx-u_x\ell_y\), and \(w\le \ell_xy+u_yx-\ell_xu_y\). The inequalities alone are generally a relaxation of the graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lift a product into a new variable; four McCormick inequalities give its rectangular convex hull but not the product graph itself.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w=xy\) is exact, whereas the four displayed inequalities describe \(\operatorname{conv}\{(x,y,xy)\}\).

notation.meaning: Lifted variable representing the bilinear product.

review_flags: McCormick convex-hull theorem lacks a supplied supporting locator

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The four inequalities and exact-versus-relaxation distinction are standard, but the convex-hull theorem has no supplied source or locator.

children.title: Degree-Reduction Liftings
children.top_down_role: Layered representations that reduce higher-degree interactions to lower-degree components.

knowledge_statements.title: Degree-Reduction Liftings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive exact conversion of high-degree monomials into linear and bilinear relations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite polynomial system. For every monomial \(m=x_{i_1}\cdots x_{i_d}\) with \(d>2\), choose a factorization \(m=ab\), introduce a variable \(w_m\), impose \(w_m=ab\), and replace \(m\) by \(w_m\). Recursively introduce variables for factors whose degree exceeds two, reusing variables for repeated factors. Stop when every defining relation has degree at most two. Output the resulting lifted system. Because each auxiliary variable is linked by an equality to its defining product, projection onto the original variables equals the input system's feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recursively replace high-degree products by auxiliary variables and exact bilinear equalities until all relations are at most quadratic.
assumptions_latex: The input contains finitely many polynomial expressions.
Every introduced product relation is enforced exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(S_{\mathrm{reduced}})=S_{\mathrm{input}}\), and every lifted defining equation has degree at most two.

notation.meaning: Auxiliary variable assigned to monomial or factor m.

children.title: Absolute-Value Representations
children.top_down_role: Representations centered on absolute-value terms in objectives or constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Absolute-Value Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraph and exact-equality representations for the absolute value of an affine residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r(x)\) be affine and let \(t\in\mathbb R\). The epigraph identity is \(t\ge |r(x)|\) if and only if \(t\ge r(x)\) and \(t\ge-r(x)\). If \(t\) occurs nowhere else in the constraints, minimizing an objective that is strictly increasing in \(t\) forces \(t=|r(x)|\) at every optimum; under weak monotonicity, a tight optimum can be selected but need not be unique. In a general feasible-set model, equality requires an explicit sign disjunction: either \(r(x)\ge0\) and \(t=r(x)\), or \(r(x)\le0\) and \(t=-r(x)\). A big-M realization of this disjunction requires finite valid bounds on \(r(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two inequalities exactly describe the absolute-value epigraph. Equality is forced by a strictly increasing minimization objective when the epigraph variable has no other role, or by an explicit sign disjunction.
assumptions_latex: Finite valid lower and upper bounds on \(r(x)\) are available if a big-M sign formulation is used.

children.title: One-Sided Deviation Models
children.top_down_role: Models distinguishing positive or negative departures from a reference.

knowledge_statements.title: One-Sided Deviation Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive- and negative-part epigraphs for directional deviations of a scalar residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a real-valued residual \(r(x)\), define \(r(x)_+=\max\{r(x),0\}\) and \(r(x)_-=\max\{-r(x),0\}\). Their epigraphs are \(d^+\ge r(x),\ d^+\ge0\) and \(d^-\ge-r(x),\ d^-\ge0\), respectively. If a deviation variable occurs nowhere else in the constraints, an objective strictly increasing in that variable forces equality at every optimum. With a merely nondecreasing objective, a tight optimum can be selected, but other optima may overestimate the deviation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative variable above a residual represents the positive-deviation epigraph, and a nonnegative variable above the negated residual represents the negative-deviation epigraph. Strictly increasing minimization makes the selected epigraph variable exact.
assumptions_latex: Any deviation variable claimed to be tight occurs nowhere else in the constraints and is minimized through a strictly increasing objective term.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{epi}(r_+)=\{(x,d^+):d^+\ge r(x),\ d^+\ge0\}\) and \(\operatorname{epi}(r_-)=\{(x,d^-):d^-\ge-r(x),\ d^-\ge0\}\).

notation.meaning: Positive and negative parts of the residual.

children.title: Two-Sided Deviation Models
children.top_down_role: Models capturing departures on both sides of a reference.

knowledge_statements.title: Two-Sided Deviation Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Signed residual decomposition into nonnegative positive and negative deviations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a real-valued residual \(r(x)\), introduce \(d^+,d^-\ge0\) and impose \(r(x)=d^+-d^-\). Every feasible decomposition satisfies \(d^++d^-\ge|r(x)|\). If \(d^+\) and \(d^-\) occur only in this decomposition, their nonnegativity restrictions, and a minimization objective containing \(\lambda(d^++d^-)\) with \(\lambda>0\), then every optimum satisfies \(d^+d^-=0\). Consequently, \(d^+=\max\{r(x),0\}\), \(d^-=\max\{-r(x),0\}\), and \(d^++d^-=|r(x)|\). Without that usage restriction or an explicit complementarity condition, the decomposition is nonunique and need not give the positive and negative parts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Split a signed residual into two nonnegative components. Minimizing their positively weighted sum makes the split exact when those components have no other model role.
assumptions_latex: \(d^+\) and \(d^-\) occur only in the decomposition, nonnegativity restrictions, and the term \(\lambda(d^++d^-)\) with \(\lambda>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d^+=\max\{r(x),0\}\), \(d^-=\max\{-r(x),0\}\), and \(d^++d^-=|r(x)|\) at every optimum under the stated usage restriction.

children.title: Distance-Based Penalties
children.top_down_role: Penalty structures based on modeled distance from targets or feasible regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Distance-Based Penalties
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifted epigraph representation of distance to a nonempty closed target set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and closed, and let \(\|\cdot\|\) be a norm. The distance penalty is \(\operatorname{dist}(x,C)=\inf_{y\in C}\|x-y\|\). Its epigraph has the lifted representation \(t\ge\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\) if and only if there exists \(y\in C\) with \(t\ge\|x-y\|\), provided the distance is attained. In finite dimensions, closedness of \(C\) ensures attainment. Linear, second-order-cone, or other convex interfaces may represent the norm epigraph according to the chosen norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Introduce a nearest-point variable in the target set and bound its norm distance from the modeled point.

children.title: Minimum Models

knowledge_statements.title: Minimum Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact bounded mixed-integer formulation for the minimum of finitely many affine expressions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a_i(x)\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\), be affine on a bounded domain \(X\), and choose constants \(M_i\ge\sup_{x\in X}\bigl(a_i(x)-\min_j a_j(x)\bigr)\). Then \(y=\min_i a_i(x)\) is represented by \(y\le a_i(x)\) for every \(i\), \(y\ge a_i(x)-M_i(1-z_i)\) for every \(i\), \(\sum_i z_i=1\), and \(z_i\in\{0,1\}\). The selected index forces equality with one expression, while all upper inequalities ensure that expression is minimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select one affine expression with a binary variable, force equality to it, and bound the result above by every candidate expression.

knowledge_statements.title: Maximum Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraph representation of a finite maximum in a minimization model.

Thus replacing an occurrence of \(\max_i a_i(x)\) in such an objective by \(y\), together with these inequalities, is exact.

children.title: Fractional Objective Reformulations

knowledge_statements.title: Fractional Objective Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parametric reformulation valid for continuous, integer, or mixed-integer feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be compact, let \(f,g:X\to\mathbb R\) be continuous, and suppose \(g(x)>0\) on \(X\). Define \(\lambda^*=\max_{x\in X} f(x)/g(x)\). Then
\[\max_{x\in X}\bigl(f(x)-\lambda^*g(x)\bigr)=0.\]
Conversely, if a scalar \(\lambda\) satisfies \(\max_{x\in X}(f(x)-\lambda g(x))=0\), then \(\lambda=\lambda^*\), and the maximizers of the difference and ratio problems coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-denominator fractional maximum equals the unique parameter for which the corresponding subtractive optimization problem has value zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda^*=\max_{x\in X}f(x)/g(x)\iff\max_{x\in X}(f(x)-\lambda^*g(x))=0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated positive-denominator parametric characterization is mathematically plausible and appropriately scoped, but no source is cited. An authoritative fractional-programming section, theorem, or page supporting both the zero-value characterization and coincidence of maximizers is required.

children.title: Ratio Constraint Reformulations
children.top_down_role: Reformulation routes for constrained ratio relations.

knowledge_statements.title: Ratio Constraint Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact cross-multiplication of a ratio inequality under a fixed positive denominator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a feasible set, let \(p,q:X\to\mathbb R\), and assume \(q(x)>0\) throughout \(X\). For any \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\),
\[\frac{p(x)}{q(x)}\le\alpha\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad p(x)-\alpha q(x)\le0.\]
Likewise, \(p(x)/q(x)\ge\alpha\) is equivalent to \(p(x)-\alpha q(x)\ge0\). Hence a ratio constraint with constant threshold can be replaced exactly by its cross-multiplied constraint without introducing a quotient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the denominator is positive, a constant-threshold ratio inequality is exactly equivalent to the corresponding cross-multiplied inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p(x)/q(x)\mathrel{\square}\alpha\iff p(x)-\alpha q(x)\mathrel{\square}0\) for \(\square\in\{\le,\ge\}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Charnes–Cooper transformation for a homogeneous linear-fractional objective
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transformation of a ratio of linear forms under a denominator that is nonzero and has a fixed sign, including inequality reversal and the nonrecoverable $t=0$ boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider $\max_{x\in X}(a^Tx)/(b^Tx)$, where $X$ is described by linear constraints and $b^Tx$ is nonzero with one fixed sign on $X$. Set $t=(b^Tx)^{-1}$ and $w=tx$. Then the objective becomes $\max a^Tw$ and the normalization is $b^Tw=1$. If an original constraint is $d^Tx\ge e$, it becomes $d^Tw-et\ge0$ when $b^Tx>0$ and $d^Tw-et\le0$ when $b^Tx<0$; other inequalities transform with the corresponding sign rule. The scale satisfies $t>0$ in the positive-denominator case and $t<0$ in the negative-denominator case. A transformed solution with $t\ne0$ recovers the original variables as $x=w/t$; a point with $t=0$ has no such inverse and is outside this recovery correspondence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When a linear denominator is everywhere nonzero and has a constant sign, scale the variables by its reciprocal, normalize the transformed denominator to one, and transform every original linear constraint using the scale variable. Inequalities reverse for a negative denominator. Recover the original variables by dividing by the nonzero scale; a transformed point with zero scale is not recoverable.
assumptions_latex: X\text{ is described by linear constraints}
b^Tx\text{ has a constant sign on }X
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \frac{a^Tx}{b^Tx}=a^Tw,\qquad b^Tw=1,\qquad x=\frac{w}{t}\ \text{for }t\ne0

children.title: Sign-Indefinite Denominator Boundary
children.top_down_role: Structural limitations arising when denominator signs are not fixed.

knowledge_statements.title: Sign-Indefinite Denominator Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of global cross-multiplication when denominator sign is not fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(q\) takes both signs on \(X\), no single inequality \(p(x)-\alpha q(x)\le0\) represents \(p(x)/q(x)\le\alpha\) over all points with \(q(x)\ne0\). Indeed, for \(X=\{-1,1\}\), \(p(x)=1\), \(q(x)=x\), and \(\alpha=0\), the ratio inequality is false at \(x=1\) but true at \(x=-1\), whereas \(p(x)-\alpha q(x)=1\le0\) is false at both points. Separate sign disjunctions are therefore required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the denominator changes sign, cross-multiplication must reverse direction on the negative region, so one global transformed inequality is invalid.
assumptions_latex: There exist feasible points where \(q\) has opposite signs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A sign-disjunctive formulation is required to preserve the ratio inequality globally.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample correctly shows that naive cross-multiplication can fail when the denominator changes sign. However, the opening claim is too universal: for particular numerator and threshold choices, one transformed inequality can coincide accidentally with the ratio constraint even when q takes both signs. Likewise, sign disjunctions are a standard general remedy but are not logically required for every special instance. A corrected general-failure statement and an authoritative source locator are required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Penalty reformulation of a finite constrained integer program
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines feasibility penalties and the associated unconstrained penalized problem, including a standard violation penalty and its basic value bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb Z^n\) be finite and let \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m,h_1,\ldots,h_l\) be continuous. Define \(S=\{x\in X:g_i(x)\le0\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\ h_j(x)=0\ (j=1,\ldots,l)\}\). A penalty function satisfies \(P(x)=0\) for \(x\in S\) and \(P(x)\ge\epsilon>0\) for \(x\in X\setminus S\); one standard choice is \(P(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m\max\{g_i(x),0\}+\sum_{j=1}^l h_j(x)^2\). For \(\mu>0\), the penalty problem is \(\min_{x\in X}T(x,\mu)\), where \(T(x,\mu)=f(x)+\mu P(x)\). Since \(T(x,\mu)=f(x)\) on \(S\), \(v(\mathrm P)\ge v(\mathrm{PEN})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite integer domain, assign zero penalty to feasible points and a uniformly positive penalty to infeasible points. Adding a positive multiple of this penalty produces an unconstrained problem whose optimal value cannot exceed that of the original constrained problem. A standard penalty sums positive inequality violations and squared equality residuals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v(\mathrm P)\ge v(\mathrm{PEN})

children.title: Objective Transformations
children.top_down_role: Reformulation choices that alter objective representation while preserving the intended optimization outcome.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective Transformations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimal-solution invariance under strictly monotone scalar transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\ne\varnothing\), let \(f:X\to D\subseteq\mathbb R\), and let \(\phi:D\to\mathbb R\) be strictly increasing. Then
\[\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}f(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\phi(f(x)),\qquad \operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in X}f(x)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in X}\phi(f(x)).\]
If \(\phi\) is strictly decreasing, minimizers of \(f\) are maximizers of \(\phi\circ f\), and maximizers of \(f\) are minimizers of \(\phi\circ f\). Objective values change, but the corresponding optimizer sets do not.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strictly increasing transformations preserve minimizers and maximizers; strictly decreasing transformations interchange minimization and maximization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strict monotonicity preserves the relevant ordering of all feasible objective values.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be a finite, nonempty set and let \(P_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty feasible set for each \(i\in I\). Variable disaggregation introduces a copy \(x^i\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and a selector \(y_i\in\{0,1\}\) for each alternative and imposes \[x=\sum_{i\in I}x^i,\qquad x^i\in y_iP_i\quad(i\in I),\qquad \sum_{i\in I}y_i=1,\] where \(y_iP_i=\{y_iv:v\in P_i\}\). Exactly one selector equals one. Its copy belongs to the corresponding \(P_i\), while every inactive copy belongs to \(0P_i=\{0\}\). Hence the projected feasible set in the original variables is exactly \(\bigcup_{i\in I}P_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variable disaggregation gives every alternative its own variable copy, activates exactly one copy, forces inactive copies to zero, and sums the copies to recover the original variable.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+p}\) is a lifted feasible set in variables \((x,u)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a lifted feasible set \(Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+p}\) expressed in original variables \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and auxiliary variables \(u\in\mathbb{R}^p\), its lifted-space projection onto the original coordinates is \[\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\exists u\in\mathbb{R}^p,\ (x,u)\in Q\}.\] Thus an original-space point is retained precisely when it has at least one feasible auxiliary completion. When \(Q\) is a polyhedron, this coordinate projection is also a polyhedron, although an inequality description in \(x\)-space can be much larger than the lifted description.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection removes auxiliary coordinates existentially: an original vector remains feasible exactly when some auxiliary completion belongs to the lifted set.

children.title: Variable Elimination
children.top_down_role: Removal of auxiliary or original variables from a formulation description.

assumptions_latex: A finite linear system is given in variables \((x,u)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Eliminating \(u\) produces inequalities in \(x\) whose solution set is exactly \(\{x:\exists u,\ (x,u)\in Q\}\).

notation.meaning: Feasible set of the input system

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fourier-Motzkin elimination for one continuous variable.

source_refs.locator: 6.6 The Complexity of Extended Formulations p. 105

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: To eliminate a continuous variable \(u\) from a finite linear system, normalize every inequality containing \(u\) into either a lower bound \(u\ge \ell_i(x)\) or an upper bound \(u\le r_j(x)\), retaining inequalities independent of \(u\). Add every pairwise comparison \[\ell_i(x)\le r_j(x)\] for each lower-bound index \(i\) and upper-bound index \(j\), and then delete \(u\) and its bounds. The resulting system in \(x\) is feasible exactly when there exists a value of \(u\) satisfying the original system, so its feasible set equals \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fourier-Motzkin elimination compares every lower bound on a continuous variable with every upper bound, producing an exact projected linear system.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable Elimination

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be an original feasible set and let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+p}\) be a lifted formulation in coordinates \((x,u)\). The two descriptions are projection-equivalent precisely when \[S=\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\exists u\in\mathbb{R}^p,\ (x,u)\in Q\}.\] More generally, two lifted sets \(Q_1\) and \(Q_2\), possibly using different auxiliary spaces, are equivalent with respect to \(x\) when \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_1)=\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_2)\). This condition concerns feasible original vectors, not equality of auxiliary representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two formulations are projection-equivalent when eliminating their auxiliary variables yields exactly the same feasible set in the original variables.

children.title: Elimination Complexity
children.top_down_role: Description growth associated with removing variables from lifted representations.

assumptions_latex: One continuous variable occurs in \(p\) normalized lower bounds, \(q\) normalized upper bounds, and \(r\) independent inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: One Fourier-Motzkin step produces at most \(pq+r\) inequalities before redundancy removal; repeated elimination can therefore have exponential output size.

notation.meaning: Number of inequalities independent of the eliminated variable

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Raw inequality growth under Fourier-Motzkin elimination.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a normalized linear system contains \(p\) lower bounds and \(q\) upper bounds on the continuous variable being eliminated, together with \(r\) inequalities independent of that variable. Fourier-Motzkin elimination compares every lower bound with every upper bound, so one elimination step outputs at most \[pq+r\] inequalities before duplicate and redundant inequalities are removed. Because the product term can be quadratic in the current number of inequalities, repeated elimination of auxiliary variables may generate exponentially many inequalities relative to the lifted input description, even when the projection itself has a concise alternative description.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating one variable creates at most one inequality per lower-upper bound pair; repeated elimination can expand a compact lifted system exponentially.
knowledge_statements.title: Elimination Complexity

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be finite and let each nonempty polytope be \(P_i=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:A_i x\le b_i\}\). Then the convex hull of their union has the lifted representation \[\operatorname{conv}\Bigl(\bigcup_{i\in I}P_i\Bigr)=\left\{x:\begin{array}{l}x=\sum_{i\in I}x^i,\\ A_i x^i\le b_i\lambda_i\quad(i\in I),\\ \sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i=1,\quad \lambda_i\ge0\quad(i\in I)\end{array}\right\}.\] Boundedness implies that \(A_i x^i\le0\) forces \(x^i=0\), so inactive alternatives with \(\lambda_i=0\) cannot contribute nonzero recession directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The convex hull of finitely many polytopes is obtained by disaggregating variables, scaling each polytope by a convex multiplier, and summing the copies.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite family of nonempty polyhedra \(\{P_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n:i\in I\}\) has heterogeneous recession when there exist indices \(i,j\in I\) such that \[\operatorname{rec}(P_i)\ne\operatorname{rec}(P_j),\qquad \operatorname{rec}(P_i)=\{d:x+\tau d\in P_i\text{ for every }x\in P_i,\ \tau\ge0\}.\] In a homogenized disaggregated system, a component whose multiplier is zero may still carry a vector from its own recession cone. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Condensed MINLP formulation and fixed-integer subproblem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a bounded minimal-variable MINLP representation and its continuous subproblem for a fixed feasible integer vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A condensed formulation of a mixed-integer nonlinear program is a representation using as few decision variables as possible, of the form \(\min\{f(x,y):g(x,y)\le 0,\ h(x,y)=0,\ \underline{x}\le x\le\bar{x},\ \underline{y}\le y\le\bar{y},\ y\in\mathbb Z^{n_y}\}\), where \(x\in\mathbb R^{n_x}\), and \(f,g,h\) are piecewise twice differentiable and may contain if--then--else expressions. For any fixed integer vector \(\widehat y\), its continuous subproblem is \(P[\widehat y]=\min\{f(x,\widehat y):g(x,\widehat y)\le0,\ h(x,\widehat y)=0,\ \underline{x}\le x\le\bar{x}\}\); its piecewise twice-differentiable objective and constraints permit the use of a standard NLP solver to seek local minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A condensed MINLP formulation uses as few decision variables as possible. It has bounded continuous variables, bounded integer variables, and piecewise twice-differentiable objective and constraint functions, possibly expressed with if-then-else rules. Fixing an integer vector produces a continuous nonlinear subproblem in the continuous variables, for which a standard NLP solver may be used to compute local minimizers.

\widehat y\text{ is a fixed integer vector within its prescribed bounds}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(x^*\) is an extreme point of \(P_Q\), then for some \(k\in Q^*\) its lift with \(\bar x=x^*\), \((\bar y^k,\bar y_0^k)=(x^*,1)\), and \((\bar y^h,\bar y_0^h)=(0,0)\) for every \(h\in Q\setminus\{k\}\) is an extreme point of \(\mathcal P\). Conversely, every extreme point \((\bar x,\{\bar y^h,\bar y_0^h\}_{h\in Q^*})\) of \(\mathcal P\) has this form for some \(k\in Q^*\), and \(\bar x\) is an extreme point of \(P_Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extreme points of the original disjunctive polyhedron correspond to extreme points of the lifted polyhedron having exactly one active alternative with weight one; conversely, every lifted extreme point has this form and projects to an original extreme point.
assumptions_latex: (\bar x,\{\bar y^h,\bar y_0^h\}_{h\in Q^*})\in\operatorname{ext}(\mathcal P)\quad\text{in the converse direction}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^*\in\operatorname{ext}(P_Q)\iff\text{its single-active-component lift belongs to }\operatorname{ext}(\mathcal P),\text{ and every point of }\operatorname{ext}(\mathcal P)\text{ is such a lift}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: One-Variable Lift-and-Project Hull Identity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded exact projected-hull characterization for one selected index.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\widetilde A x\geq\widetilde b\}, let j\in\{1,\ldots,p\}, and let P_j(K) be the x-space projection produced by the preceding single-index lifting and linearization procedure. Then
\[
P_j(K)=\operatorname{conv}\bigl(K\cap\{x\in\mathbb R^n:x_j\in\{0,1\}\}\bigr).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The projection produced by the single-index lift-and-project procedure is exactly the convex hull of the points of K whose selected coordinate is zero or one.
assumptions_latex: P_j(K)\text{ is defined by the preceding single-index lifting, linearization, and projection procedure}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_j(K)=\operatorname{conv}\bigl(K\cap\{x\in\mathbb R^n:x_j\in\{0,1\}\}\bigr).

children.title: Projected-Face Structure
children.top_down_role: Facial behavior retained or altered under projection.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+q}\) is a nonempty polyhedron and \(P=\pi_x(Q)\), where \(\pi_x:\mathbb{R}^{n+q}\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is coordinate projection.
There exist \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(\beta\in\mathbb{R}\) such that \(c^Tx\leq\beta\) for every \(x\in P\) and \(F=\{x\in P:c^Tx=\beta\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\widehat F=Q\cap\{(x,z)\in\mathbb{R}^{n+q}:c^Tx=\beta\}\ \text{is a nonempty face of }Q,\qquad \pi_x(\widehat F)=F.\]

notation.meaning: Projection of the lifted polyhedron onto the original variables.
A nonempty face of the projected polyhedron.
The face of the lifted polyhedron exposed using only original-variable coefficients.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Faces of a projected polyhedron lift through inequalities having zero coefficients on the auxiliary variables.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every nonempty face \(F\) of \(P=\pi_x(Q)\), exposed by \(c^Tx\leq\beta\), is the projection of the nonempty face \(\widehat F=Q\cap\{(x,z):c^Tx=\beta\}\) of \(Q\). Thus \(\pi_x(\widehat F)=F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every nonempty face of the projected polyhedron is the projection of a nonempty lifted face exposed by an inequality involving only the original variables.
