children.title: Unary Encodings
children.top_down_role: One-indicator-per-alternative representations.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[y\in\{0,1\}^k,\qquad \sum_{i=1}^k y_i=1,\qquad y=e_i\ \text{for the selected alternative }i.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-hot representation of a finite alternative index.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A unary encoding assigns alternative \(i\) the code \(e_i\in\{0,1\}^k\). A selection vector \(y\) is feasible precisely when \(y\in\{0,1\}^k\) and \(\sum_{i=1}^k y_i=1\); hence exactly one coordinate is one. In a disjunctive formulation, constraints associated with alternative \(i\) are activated when \(y_i=1\). The encoding uses \(k\) binary coordinates and uniquely identifies every alternative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A unary encoding uses one binary indicator per alternative and requires exactly one indicator to equal one.
knowledge_statements.title: Unary Encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The one-hot definition is mathematically standard, precise, and appropriate for the Unary Encodings topic, but the record supplies no inspectable citation. An encoding-specific source with a section, theorem, definition, or page locator is required.

children.title: Compact Code Encoding Family
children.top_down_role: Compact code-based representations of finite alternatives.

children.title: Binary Encodings
children.top_down_role: Code-based representations using binary labels for finite alternatives.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[h:\{1,\ldots,k\}\hookrightarrow\{0,1\}^r,\qquad z=h(i)\ \text{selects alternative }i.\]

notation.meaning: Injective assignment of binary codewords to alternatives.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Injective fixed-length binary representation of a finite alternative index.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A binary encoding of \(k\) alternatives is an injective map \(h:\{1,\ldots,k\}\to\{0,1\}^r\). Alternative \(i\) is represented by imposing \(z=h(i)\) on an \(r\)-dimensional binary code variable. Injectivity is necessary and sufficient for the codeword alone to identify the selected alternative. Since \(\{0,1\}^r\) has \(2^r\) elements, such an encoding exists exactly when \(k\leq2^r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A binary encoding assigns every alternative a distinct bit vector; code length must be large enough to provide at least k codewords.
knowledge_statements.title: Binary Encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The injective fixed-length bit-vector definition is mathematically sound and the definition kind fits Binary Encodings. No source is supplied, so the terminology and formulation-specific interpretation cannot yet be reviewed against evidence.

children.title: Logarithmic-Size Encodings
children.top_down_role: Encodings whose discrete dimension scales logarithmically with the alternative count.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[r_{\min}=\left\lceil\log_2 k\right\rceil.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information-theoretic binary-variable count for injectively labeling finitely many alternatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An injective binary encoding with \(r\) coordinates can represent at most \(2^r\) alternatives, so every such encoding satisfies \(r\geq\lceil\log_2 k\rceil\). Conversely, choosing any \(k\) distinct vectors from \(\{0,1\}^{\lceil\log_2 k\rceil}\) attains this bound. Thus the alternative label requires exactly \(\lceil\log_2 k\rceil\) binary variables in the fixed-length binary-code model, excluding continuous lifting variables and formulation constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exactly ceiling(log2 k) binary coordinates are necessary and sufficient to assign distinct fixed-length codes to k alternatives.
knowledge_statements.title: Logarithmic-Size Encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact bound is correct for fixed-length injective binary labels and is properly scoped to exclude other formulation variables and constraints. The complexity-bound kind fits the terminal container, but an authoritative source with a specific locator is required.

children.title: Code Assignment Choices
children.top_down_role: Structural effects of assigning binary labels to modeled alternatives.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\|T(h(i))-T(h(j))\|_1=\|h(i)-h(j)\|_1\quad\text{for all }i,j.\]

notation.meaning: Hypercube symmetry formed by coordinate permutation and bit complementation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric invariants and noninvariants under reassignment of binary codewords.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Replacing \(h\) by \(T\circ h\) preserves injectivity, all pairwise Hamming distances, and the face-incidence geometry of \(\operatorname{conv}(h(1),\ldots,h(k))\) up to an affine hypercube symmetry. An arbitrary permutation of the alternatives among a fixed set of codewords preserves only distinctness in general: it can change which semantically adjacent alternatives receive adjacent codewords. Therefore code assignment is immaterial for label capacity but may affect an embedding formulation whose inequalities depend on alternative adjacency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hypercube symmetries preserve code geometry, while arbitrary assignments can change which alternatives are adjacent and thereby alter geometry-sensitive formulations.
knowledge_statements.title: Code Assignment Choices

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Hypercube symmetries preserve Hamming distances and affine face incidence, while reassignment can change the relation between semantic adjacency and code adjacency. However, permuting alternatives over a fixed codeword set does not change the unlabeled code polytope itself, so the claimed invariance boundary needs formulation-specific sourcing and clarification.

children.title: Relaxation Strength Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits on relaxation quality arising from compact code representations.

assumptions_latex: \(h:\{1,\ldots,k\}\to\{0,1\}^r\) is used as the sole alternative label.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[h(i)=h(j)\ \text{for some }i\neq j\quad\Longrightarrow\quad h^{-1}(h(i))\text{ is not a singleton}.\]

notation.meaning: Binary code variable in the continuous relaxation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates label validity from ideality of a particular compact extended formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Injectivity is a necessary boundary for exact identification: if \(h(i)=h(j)\) with \(i\neq j\), the code variable cannot distinguish alternatives \(i\) and \(j\). Injectivity alone does not certify an ideal formulation. A relaxation allowing \(z\in H\) may contain fractional code points and must be coupled with constraints whose projection equals the intended disjunctive hull. Hence logarithmic label size gives no general guarantee that every associated compact linear formulation has the unary formulation's relaxation strength.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distinct codes are necessary for identification, but logarithmic code size alone does not guarantee an ideal or unary-strength relaxation.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Strength Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The distinction between label injectivity and relaxation ideality is appropriate for this failure-boundary container. The stronger comparison with unary relaxation strength depends on the associated formulation class, and no source is provided to establish the intended boundary.

children.title: Adjacency-Preserving Embedding Encodings
children.top_down_role: Encodings organized around adjacency and embedded alternative geometry.

children.title: Gray-Code Encodings
children.top_down_role: Finite-alternative encodings organized by single-bit transitions.

assumptions_latex: Alternatives \(1,\ldots,k\) have a fixed linear order.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gray coding for a linearly ordered family of alternatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A Gray-code encoding is an injective map \(g:\{1,\ldots,k\}\to\{0,1\}^r\) such that successive alternatives differ in exactly one coordinate. Equivalently, \(g(1),\ldots,g(k)\) forms a simple path in the \(r\)-dimensional hypercube. A reflected binary Gray code supplies \(2^r\) such codewords, so truncating its path after \(k\) vertices produces an encoding for any \(k\leq2^r\) while retaining the successive-distance condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Gray-code encoding assigns ordered alternatives distinct bit vectors so that consecutive alternatives differ in exactly one bit.
knowledge_statements.title: Gray-Code Encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and truncated reflected-Gray-code construction are mathematically correct for linearly ordered alternatives, and the definition kind fits the container. A specific authoritative citation is still required.

children.title: Geometric Embedding Encodings
children.top_down_role: Representations based on embedding alternative labels into a geometric code space.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\pi_x\left(\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{i=1}^k(P_i\times\{h^i\})\right)=\operatorname{conv}\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^kP_i\right).\]

notation.meaning: Embedding of alternative \(i\) at its code point.
Convex hull of the embedded alternatives.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Embedding a union of polyhedra at distinct geometric code points before convexification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(Q_h=\operatorname{conv}\bigl(\bigcup_{i=1}^k(P_i\times\{h^i\})\bigr)\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+r}\). The slice \(P_i\times\{h^i\}\) records both a feasible point of alternative \(i\) and its code. Projection commutes with convexification, giving the displayed equality. If integer restrictions on the encoding coordinates are intended to recover the original union rather than merely its convex hull, additional hypotheses excluding unintended integer code points and mixed fibers are required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A geometric embedding attaches a distinct code point to each polyhedron and convexifies the resulting lifted union before projection.
knowledge_statements.title: Geometric Embedding Encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The projection identity is correct and the representation kind fits geometric embedding encodings. Distinct encoding points are not needed for that identity itself but are relevant to labeling; the conditions needed for integer recovery are formulation-specific and require an inspectable source.

children.title: Adjacency-Preserving Codes
children.top_down_role: Code assignments reflecting adjacency among modeled alternatives.

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is the prescribed adjacency graph on \(V=\{1,\ldots,k\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\{i,j\}\in E\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \|h(i)-h(j)\|_1=1.\]

notation.meaning: Graph describing which alternatives are adjacent.
Binary code assigned to each graph vertex.
Hamming distance of two binary vectors.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Edge-preserving embedding of an alternative-adjacency graph into a hypercube.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The code \(h\) is adjacency-preserving for \(G\) when every prescribed edge is mapped to a hypercube edge, equivalently when adjacent alternatives have Hamming distance one. Thus \(h\) defines an injective graph homomorphism from \(G\) into the \(r\)-cube graph on \(\{0,1\}^r\). The condition need not preserve nonedges: requiring the converse implication would instead demand that \(G\) be represented as an induced subgraph of the hypercube.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An adjacency-preserving code maps every adjacent pair of alternatives to binary codewords differing in exactly one coordinate.
knowledge_statements.title: Adjacency-Preserving Codes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The edge-preserving condition is precise, distinguishes edge preservation from induced-subgraph preservation, and the condition kind fits the terminal container. No graph-encoding or embedding-formulation source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Embedding Geometry Effects
children.top_down_role: Formulation behavior induced by the geometry of embedded labels.

knowledge_statements.title: Embedding Geometry Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of code-point geometry on an embedding formulation’s continuous relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_i\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty polyhedra and let distinct code points \(h^i\in\mathbb R^k\) represent disjuncts. The embedding polyhedron is \[Q_H=\operatorname{conv}\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^m P_i\times\{h^i\}\right).\] Although every valid encoding preserves the integer-level projection \(\bigcup_i P_i\), changing \(H=\{h^1,\ldots,h^m\}\) can change the faces, inequalities, and relaxation strength of \(Q_H\). Embeddings related by an invertible affine transformation of code space yield affinely equivalent polyhedra; embeddings not so related need not yield equivalent relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Code geometry can change the embedding polyhedron and relaxation strength without changing the represented disjunction; invertible affine changes of code preserve equivalence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_H\) depends geometrically on \(H\), while its code-restricted projection represents \(\bigcup_{i=1}^m P_i\).

notation.meaning: code point assigned to disjunct i
embedding polyhedron induced by code set H

review_flags: Exact embedding-formulation reference and locator are missing.
standard_field_rationale: follows directly from convex-hull embedding geometry and affine equivalence.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No inspectable citation supports the geometry claims. Distinct code points alone do not ensure that restricting the code coordinate to a code point recovers only its assigned disjunct; an additional valid-encoding condition must be defined and sourced.

children.title: Hybrid Encodings
children.top_down_role: Mixed unary, binary, and partially disaggregated representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Encodings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mixed unary and compact coding of a finite disjunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For disjuncts \(P_1,\ldots,P_m\), a hybrid encoding partitions the index set into groups \(G_1,\ldots,G_r\), assigns a compact code \(h^g\) to each group, and retains unary weights within groups. Variables \(\lambda_i\ge0\) satisfy \(\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i=1\), group weights are \(u_g=\sum_{i\in G_g}\lambda_i\), and the compact variable satisfies \(y=\sum_{g=1}^r h^g u_g\). Disaggregated variables enforce membership in the selected disjuncts. Thus the representation is unary within each group and compact across groups; singleton groups recover a compact encoding, while one group recovers a unary representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hybrid encoding uses unary selection inside groups of disjuncts and compact codes to select among those groups.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u_g=\sum_{i\in G_g}\lambda_i\) and \(y=\sum_g h^g u_g\) combine unary and compact representations.
review_flags: A source defining this precise hybrid-encoding convention is required.
standard_field_rationale: hierarchical grouping naturally combines unary and compact disjunct selection.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The precise hybrid-encoding convention and its limiting cases require a source. The assumption also contains the malformed expression \(\{1,ldots,m\}\), and the claim that singleton groups recover a compact encoding requires clarification about elimination of retained unary variables.

children.title: Formulation Composition
children.top_down_role: Combination of local formulations and the resulting interactions among strength, size, and shared geometry.

children.title: Constraintwise Composition
children.top_down_role: Independent formulation of separate constraints or local structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraintwise Composition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact formulations composed independently across constraints sharing original variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_j\subseteq X\) be the feasible set imposed by constraint block \(j\), and let \(Q_j\subseteq X\times Y_j\) be an exact extended formulation satisfying \(\operatorname{proj}_X(Q_j)=S_j\). The constraintwise composition is \[Q=\{(x,y^1,\ldots,y^p):(x,y^j)\in Q_j\text{ for every }j\}.\] Then \(\operatorname{proj}_X(Q)=\bigcap_{j=1}^p S_j\). Exactness of the represented feasible set is therefore preserved, but the continuous relaxation may be weaker than a formulation constructed jointly for the coupled intersection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersecting exact formulations of separate constraint blocks remains exact after projection, though it may lose relaxation strength relative to joint modeling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_X(Q)=\bigcap_{j=1}^p S_j\).

notation.meaning: feasible set of constraint block j

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports formulation composition.
standard_field_rationale: projection commutes with this independently lifted intersection.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The projection identity is mathematically sound for independently replicated auxiliary spaces and fits the principle container, but no inspectable source or locator is supplied for the formulation-composition claim.

children.title: Joint Composition of Coupled Structures
children.top_down_role: Combined treatment of interacting constraints to preserve shared geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Composition of Coupled Structures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A single lifted representation of interacting constraint blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_1,\ldots,S_p\subseteq X\) share decision variables and let \(S=\bigcap_{j=1}^p S_j\). A joint composition is an extended set \(Q^{\mathrm{joint}}\subseteq X\times Y\) whose auxiliary variables and disjunct selectors encode the compatible combinations of all blocks simultaneously, with \[\operatorname{proj}_X(Q^{\mathrm{joint}})=S.\] If the joint formulation is ideal, its continuous relaxation additionally satisfies \(\operatorname{proj}_X(Q^{\mathrm{joint}}_{m LP})=\operatorname{conv}(S)\). This can be strictly stronger than constraintwise composition because generally \(\operatorname{conv}(\bigcap_j S_j)\subsetneq\bigcap_j\operatorname{conv}(S_j)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint composition models compatible combinations across interacting blocks and can recover the convex hull missed by independently composed relaxations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_X(Q^{\mathrm{joint}})=S\), and ideality gives \(\operatorname{proj}_X(Q^{\mathrm{joint}}_{\rm LP})=\operatorname{conv}(S)\).

notation.meaning: continuous relaxation of the joint formulation

review_flags: No supplied source locator addresses joint disjunctive composition.
standard_field_rationale: convexification of an intersection can be stronger than intersecting separate convexifications.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation and convex-hull comparison fit the joint-composition container and are mathematically plausible, but the terminology and strength claim lack an inspectable source.

children.title: Granularity-Based Composition Regimes
children.top_down_role: Intermediate groupings balancing local strength and formulation size.

children.title: Partial Composition
children.top_down_role: Composition applied to selected portions of a larger formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial Composition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint formulation of selected blocks with remaining blocks modeled separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,p\}\) identify constraint blocks to be composed jointly. Suppose \(Q_J\) exactly formulates \(S_J= igcap_{j\in J}S_j\), while \(Q_j\) exactly formulates \(S_j\) for each \(j
otin J\). The partial composition is the intersection, over the shared variable \(x\), of \(Q_J\) and all \(Q_j\) with \(j
otin J\). Its projection is \[\operatorname{proj}_X(Q^{J})=S_J\cap igcap_{j
otin J}S_j= igcap_{j=1}^pS_j.\] It interpolates between fully constraintwise and fully joint composition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial composition jointly models a selected subset of blocks and independently models the rest while preserving the original feasible intersection.
assumptions_latex: \(Q_J\) and every \(Q_j\) used are exact for their stated sets.
All component formulations share the same original variable \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_X(Q^J)=\bigcap_{j=1}^p S_j\).

notation.meaning: intersection of blocks indexed by J

review_flags: A formulation-composition source is required for terminology.
standard_field_rationale: exactness follows from intersecting exact lifts over a shared original space.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition matches partial composition and its projection identity is sound under the stated exactness assumptions, but the terminology and formulation claim have no cited source.

children.title: Clustered Composition
children.top_down_role: Composition organized around groups of related constraints or variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Clustered Composition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint composition within clusters and independent composition between clusters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal C=\{C_1,\ldots,C_q\}\) partition the constraint-block indices \(\{1,\ldots,p\}\). For each cluster define \(S_{C_t}=\bigcap_{j\in C_t}S_j\) and choose an exact joint formulation \(Q_{C_t}\) of that set. The clustered composition is \[Q^{\mathcal C}=\{(x,y^1,\ldots,y^q):(x,y^t)\in Q_{C_t}\text{ for all }t\}.\] Its original-space projection equals \(\bigcap_{j=1}^pS_j\). Couplings are represented jointly inside each cluster but only through shared original variables across different clusters.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clustered composition jointly formulates constraints inside each partition block and intersects the resulting cluster formulations across blocks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_X(Q^{\mathcal C})=\bigcap_{j=1}^pS_j\).
review_flags: A direct source for clustered formulation composition is missing.
standard_field_rationale: clusterwise exact lifts preserve the intersection under projection.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition matches clustered composition and the projection equality follows under independent cluster lifts, but no inspectable source supports the terminology or construction.

children.title: Cluster Granularity
children.top_down_role: Structural choices governing the size and scope of composed groups.

knowledge_statements.title: Cluster Granularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relaxation ordering induced by merging or splitting formulation clusters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a partition \(\mathcal C\) of constraint indices, define the ideal clusterwise relaxation \[R(\mathcal C)=\bigcap_{C\in\mathcal C}\operatorname{conv}\left(\bigcap_{j\in C}S_j\right).\] If \(\mathcal D\) is coarser than \(\mathcal C\), so every cluster of \(\mathcal C\) lies in a cluster of \(\mathcal D\), then \(R(\mathcal D)\subseteq R(\mathcal C)\). Hence larger clusters cannot weaken this idealized original-space relaxation, while splitting clusters cannot strengthen it. Equality may hold when the additional cross-block coupling creates no new convex-hull inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Merging clusters produces an equal or stronger ideal clusterwise relaxation; splitting clusters produces an equal or weaker one.
assumptions_latex: Every cluster is represented by its exact convex hull.
\(\mathcal D\) is a coarsening of \(\mathcal C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R(\mathcal D)\subseteq R(\mathcal C)\).

notation.meaning: fine and coarse partitions of constraint indices
ideal clusterwise relaxation for partition C
feasible set of constraint block j

review_flags: No supplied locator states the cluster-refinement ordering.
standard_field_rationale: the ordering follows from convex hull of intersection versus intersection of convex hulls.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The coarsening inclusion is mathematically plausible and fits the property container, but the common ambient space for the sets \(S_j\) is not introduced and no source states the cluster-refinement ordering.

children.title: Strength–Size Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Balance between local formulation strength and total representation size.

knowledge_statements.title: Strength–Size Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formulation strength versus combinatorial and extended-space growth under clustering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In clustered disjunctive composition, merging clusters replaces separate convexifications by a convexification of their coupled intersection, so the projected relaxation can only strengthen under ideal cluster formulations. The cost is that compatible disjunct combinations may grow multiplicatively: if blocks in a cluster have \(m_j\) alternatives, direct enumeration can require up to \(\prod_j m_j\) combined alternatives, together with corresponding lifted variables or inequalities. Splitting clusters reduces this representation size but may admit points belonging to separate cluster convex hulls that are absent from the convex hull of the full intersection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Larger clusters can strengthen relaxations but may multiply the number of combined alternatives; smaller clusters reduce size while potentially weakening the relaxation.
assumptions_latex: Cluster formulations use direct compatible-combination enumeration.
Relaxation strength is compared after projection to the common original space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Coarser clustering strengthens or preserves the ideal relaxation but may increase representation size from additive to multiplicative growth.

notation.meaning: number of alternatives in block j
upper bound on enumerated joint alternatives

review_flags: A source is needed for the stated direct-enumeration size model.
standard_field_rationale: Cartesian combination counts multiply, while cluster convexification yields the stated relaxation ordering.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The qualitative strength–size tradeoff fits the principle container, but the multiplicative enumeration model and the asserted lifted-variable or inequality growth require a direct source and a more explicit formulation model.

children.title: Formulation Fidelity Criteria

children.title: Feasible-Set Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Agreement of represented feasible decisions after accounting for auxiliary variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible-Set Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality of feasible decisions under specified decoding maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let formulations \(F_1\subseteq Z_1\) and \(F_2\subseteq Z_2\) have decoding maps \(d_1:Z_1\to X\) and \(d_2:Z_2\to X\) into a common decision space. They are feasible-set equivalent relative to these maps when \[d_1(F_1)=d_2(F_2).\] Equivalently, every feasible point of either formulation decodes to a decision attainable by a feasible point of the other formulation. The definition does not require equality or a bijection between auxiliary-variable realizations; it requires equality only of represented feasible decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two formulations are feasible-set equivalent when their feasible points decode to exactly the same decisions, regardless of auxiliary-variable multiplicity.
assumptions_latex: \(d_i:Z_i\to X\) map into the same decision space.

source_refs.locator: 1.1 Classification of Nonlinear Integer Programming Formulations p. 2

children.title: Projection Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Agreement in the original decision space after eliminating auxiliary variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality after eliminating each formulation’s auxiliary coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q_1\subseteq X\times Y_1\) and \(Q_2\subseteq X\times Y_2\) be formulations sharing original-variable space \(X\). They are projection equivalent when \[\operatorname{proj}_X(Q_1)=\operatorname{proj}_X(Q_2),\] where \(\operatorname{proj}_X(Q_i)=\{x\in X:\exists y_i\in Y_i,\ (x,y_i)\in Q_i\}\). Projection equivalence permits different auxiliary dimensions, constraints, and numbers of lifts for the same \(x\); it asserts only equality of the represented set in the designated original coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two lifted formulations are projection equivalent when eliminating their auxiliary variables yields the same set of original decisions.
assumptions_latex: \(Q_i\subseteq X\times Y_i\) share the designated original space \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_X(Q_1)=\operatorname{proj}_X(Q_2)\).

notation.meaning: lifted feasible set of formulation i
coordinate projection onto original space X

children.title: Optimization-Outcome Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Agreement of optimization outcomes despite differing feasible representations.

children.title: Objective-Value Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Agreement of optimal objective values across differing representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Value Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality of extended-real optimal values for corresponding objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_i\subseteq Z_i\) be formulations with decoding maps \(d_i:Z_i\to X\), and let \(f:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be a common minimization objective. They are objective-value equivalent for \(f\) when \[\inf_{z_1\in F_1}f(d_1(z_1))=\inf_{z_2\in F_2}f(d_2(z_2)),\] with both sides interpreted in the extended real line so infeasibility and unboundedness are included. Equality for one objective does not imply feasible-set equivalence or equality of optimizer sets; equivalence for a class of objectives requires this equality for every objective in that class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two formulations are objective-value equivalent when corresponding objectives have the same extended-real optimum, even if their feasible or optimal sets differ.
assumptions_latex: Both formulations use the common objective \(f\) after decoding.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation and General Solution Procedures p. 13

children.title: Optimal-Solution Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Agreement of optimizer sets or their intended projections.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimal-Solution Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality of decoded optimizer sets for a common objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_i\subseteq Z_i\) have decoding maps \(d_i:Z_i\to X\), and suppose the common objective \(f:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) attains a finite minimum in both formulations. They are optimal-solution equivalent for \(f\) when \[d_1\!\left(\operatorname*{argmin}_{z_1\in F_1}f(d_1(z_1))\right)=d_2\!\left(\operatorname*{argmin}_{z_2\in F_2}f(d_2(z_2))\right).\] The equality concerns decoded decisions and permits different auxiliary realizations. It implies objective-value equivalence under the attainment assumption, whereas equality of objective values alone need not imply equality of decoded optimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two formulations are optimal-solution equivalent when their decoded minimizers coincide; auxiliary representations may still differ.
assumptions_latex: \(F_i\subseteq Z_i\) have decoding maps into the same space \(X\).
The common objective \(f\) attains a finite minimum in both formulations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_1(\operatorname*{argmin}_{F_1} f\circ d_1)=d_2(\operatorname*{argmin}_{F_2} f\circ d_2)\).

children.top_down_role: Correspondence between optimal solutions in original and reformulated spaces.

notation.meaning: Target feasible set in original variables
Projection map restricted to the formulation optimizer set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimizer correspondence induced by projection from an extended formulation.

source_refs.locator: 1.5 Mixed Integer Formulations p. 9

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+p}\), let \(\pi_x(x,y)=x\), and let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\). Define the optimizer mapping of the formulation by \[\mathcal{M}_f^{Q\to S}:\operatorname*{argmin}_{(x,y)\in Q}f(x)\to\mathbb{R}^n,\qquad \mathcal{M}_f^{Q\to S}(x,y)=\pi_x(x,y)=x.\] It is optimizer-preserving when its image is exactly the target optimizer set, that is, when \[\mathcal{M}_f^{Q\to S}\!\left(\operatorname*{argmin}_{(x,y)\in Q}f(x)\right)=\pi_x\!\left(\operatorname*{argmin}_{(x,y)\in Q}f(x)\right)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in S}f(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The optimizer mapping sends each optimal extended-formulation solution to its original-variable projection; it preserves optimizers exactly when its image equals the target optimizer set.

children.title: Outcome Mismatch Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where value agreement does not ensure agreement of optimal solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Outcome Mismatch Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-value agreement does not by itself imply optimizer agreement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=\{0,1\}\), let its relaxation be \(R=[0,1]\), and minimize the constant objective \(f(x)=0\). Then \[\min_{x\in S}f(x)=0=\min_{x\in R}f(x),\] but \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in S}f(x)=\{0,1\}\neq[0,1]=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in R}f(x).\] Thus equality of optimal objective values is insufficient for optimal-solution equivalence; fractional relaxation optimizers may remain even when the optimal values coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant objective gives equal optimal values on a binary set and its interval relaxation, while every fractional point becomes an additional relaxation optimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Equality of optimal values does not imply equality of optimizer sets.

children.title: Relaxation-Only Representations
children.top_down_role: Models intended to provide bounds or approximations rather than exact equivalence.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Only Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer representations used for valid bounds without exact feasible-set equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem with feasible set \(S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), an extended set \(R\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+p}\) is a relaxation-only representation when \[S\subseteq\pi_x(R)\] and equality is not required. For every objective \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) for which both infima are defined, \[\inf_{(x,y)\in R}f(x)\leq\inf_{x\in S}f(x).\] Hence the representation supplies a valid lower bound, but its feasible points, optimizers, and optimal value need not reproduce those of the original model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxation-only representation contains the target feasible set after projection and therefore gives a minimization lower bound, without claiming exact feasible points or optimizers.
assumptions_latex: The objective depends only on the original variable \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\subseteq\pi_x(R)\) implies \(\inf_R f\leq\inf_S f\).

children.title: Strength Hierarchy of Formulations
children.top_down_role: Geometric quality classes based on continuous relaxations and integral structure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Relaxation-Inclusion Ordering of Equivalent Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies two representations of the same mixed-integer set by inclusion of their linear relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\{(x,y):A_1x+G_1y\le b_1,\ x\text{ integral}\}\) and \(\{(x,y):A_2x+G_2y\le b_2,\ x\text{ integral}\}\) represent the same mixed-integer set \(S\), and let \(P_i:=\{(x,y):A_ix+G_iy\le b_i\}\) for \(i=1,2\). The first representation is better if \(P_1\subsetneq P_2\); the representations are equivalent if \(P_1=P_2\); and they are incomparable if both \(P_1\setminus P_2\) and \(P_2\setminus P_1\) are nonempty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For two representations of the same mixed-integer set, the first is better when its linear relaxation is properly contained in the second, equivalent when the relaxations coincide, and incomparable when each relaxation contains points excluded by the other.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_1\subsetneq P_2\Rightarrow \text{the first representation is better};\quad P_1=P_2\Rightarrow \text{the representations are equivalent};\quad P_1\setminus P_2\ne\varnothing\ \land\ P_2\setminus P_1\ne\varnothing\Rightarrow \text{the representations are incomparable}

children.title: Relaxation Dominance
children.top_down_role: Comparison by containment and bound quality of continuous relaxations.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Dominance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strength comparison for minimization formulations after projection into common original variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_1\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+p_1}\) and \(R_2\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+p_2}\) be relaxations of the same feasible set \(S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\). Formulation \(R_1\) dominates \(R_2\) when \[\pi_x(R_1)\subseteq\pi_x(R_2).\] Consequently, for every objective \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) whose infima exist, \[\inf_{(x,y_1)\in R_1}f(x)\geq\inf_{(x,y_2)\in R_2}f(x).\] Thus the dominating relaxation yields a lower bound at least as strong for minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One relaxation dominates another when its projection is contained in the other’s; its minimization lower bound is then never weaker.
assumptions_latex: Both formulations use the same original-space objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{R_1}f\geq\inf_{R_2}f\) for every admissible minimization objective \(f\).

notation.meaning: Projection into the common original-variable space

children.title: Sharp Formulations
children.top_down_role: Formulations whose projected relaxation reaches the target convex hull.

knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected-relaxation definition of sharpness for an extended mixed-integer formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be the target integer-feasible set and let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+p}\) be the continuous relaxation of an extended formulation. The formulation is sharp when \[\pi_x(Q)=\operatorname{conv}(S).\] Equivalently, optimizing any linear objective \(c^\top x\) over \(Q\) gives the same optimal value as optimizing it over \(S\), provided the relevant optima exist. Sharpness concerns the projection and does not require every extreme point of \(Q\) itself to satisfy the formulation’s integrality restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A formulation is sharp when projecting its continuous relaxation yields exactly the convex hull of target integer-feasible points.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is the continuous relaxation of a valid extended formulation of \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The formulation is sharp exactly when \(\pi_x(Q)=\operatorname{conv}(S)\).

children.title: Formulation Ideality Regimes

children.title: Ideal Formulations
children.top_down_role: Global relaxation structure associated with intended discrete vertices.

knowledge_statements.title: Ideal Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vertex-integrality definition for a polyhedral mixed-integer formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q=\{z\in\mathbb{R}^d:Az\leq b\}\) be the continuous relaxation of a formulation, and let \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\) index variables required to be integral. The formulation is ideal when every extreme point \(z\) of \(Q\) satisfies \[z_i\in\mathbb{Z}\qquad\text{for every }i\in I.\] If a finite linear optimum over \(Q\) is attained at an extreme point, then an optimal solution exists that satisfies all declared integrality restrictions, so solving the linear relaxation suffices to obtain an integer-feasible optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ideal formulation has no fractional extreme point in its integer-designated coordinates, so an attained vertex optimum can be chosen integer-feasible.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is the fixed index set of integer-designated variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every \(z\in\operatorname{ext}(Q)\) satisfies \(z_I\in\mathbb{Z}^{|I|}\).

notation.meaning: Set of extreme points of Q

children.title: Locally Ideal Formulations
children.top_down_role: Ideality restricted to designated components or local structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Locally Ideal Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Blockwise ideality relative to a specified decomposition of a formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a formulation has continuous relaxation \[Q=\bigcap_{k=1}^m Q_k,\qquad Q_k\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d,\] and integer-designated coordinate set \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\). Relative to this decomposition, the formulation is locally ideal when every block relaxation is ideal: \[z_I\in\mathbb{Z}^{|I|}\qquad\text{for every }k\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\text{ and every }z\in\operatorname{ext}(Q_k).\] This property is decomposition-dependent and does not assert that every extreme point of the intersection \(Q\) is integral.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A formulation is locally ideal relative to a decomposition when every block relaxation has integral extreme points in the designated coordinates; their intersection need not be ideal.
assumptions_latex: All blocks use the same integer-designated coordinate set \(I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each block \(Q_k\) is ideal, without necessarily implying that \(Q\) is ideal.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed blockwise definition is internally coherent, but 'locally ideal formulation' is convention-dependent and the candidate supplies no source establishing that this exact intersection-of-ideal-blocks meaning is intended. Source uncertainty therefore affects the mathematical scope of the definition.

children.title: Local-to-Global Gaps
children.top_down_role: Limits of inferring global ideality from locally ideal components.

knowledge_statements.title: Local-to-Global Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intersection can destroy integrality even when every constituent polyhedron is integral.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[Q_1=\{x\in[0,1]^2:x_1+x_2\leq1\},\qquad Q_2=\{x\in[0,1]^2:x_1=x_2\}.\] Both \(Q_1\) and \(Q_2\) are integral polyhedra: their extreme points are respectively \(\{(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)\}\) and \(\{(0,0),(1,1)\}\). However, \[Q_1\cap Q_2=\{(t,t):0\leq t\leq\tfrac12\}\] has the fractional extreme point \((\tfrac12,\tfrac12)\). Therefore blockwise or local ideality does not imply ideality of the combined formulation without additional compatibility conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two integral polyhedra can have a nonintegral intersection; thus locally ideal blocks need not produce a globally ideal formulation.
assumptions_latex: Both coordinates are designated integer variables.
Global composition is intersection of the two block relaxations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_1\) and \(Q_2\) are integral, but \(Q_1\cap Q_2\) is not integral.

notation.meaning: Scalar parameter on the intersection segment

children.title: Perfect Formulations
children.top_down_role: Descriptions aligned with integral polyhedral representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Perfect Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Original-space inequality description equal to the integer hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^n\) be the feasible set of an integer program. A linear formulation \[P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\leq b\}\] in the original variables is perfect when \[P=\operatorname{conv}(S).\] Consequently, every linear objective has the same infimum over \(P\) and \(S\), whenever these infima are well defined; if a finite optimum is attained at an extreme point of \(P\), that point belongs to \(S\). Unlike a general sharp extended formulation, this definition introduces no auxiliary variables or projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A perfect formulation describes the integer hull directly in the original variables, so its linear relaxation exactly captures all linear-objective values.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a polyhedron expressed only in the original variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The formulation is perfect exactly when \(P=\operatorname{conv}(S)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent Characterizations of Mixed-Integer-Integral Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes equality with the convex hull of points having integral designated coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^p\) be a rational polyhedron and let \(S:=P\cap(\mathbb{Z}^n\times\mathbb{R}^p)\). The following are equivalent: (i) \(P=\operatorname{conv}(S)\); (ii) every minimal face of \(P\) contains a point in \(\mathbb{Z}^n\times\mathbb{R}^p\); (iii) for every \((c,h)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^p\) for which \(\max\{c^\top x+h^\top y:(x,y)\in P\}\) is finite, the maximum is attained at a point in \(P\cap(\mathbb{Z}^n\times\mathbb{R}^p)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rational polyhedron equals the convex hull of its points with integral designated coordinates exactly when every minimal face contains such a point, equivalently when every finite linear maximum has an optimizer with those coordinates integral.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P=\operatorname{conv}(S)\iff\text{every minimal face of }P\text{ meets }\mathbb{Z}^n\times\mathbb{R}^p\iff\text{condition (iii)}

children.title: Row Count

knowledge_statements.title: Row Count
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-count component of a linear or mixed-integer formulation’s description size.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a formulation written as \[Ax\leq b,\qquad Cx=d,\] with \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m_\leq\times n}\) and \(C\in\mathbb{R}^{m_=\times n}\), its row count is \[m:=m_\leq+m_=,\] after applying the stated convention for whether variable bounds and redundant rows are included. If every equality is converted into two inequalities, the corresponding inequality-only row count is \(m_\leq+2m_=\). Row count measures the number of scalar constraint rows, not their encoding length or sparsity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Row count is the number of scalar constraint rows under a declared convention; equality conversion, bounds, and redundant constraints can change the reported count.
assumptions_latex: The formulation is finite-dimensional and explicitly represented.
The counting convention for bounds and equalities is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m=m_\leq+m_=\) in the mixed inequality-equality convention.

children.title: Column Count
children.top_down_role: Explicit-variable dimension used in formulation-size comparisons.

knowledge_statements.title: Column Count
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variable-count component of a formulation’s dimension and description size.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite-dimensional formulation with decision vector \(z=(z_1,\ldots,z_d)\in\mathbb{R}^d\), its column count is \[d=|\{z_1,\ldots,z_d\}|,\] namely the number of scalar decision-variable columns in its constraint matrix. Original, auxiliary, continuous, and integer-designated variables are all counted unless a narrower convention is explicitly declared. Fixed quantities that have been eliminated are not columns; retained fixed variables are columns. Column count alone does not measure coefficient encoding length, sparsity, or the number of feasible degrees of freedom.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Column count is the number of retained scalar decision variables, including original and auxiliary variables unless the counting convention says otherwise.
assumptions_latex: Variables are represented as finitely many scalar columns.
The convention for retained fixed variables is specified.

children.title: Auxiliary Dimension

knowledge_statements.title: Auxiliary Dimension
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Number of added coordinates in an extended formulation relative to its target space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the target variables be \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and let an extended formulation use \((x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^{n+p}\), where \(y\in\mathbb{R}^p\) consists of variables absent from the target model. The auxiliary dimension of this representation is \[p=(n+p)-n.\] It counts scalar added coordinates, irrespective of whether they are continuous or integer-designated. The quantity is representation-dependent: eliminating auxiliary variables can reduce \(p\) while increasing row count or coefficient complexity, and introducing redundant auxiliaries can increase it without changing the projected feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Auxiliary dimension is the number of scalar variables added beyond the target variables; it depends on the chosen extended representation.
assumptions_latex: The extended vector is partitioned explicitly as \((x,y)\).

children.title: Numerical Encoding Complexity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polynomial Time Is Measured in Encoded Input Length
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case complexity for combinatorial inputs containing integer capacities, costs, or related numerical data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The worst-case complexity of an algorithm is measured as a function of the encoded size of the entire instance. An integer \(K\) has encoding length \(\Theta(\log K)\) under positional encoding, so a running time proportional to \(K\) can be exponential in the length of the numerical input and is therefore not polynomial-time in general. Consequently, polynomial solvability of an uncapacitated problem does not by itself imply a polynomial algorithm for its capacitated extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complexity is measured against the full encoded input length. Because writing an integer K takes on the order of log K digits, a runtime proportional to K may be exponential in the input length. Thus an algorithm polynomial for an uncapacitated problem need not remain polynomial for its capacitated version.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T(K)=\Theta(K)\ \text{may equal}\ 2^{\Theta(\operatorname{len}(K))}\ \text{and hence need not be polynomial in input length}

knowledge_statements.title: Encoding Length
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary description length for rational mixed-integer formulation data.

A sparse or dense storage convention is fixed.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Binary encoding size of integer and rational input data
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard representation-dependent bit-length conventions for rational optimization data.

children.title: Dimension–Bitlength Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Interactions between formulation dimensions and numerical description size.

knowledge_statements.title: Dimension–Bitlength Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact unary and binary encodings expose a basic variable-count versus coefficient-size tradeoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z\in\mathbb{Z}\) satisfy \(0\le z\le U\), where \(U\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}\). An exact unary encoding uses \(U\) binary variables and unit coefficients: \(z=\sum_{i=1}^{U}u_i\), with \(u_i\in\{0,1\}\). An exact binary encoding uses \(t=\lceil\log_2(U+1)\rceil\) binary variables: \(z=\sum_{i=0}^{t-1}2^i b_i\), with \(b_i\in\{0,1\}\), together with \(z\le U\). Thus logarithmic auxiliary dimension is obtained at the cost of coefficients as large as \(2^{t-1}\), whereas unary encoding has linear dimension and unit coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded integer can be encoded with many binary variables and unit coefficients, or logarithmically many variables and coefficients of order its upper bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Unary encoding uses \(U\) binaries with unit weights, while binary encoding uses \(\lceil\log_2(U+1)\rceil\) binaries with exponentially increasing weights.

knowledge_statements.title: Extension Size Measures

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fooling-set certificates for exact linear extension-complexity lower bounds.

source_refs.locator: 6.6 The Complexity of Extended Formulations p. 105

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty polytope with complete facet description \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\text{ for all }i\in I\}\) and vertex set \(\{v_j:j\in J\}\). Its facet-vertex slack matrix is \(S\in\mathbb{R}_+^{I\times J}\), with \(S_{ij}=b_i-a_i^{\mathsf T}v_j\). A fooling set of size \(t\) is a collection \(F=\{(i_s,j_s):1\le s\le t\}\) such that \(S_{i_sj_s}>0\) and, for every distinct \(s,r\), at least one of \(S_{i_sj_r}\) and \(S_{i_rj_s}\) is zero. This checkable pattern certifies \(\operatorname{rank}_+(S)\ge t\) and hence, by the exact slack-matrix characterization, \(\operatorname{xc}(P)\ge t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A size-t fooling set in the complete facet-vertex slack matrix is a checkable zero-pattern certificate that every exact linear extension of the polytope needs at least t inequalities.

children.title: Approximate Extended Formulations

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Extended Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hausdorff-additive approximation convention for lifted linear descriptions of compact convex sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a norm \(\|\cdot\|\) on \(\mathbb{R}^n\) with closed unit ball \(B\), and let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, compact, and convex. A polyhedron \(Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+r}\) is an additive \(\varepsilon\)-approximate extended formulation of \(P\) if its projection \(K=\pi_x(Q)\) satisfies \(P\subseteq K\subseteq P+\varepsilon B\). Its approximate extension size is the number of inequalities defining \(Q\); the minimum such number is denoted \(\operatorname{xc}_{\varepsilon}(P;\|\cdot\|)\). The definition is norm- and scaling-dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An additive approximate extension projects to a convex relaxation lying between the target set and its epsilon-neighborhood; its size counts defining inequalities.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a nonempty compact convex subset of \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
A norm and an additive tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Approximation requires \(P\subseteq\pi_x(Q)\subseteq P+\varepsilon B\).

notation.meaning: closed unit ball of the fixed norm

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive Hausdorff-style convention is coherent and fits the topic, but no citation is supplied. Because several inequivalent notions of approximate extension complexity exist, a dedicated source and locator are required before selecting this convention.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Integer Description Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint resource profile for inequalities, integer coordinates, auxiliary dimension, and encoded data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\). A rational mixed-integer linear description of \(S\) is a system \(Ax+By+Cz\le d\), with \(y\in\mathbb{R}^r\) and \(z\in\mathbb{Z}^k\), whose projection onto \(x\) equals \(S\). Its description profile is \((m,k,r,L)\), where \(m\) is the number of inequalities, \(k\) the integer dimension, \(r\) the continuous auxiliary dimension, and \(L\) the binary encoding length. Mixed-integer description complexity is the set of Pareto-minimal attainable profiles under componentwise order, unless a specified scalar cost combines these resources.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixed-integer description complexity records Pareto-minimal combinations of inequality count, integer dimension, continuous auxiliary dimension, and encoding length for exact projected descriptions.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) admits at least one finite rational mixed-integer linear description.
A binary encoding convention is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The complexity profile comprises the Pareto-minimal attainable tuples \((m,k,r,L)\).

children.title: Strength–Size Tradeoffs

knowledge_statements.title: Strength–Size Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partial-order comparison of formulation relaxation strength and description resources.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let two formulations for the same minimization problem have projected continuous relaxations \(R_1,R_2\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), both containing the integer-feasible set \(S\). If \(R_1\subseteq R_2\), then for every objective vector \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(\inf_{x\in R_1}c^{\mathsf T}x\ge\inf_{x\in R_2}c^{\mathsf T}x\); thus formulation \(1\) is at least as strong. Given a size measure \(s\), formulation \(1\) dominates formulation \(2\) when additionally \(s_1\le s_2\), with at least one strict relation. Nondominated formulations form the strength–size frontier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smaller relaxation gives at least as strong every minimization bound; adding description size yields a Pareto frontier of nondominated formulations.
assumptions_latex: Both projected relaxations contain the same integer-feasible set.
The same linear minimization objective is evaluated on both relaxations.
A common size convention is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inclusion \(R_1\subseteq R_2\) implies uniformly stronger minimization bounds for \(R_1\).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Bounded representability requires finite componentwise bounds \(\underline z\le z\le\overline z\) on every integer auxiliary coordinate.

notation.meaning: represented set in the original space
finite integral lower and upper bound vectors for the integer auxiliaries

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact projected representation with finitely bounded integer auxiliary coordinates.

source_refs.locator: 1.5 Mixed Integer Formulations p. 9

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A set \(S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is bounded mixed-integer linear representable if there exist integers \(r,k\ge0\), rational matrices and vectors defining a polyhedron \(Q=\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^r\times\mathbb{R}^k:Ax+By+Cz\le d\}\), and vectors \(\underline z,\overline z\in\mathbb{Z}^k\) such that \(S=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\exists y\in\mathbb{R}^r,\exists z\in\mathbb{Z}^k,\ (x,y,z)\in Q,\ \underline z\le z\le\overline z\}\). The bounds make the admissible integer set finite, although \(S\), the continuous variables, and \(Q\) need not be bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set is bounded mixed-integer representable when it is the projection of a finite rational linear system whose integer auxiliary variables range over a finite box; the represented set and continuous auxiliaries need not be bounded.
knowledge_statements.title: Bounded Mixed-Integer Representability

source_witnesses.locator: 1.5 Mixed Integer Formulations p. 9

children.title: Projected Mixed-Integer Representability
children.top_down_role: Representability after eliminating auxiliary discrete and continuous variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Projected Mixed-Integer Representability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact representation obtained by existentially eliminating continuous and integer auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A set \(S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) has a rational projected mixed-integer linear representation if there exist integers \(r,k\ge0\) and rational data \(A,B,C,d\) such that \[S=\operatorname{proj}_x\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^r\times\mathbb{Z}^k:Ax+By+Cz\le d\}=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\exists y\in\mathbb{R}^r,\exists z\in\mathbb{Z}^k,\ Ax+By+Cz\le d\}.\] No boundedness of the auxiliary variables is imposed unless stated separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set is projected mixed-integer representable when it consists exactly of original-variable points admitting continuous and integer auxiliaries satisfying a finite rational linear system.
assumptions_latex: The representation uses finitely many rational linear inequalities.
Projection retains precisely the original coordinates \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The represented set equals the existential projection of the mixed-integer linear feasible region.

source_refs.locator: 1.5 Mixed Integer Formulations p. 9

children.title: General Unbounded Mixed-Integer Representability
children.top_down_role: Representability permitting unbounded integer auxiliary variables and monoidal structure.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The set \(S\) is representable using unrestricted integer auxiliaries, and every element of \(M\) preserves feasibility by integer translation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rational mixed-integer linear representability without finite bounds on auxiliary integer variables.

source_refs.locator: 1.5 Mixed Integer Formulations p. 9
1.4.1 Example: A Two-Dimensional Mixed Integer Set p. 22

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A set \(S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is generally mixed-integer linear representable if there exist nonnegative integers \(p,q\) and rational matrices and vectors \(A,B,C,d\) such that \[S=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\exists u\in\mathbb{R}^p,\ \exists z\in\mathbb{Z}^q,\ Ax+Bu+Cz\le d\}.\] No finite bounds on \(z\) are required. The integer recession set \[M=\{r\in\mathbb{Z}^q:Cr\le0\}\] is an additive monoid; whenever \((x,u,z)\) satisfies the formulation and \(r\in M\), the tuple \((x,u,z+r)\) also satisfies it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set is generally mixed-integer representable when it is the projection of a rational linear system with unrestricted integer auxiliaries; feasible integer recession directions form an additive monoid.
knowledge_statements.title: General Unbounded Mixed-Integer Representability

source_witnesses.locator: 1.5 Mixed Integer Formulations p. 9

children.title: Functional-Set Representability Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Representability of functions through graphs, epigraphs, and level-set structures.

children.title: Function Graph Representability
children.top_down_role: Mixed-integer representation of input-output graph structure.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Function graph representability is precisely mixed-integer linear representability of \(\operatorname{gph}f\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+1}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact graph representation, not merely representation of an epigraph or sampled values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The graph of \(f\) is \[\operatorname{gph}f=\{(x,t)\in D\times\mathbb{R}:t=f(x)\}.\] The function \(f\) is graph-representable by a mixed-integer linear formulation if there exist nonnegative integers \(p,q\) and rational data \(A,B,C,d\) such that \[\operatorname{gph}f=\{(x,t):\exists u\in\mathbb{R}^p,\ \exists z\in\mathbb{Z}^q,\ A(x,t)+Bu+Cz\le d\}.\] Equality is required after projection: the formulation may contain neither points above nor points below the value \(f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A function is graph-representable when its exact graph is the projection of a rational mixed-integer linear feasible set.
knowledge_statements.title: Function Graph Representability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact-graph definition is mathematically precise and fits the leaf, but no source or inspectable locator supports this representation terminology.

children.title: Epigraph Representability
children.top_down_role: Mixed-integer representation of upper-level function geometry.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Epigraph representability is mixed-integer linear representability of every pair \((x,t)\) satisfying \(x\in D\) and \(t\ge f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation of the closed upward value relation, without asserting exact graph representability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The epigraph of \(f\) is \[\operatorname{epi}f=\{(x,t)\in D\times\mathbb{R}:t\ge f(x)\}.\] The function \(f\) is epigraph-representable by a mixed-integer linear formulation if there exist nonnegative integers \(p,q\) and rational data \(A,B,C,d\) such that \[\operatorname{epi}f=\{(x,t):\exists u\in\mathbb{R}^p,\ \exists z\in\mathbb{Z}^q,\ A(x,t)+Bu+Cz\le d\}.\] Thus the projection must contain exactly the points lying on or above the function over \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A function is epigraph-representable when the set of domain-value pairs lying on or above it is a rational mixed-integer linear projection.
knowledge_statements.title: Epigraph Representability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed epigraph definition is precise, but no supporting citation is supplied. The scope note also calls the epigraph closed without assumptions ensuring that property.

children.title: Level-Set Representability
children.top_down_role: Mixed-integer representation of parameterized function level sets.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sublevel set \(L_\alpha(f)\) is representable exactly when it equals the displayed mixed-integer linear projection.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-threshold sublevel-set representability; uniform formulations over varying thresholds are not asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed threshold \(\alpha\), the sublevel set of \(f\) is \[L_\alpha(f)=\{x\in D:f(x)\le\alpha\}.\] It is mixed-integer linear representable if there exist nonnegative integers \(p,q\) and rational data \(A,B,C,d\), which may depend on \(\alpha\), such that \[L_\alpha(f)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\exists u\in\mathbb{R}^p,\ \exists z\in\mathbb{Z}^q,\ Ax+Bu+Cz\le d\}.\] This definition concerns one fixed level and does not require a single formulation valid simultaneously for every \(\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed sublevel set is representable when it is exactly the projection of a rational mixed-integer linear system; the formulation may depend on the threshold.
knowledge_statements.title: Level-Set Representability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-threshold sublevel-set definition is internally consistent and correctly allows threshold-dependent formulations, but it has no cited source or locator.

children.title: Graph–Epigraph Separation
children.top_down_role: Regimes where representability of one function-associated set does not transfer to another.

assumptions_latex: The representation class is closed under auxiliary variables, linear equations, and intersection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Graph representability yields epigraph representability, while recovering the graph from an epigraph certificate additionally requires a hypograph certificate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical separation between exact-value and upper-value formulations in mixed-integer linear representation classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(f:D\to\mathbb{R}\), \[\operatorname{epi}f=\operatorname{gph}f+(\{0\}\times\mathbb{R}_+)\quad\text{and}\quad \operatorname{gph}f=\operatorname{epi}f\cap\operatorname{hypo}f,\] where \(\operatorname{hypo}f=\{(x,t)\in D\times\mathbb{R}:t\le f(x)\}\). Consequently, a mixed-integer linear representation of \(\operatorname{gph}f\) produces one for \(\operatorname{epi}f\) by introducing \(s\ge0\) and imposing \(t=f(x)+s\) through the represented graph. Conversely, an epigraph representation alone does not supply the reverse inequality; a representable hypograph suffices to recover the graph by intersection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact graph formulation generates an epigraph by adding nonnegative vertical slack. An epigraph alone lacks the reverse inequality; combining representable epi- and hypographs recovers the graph.
knowledge_statements.title: Graph–Epigraph Separation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The graph–epigraph and graph–hypograph relations are correctly stated and the property kind fits the leaf, but no citation supports the claimed representability implications.

children.title: Nonrepresentability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Rationality, closedness, convex-hull, recession, and discontinuity obstructions.

assumptions_latex: Mixed-integer linear representations use finitely many rational inequalities and finitely many continuous and integer auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The bounded set \(S=\{0\}\cup\{1/k:k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}\}\) is not rational mixed-integer linear representable.

notation.meaning: a bounded set with an accumulation point and infinitely many isolated points

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A concrete closed bounded obstruction derived from the rational MILP structure theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A bounded rational mixed-integer linear representable set is a finite union of rational polytopes, because every nonzero integer-monoid recession direction in its structural representation would make the set unbounded. Consider \[S=\{0\}\cup\{1/k:k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}\}\subseteq\mathbb{R}.\] The set \(S\) is closed and bounded, but it is not a finite union of polytopes in \(\mathbb{R}\): such a union is a finite union of closed intervals and points, whereas \(S\) has infinitely many isolated points. Hence \(S\) is not rational mixed-integer linear representable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded rational MILP-representable sets are finite unions of rational polytopes. The closed set consisting of zero and all reciprocals of positive integers violates this structure.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonrepresentability Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample depends on the nontrivial structural theorem that every bounded rational MILP-representable set is a finite union of rational polytopes. No source or theorem locator is supplied for that essential premise.

children.top_down_role: Structural mechanisms certifying that a linear formulation already captures integral solutions.
