children.title: Total Unimodularity Certificates
children.top_down_role: Matrix-structural certification routes for integral polyhedra.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The polyhedron \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\le b,\ x\ge0\}\) is integral.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard total-unimodularity certificate with integral right-hand side and nonnegative variables.

source_refs.locator: 4.2 Total Unimodularity p. 131

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matrix \(A\) is totally unimodular when every square submatrix has determinant in \(\{-1,0,1\}\). If \(A\in\mathbb{Z}^{m\times n}\) is totally unimodular and \(b\in\mathbb{Z}^m\), then \[P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\le b,\ x\ge0\}\] is an integral polyhedron. Equivalently, \[P=\operatorname{conv}(P\cap\mathbb{Z}^n)+\operatorname{rec}(P),\] and every vertex of \(P\), when vertices exist, belongs to \(\mathbb{Z}^n\). Thus total unimodularity of \(A\), together with integrality of \(b\), is a directly checkable structural certificate for integrality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the constraint matrix is totally unimodular and the right-hand side is integral, the associated nonnegative polyhedron is integral and all its vertices are integer.
knowledge_statements.title: Total Unimodularity Certificates

source_witnesses.locator: 4.2 Total Unimodularity p. 131

children.title: Total Dual Integrality Certificates
children.top_down_role: Dual-system certification routes for integrality.

assumptions_latex: The system \(Ax\le b\) is totally dual integral.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The polyhedron \(P\) is integral.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximization-form TDI convention with nonnegative multipliers for inequalities \(Ax\le b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The rational system \(Ax\le b\) is totally dual integral if, for every \(c\in\mathbb{Z}^n\) for which \(\max\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\le b\}\) is finite, the dual program \[\min\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y=c,\ y\ge0\}\] has an optimal solution \(y\in\mathbb{Z}^m\). If \(Ax\le b\) is totally dual integral, \(b\in\mathbb{Z}^m\), and \(P=\{x:Ax\le b\}\) is nonempty, then \(P\) is integral. Thus integral optimal dual multipliers for every integral objective certify primal polyhedral integrality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A TDI system has an integral optimal dual multiplier for every bounded integral objective. With an integral right-hand side, this certifies that the primal polyhedron is integral.
knowledge_statements.title: Total Dual Integrality Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The maximization-form TDI convention and resulting integrality certificate are correctly formulated, but this nontrivial theorem has no citation or locator.

children.title: Network-Incidence Integrality Certificates
children.top_down_role: Graph and network structures yielding integral formulations.

children.title: Network-Matrix Certificates
children.top_down_role: Integrality certificates arising from directed network matrix structure.

assumptions_latex: A directed graph has a spanning tree \(T\).
One row is deleted from its node-arc incidence matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The matrix \(D_T^{-1}D_N\) is totally unimodular and therefore supplies a total-unimodularity certificate.

notation.meaning: reduced incidence columns for tree arcs
reduced incidence columns for non-tree arcs

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical directed network matrices obtained from a spanning-tree basis of reduced incidence.

source_refs.locator: 4.2 Total Unimodularity p. 131

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be the node-arc incidence matrix of a directed graph, delete one row in each connected component, and partition the resulting matrix as \(D=[D_T\ D_N]\), where \(T\) is a spanning forest and \(D_T\) is square and nonsingular. The matrix \[N=D_T^{-1}D_N\] is a network matrix. Every square subdeterminant of \(N\) belongs to \(\{-1,0,1\}\), so \(N\) is totally unimodular. Consequently, any polyhedron described using \(N\), integral right-hand sides, and compatible sign or bound rows inherits the standard total-unimodularity integrality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Selecting spanning-tree columns from a reduced directed incidence matrix produces a network matrix. Such matrices are totally unimodular and certify integrality with integral data.
knowledge_statements.title: Network-Matrix Certificates

source_witnesses.locator: 4.2 Total Unimodularity p. 131

children.title: Incidence-Matrix Certificates
children.top_down_role: Integrality certificates arising from graph incidence structure.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The node-arc incidence matrix \(B\) is totally unimodular.

notation.meaning: tail and head of an arc

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directed node-arc incidence matrices; deleting redundant node rows preserves the certificate.

source_refs.locator: 4.2 Total Unimodularity p. 131

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a directed graph \(G=(V,E)\), define its node-arc incidence matrix \(B\in\{-1,0,1\}^{V\times E}\) by \[B_{ve}=\begin{cases}-1,&v=\operatorname{tail}(e),\\1,&v=\operatorname{head}(e),\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\] Every square submatrix of \(B\) has determinant in \(\{-1,0,1\}\); hence \(B\) is totally unimodular. Row deletion, column sign reversal, and adjoining unit rows preserve total unimodularity, so reduced incidence matrices and incidence systems augmented with ordinary variable bounds retain the certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A directed node-arc incidence matrix is totally unimodular. Removing redundant rows, reversing arc orientations, or adjoining variable-bound rows preserves this certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Incidence-Matrix Certificates

source_witnesses.locator: 4.2 Total Unimodularity p. 131

children.title: Flow-Polytope Integrality
children.top_down_role: Integral polyhedral behavior associated with network-flow representations.

assumptions_latex: \(B\) is the node-arc incidence matrix of a directed graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The flow polyhedron \(F=\{x:Bx=b,\ l\le x\le u\}\) is integral.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-commodity directed flows with integral balances and integral lower and upper capacities.

source_refs.locator: 4.2 Total Unimodularity p. 131
3.7 Two Harder Network Flow Problems* p. 57

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\) be the node-arc incidence matrix of a directed graph, let \(b\in\mathbb{Z}^{V}\), and let the finite components of \(l,u\) be integral with \(l\le u\). Then the feasible flow polyhedron \[F=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^{E}:Bx=b,\ l\le x\le u\}\] is integral. In particular, every vertex of \(F\) is an integral flow. This follows as an integrality certificate from total unimodularity of the incidence matrix together with preservation of total unimodularity under row negation and adjoining the unit rows encoding the capacity bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single-commodity flow polyhedron with integral node balances and integral capacities is integral; every vertex is an integer flow.
knowledge_statements.title: Flow-Polytope Integrality

source_witnesses.locator: 4.2 Total Unimodularity p. 131
3.7 Two Harder Network Flow Problems* p. 57

children.title: Network-Structure Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural modifications that prevent direct network-based certification.

assumptions_latex: The base network has two parallel arcs from \(s\) to \(t\), each with bounds \(0\le x_i\le1\).
One unit of flow must be sent from \(s\) to \(t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Adding the side constraint \(x_1-x_2=0\) destroys integrality and leaves the fractional point \((1/2,1/2)\).

notation.meaning: flows on the two parallel arcs

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A side constraint can destroy the network certificate even when all data remain integral.

source_refs.locator: 3.7 Two Harder Network Flow Problems* p. 57
4.2 Total Unimodularity p. 131

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider two parallel arcs from \(s\) to \(t\), with one unit of required flow and capacities \(0\le x_1,x_2\le1\). The network flow equation \(x_1+x_2=1\) has the integral vertices \((1,0)\) and \((0,1)\). Add the integral side constraint \(x_1-x_2=0\). The resulting feasible set is the singleton \[\{(x_1,x_2)\} = \{(1/2,1/2)\}.\] Indeed, the augmented equality matrix \[A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}\] has determinant \(-2\), so it is not totally unimodular. Thus an arbitrary side row can destroy both the network-matrix certificate and flow-polytope integrality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-parallel-arc integral flow model becomes fractional after imposing equal arc flows: its sole feasible point is one-half on each arc, and total unimodularity fails.
knowledge_statements.title: Network-Structure Failure Boundaries

source_witnesses.locator: 3.7 Two Harder Network Flow Problems* p. 57
4.2 Total Unimodularity p. 131

children.title: Balanced-Matrix Certificates
children.top_down_role: Balanced and totally balanced matrix structures supporting integrality.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The polyhedron \(P(A)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}_{+}^{n}:Ax\leq\mathbf{1}\}\) is integral.

notation.meaning: The set-packing polyhedron associated with A.
The all-ones vector of the required dimension.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite binary matrices and their set-packing polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A binary matrix \(A\) is balanced if it has no square submatrix of odd order in which every row and every column contains exactly two ones. It is totally balanced if it has no square submatrix of any order with that property. If \(A\) is balanced, then every extreme point of \[P(A)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}_{+}^{n}:Ax\leq\mathbf{1}\}\] is integral. Thus the forbidden-submatrix test is an integrality certificate for the associated set-packing formulation; total balancedness is a stronger certificate because every totally balanced matrix is balanced.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Absence of an odd cycle submatrix certifies integrality of the binary matrix's set-packing relaxation; total balancedness imposes the stronger all-orders exclusion.
knowledge_statements.title: Balanced-Matrix Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The balanced-matrix integrality claim is mathematically standard and fits the certificate container, but no source or inspectable locator is supplied.

children.title: Submodular Certificates
children.top_down_role: Integrality support derived from submodular set-function structure.

assumptions_latex: \(E\) is finite and \(f:2^E\to\mathbb{Z}_{+}\) is normalized, nondecreasing, and submodular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The polymatroid \(P(f)\) is integral.

notation.meaning: The sum of components indexed by S.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integral polymatroids induced by integer-valued submodular rank functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Submodularity means \(f(S)+f(T)\geq f(S\cup T)+f(S\cap T)\) for all \(S,T\subseteq E\), while normalization means \(f(\varnothing)=0\). Define \[P(f)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}_{+}^{E}:x(S)\leq f(S)\text{ for every }S\subseteq E\}.\] If \(f\) is integer-valued, nondecreasing, normalized, and submodular, every vertex of \(P(f)\) is integral. Consequently, exhibiting such a function \(f\) whose subset inequalities describe a relaxation certifies that relaxation's integrality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An integer-valued, normalized, nondecreasing submodular function certifies that its subset-inequality polymatroid has only integral vertices.
knowledge_statements.title: Submodular Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The integral-polymatroid statement is precise and appropriately classified as a certificate, but its vertex-integrality theorem has no cited source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimal dual certificate from the greedy closure chain
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit optimal dual solution for the matroid rank-inequality LP when the displayed greedy solution is nonempty; the proposition's formula does not state the empty-solution case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $S^G=\{j_1,\ldots,j_p\}$, with $p\ge 1$, be the greedy solution to the maximum-weight independent-set problem, listed in greedy acceptance order. Define $J_t=\{j_1,\ldots,j_t\}$ and $K_t=\operatorname{sp}(J_t)$. Then the dual solution given by $y_{K_t}=c_{j_t}-c_{j_{t+1}}$ for $t=1,\ldots,p-1$, $y_{K_p}=c_{j_p}$, and $y_K=0$ for all other $K\subseteq N$ is optimal for the dual of the matroid rank-inequality linear program.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonempty greedy solution, assign successive accepted-weight differences to the closures of successive greedy sets, assign the final accepted weight to the last closure, and set every other dual variable to zero. This gives an optimal dual solution.
assumptions_latex: (N,r)\text{ is the matroid defining the rank-inequality linear program}
S^G=\{j_1,\ldots,j_p\}\text{ is the greedy solution in acceptance order}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Greedy optimization over a submodular polyhedron
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Greedy construction for a nonnegative linear objective after ordering its coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), let \(f:2^N\to\mathbb{Z}\) be submodular with \(f(\varnothing)=0\), and let \(P(f)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:x(S)\le f(S)\ \forall S\subseteq N\}\). After relabeling so that \(c_1\ge c_2\ge\cdots\ge c_n\ge0\), set \(S_0=\varnothing\), \(S_j=\{1,\ldots,j\}\), and \(\bar x_j=f(S_j)-f(S_{j-1})\). Then \(\bar x\) is an optimal solution of \(\max\{c^Tx:x\in P(f)\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sort the nonnegative objective coefficients in decreasing order and assign each coordinate the marginal increase of the submodular function along the resulting chain; the constructed vector optimizes the linear objective over the submodular polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar x_j=f(S_j)-f(S_{j-1})\ (j\in N)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \bar x\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in P(f)}c^Tx

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Integrality and total dual integrality of submodular polyhedra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integrality and TDI certificate for normalized integer-valued submodular functions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monotone, Submodular, Supermodular, and Submodular Rank Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Collects the defining inequalities and normalization conditions for finite-set functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let N be finite and f:2^N\to\mathbb R. The function f is nondecreasing if S\subseteq T\subseteq N implies f(S)\le f(T); it is submodular if f(S)+f(T)\ge f(S\cup T)+f(S\cap T) for all S,T\subseteq N; and it is supermodular if -f is submodular. A function r:2^N\to\mathbb R is a submodular rank function if r(\varnothing)=0, r is integer-valued, nondecreasing, and submodular, and r(\{j\})\le 1 for every j\in N.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set function is nondecreasing when inclusion cannot decrease its value, submodular when it satisfies the union-intersection inequality, and supermodular when its negative is submodular. A submodular rank function is normalized at the empty set, integer-valued, nondecreasing, submodular, and at most one on every singleton.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}f\text{ nondecreasing}&\iff \forall S\subseteq T\subseteq N,\ f(S)\le f(T),\\ f\text{ submodular}&\iff \forall S,T\subseteq N,\ f(S)+f(T)\ge f(S\cup T)+f(S\cap T),\\ f\text{ supermodular}&\iff -f\text{ is submodular},\\ r\text{ rank}&\iff r(\varnothing)=0,\ r\in\mathbb Z,\ r\text{ is nondecreasing and submodular, and }\forall j\in N,\ r(\{j\})\le1.\end{aligned}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite matroid independence systems and their rank-inequality formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite matroid \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) with rank function \(r\), define \[P_I(M)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}_{+}^{E}:x(S)\leq r(S)\text{ for every }S\subseteq E\}.\] Then \[P_I(M)=\operatorname{conv}\{\chi^I:I\in\mathcal I\}.\] In particular, every vertex is a zero-one incidence vector of an independent set. Therefore, a valid matroid rank function together with the complete family of rank inequalities is an integrality certificate for the corresponding independence-set formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matroid rank inequalities describe exactly the convex hull of independent-set incidence vectors and therefore certify a zero-one integral relaxation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear Matroid Minors and Closure of Regularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines contraction-deletion minors and records minor closure for regular and binary matroids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let M=(S,\mathcal I) be a linear matroid and let S_1,S_2\subseteq S be disjoint. On S\setminus(S_1\cup S_2), define \mathcal I'=\{S' : S'\text{ is linearly independent modulo }\operatorname{span}(S_1)\}. Then (S\setminus(S_1\cup S_2),\mathcal I') is the minor obtained by contracting S_1 and deleting S_2. Every minor of a regular matroid is regular, and every minor of a binary matroid is binary. Consequently, a regular matroid has neither the Fano matroid nor its dual as a minor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Contracting one set of elements and deleting a disjoint set produces a linear-matroid minor, with independence measured modulo the span of the contracted elements. Regular and binary matroids are closed under minors; in particular, regular matroids cannot contain the Fano matroid or its dual as a minor.
assumptions_latex: M=(S,\mathcal I)\text{ is a linear matroid represented by vectors}
V\text{ is independent modulo }L\iff V\cup B_L\text{ is independent for a basis }B_L\text{ of }L
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M/S_1\setminus S_2\text{ is a linear matroid};\quad M\text{ regular (binary)}\Rightarrow M/S_1\setminus S_2\text{ regular (binary)};\quad M\text{ regular}\Rightarrow F_7,F_7^*\not\preccurlyeq M.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Maximal and Maximum Independent Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes inclusion maximality from maximum cardinality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \mathcal I=(N,\mathcal F) be an independence system. An independent set F\in\mathcal F is maximal if F\cup\{j\}\notin\mathcal F for every j\in N\setminus F. A maximal independent set T is maximum if |S|\le |T| for every S\in\mathcal F.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An independent set is maximal if no element outside it can be added while preserving independence. A maximal independent set is maximum if its cardinality is at least that of every independent set.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal I=(N,\mathcal F)\text{ is an independence system}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ maximal}\iff \forall j\in N\setminus F,\ F\cup\{j\}\notin\mathcal F;\qquad T\text{ maximum}\iff \forall S\in\mathcal F,\ |S|\le |T|

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Independence System
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines hereditary set systems and their independent and dependent subsets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let N=\{1,\ldots,n\} be finite and \mathcal F\subseteq 2^N. The pair \mathcal I=(N,\mathcal F) is an independence system if, for every F_1\in\mathcal F and F_2\subseteq F_1, one has F_2\in\mathcal F. Members of \mathcal F are independent sets; subsets of N outside \mathcal F are dependent sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An independence system is a finite ground set together with a downward-closed family of subsets. Members of the family are independent, and all other subsets are dependent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F_1\in\mathcal F\ \land\ F_2\subseteq F_1\ \Longrightarrow\ F_2\in\mathcal F

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Basis, circuit, and closure of a matroid
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions for a matroid with a specified rank function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $M=(N,\mathcal F)$ be a matroid with rank function $r$. A set $A$ is a basis if $A\in\mathcal F$ and $r(A)=r(N)$. It is a circuit if it is minimally dependent: $A\notin\mathcal F$ and $A\setminus\{j\}\in\mathcal F$ for every $j\in A$. For any $A\subseteq N$, its span or closure is $\operatorname{sp}(A)=\{j\in N:r(A\cup\{j\})=r(A)\}$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A basis is an independent set having full matroid rank. A circuit is a dependent set whose deletion of any element is independent. The span or closure of A consists of all ground-set elements whose addition does not increase the rank of A.
assumptions_latex: $M=(N,\mathcal F)$ is a matroid with rank function $r$
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A\text{ is a basis iff }A\in\mathcal F\text{ and }r(A)=r(N);\quad A\text{ is a circuit iff }A\notin\mathcal F\text{ and }A\setminus\{j\}\in\mathcal F\ \forall j\in A;\quad \operatorname{sp}(A)=\{j\in N:r(A\cup\{j\})=r(A)\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Maximum-Cardinality Matroid Intersection Algorithm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Augmenting-path algorithm using the exchange digraph of the current common independent set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize with $S^1\in\mathcal F_1\cap\mathcal F_2$ and set $q=1$. At iteration $q$, construct $\mathcal D_{S^q}$. If it has no $s$-$t$ dipath, stop and return $S^q$. Otherwise choose a shortest dipath $(s,j_1,k_1,\ldots,j_p,t)$, set $S^{q+1}=(S^q\cup\{j_1,\ldots,j_p\})\setminus\{k_1,\ldots,k_{p-1}\}$, increment $q$, and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Begin with a set independent in both matroids. Repeatedly construct its exchange digraph. If no directed s–t path exists, return the current set as optimal; otherwise augment along a shortest such path by adding its j-nodes and deleting its k-nodes.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal D_{S^q}\text{ is the exchange digraph associated with }S^q
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The stopping iterate }S^q\text{ is an optimal maximum-cardinality common independent set}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fractional matroid covering characterization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Here \(\zeta_w\) is the value of the referenced fractional covering problem and \(y^*\) is an optimal covering solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a matroid polytope \(P(r)\), the fractional covering value satisfies (i) \(\zeta_w\le 1\iff w\in P(r)\); (ii) \(\zeta_w=\max_{S\subseteq N}\frac{\sum_{j\in S}w_j}{r(S)}\); and (iii) \(w/\zeta_w\in P(r)\). Moreover, if \(y^*\) is optimal, then \(y^*/\zeta_w\) expresses \(w/\zeta_w\) as a convex combination of points of \(P(r)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a matroid polytope, the fractional independent-set covering value is the maximum rank-density ratio. A vector has covering value at most one exactly when it lies in the polytope, and normalization by the covering value yields a point of the polytope together with a convex-combination representation from any normalized optimal covering solution.
assumptions_latex: P(r)\text{ is a matroid polytope on }N
\zeta_w\text{ is the value of the fractional covering problem for }w
y^*\text{ is an optimal solution when the final assertion is invoked}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \zeta_w\le 1\iff w\in P(r),\quad \zeta_w=\max_{S\subseteq N}\frac{\sum_{j\in S}w_j}{r(S)},\quad \frac{w}{\zeta_w}\in P(r),\quad \frac{y^*}{\zeta_w}\text{ represents }\frac{w}{\zeta_w}\text{ as a convex combination in }P(r).

children.top_down_role: Polyhedral structure associated with bases of combinatorial independence systems.

assumptions_latex: \(E\) is finite and \(f:2^E\to\mathbb{R}\) is normalized and submodular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every vertex of \(B(f)\) is generated by a greedy ordering; if \(f\) is integer-valued, \(B(f)\) is integral.

notation.meaning: The prefix set induced by a permutation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Greedy vertex representation of finite submodular base polytopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The base polytope of \(f\) is \[B(f)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^{E}:x(S)\leq f(S)\text{ for all }S\subseteq E,\ x(E)=f(E)\}.\] For a permutation \((e_1,\ldots,e_n)\) of \(E\), let \(S_k=\{e_1,\ldots,e_k\}\) and set \(x_{e_k}=f(S_k)-f(S_{k-1})\). Every such greedy vector belongs to \(B(f)\), and every vertex of \(B(f)\) is obtained from some permutation, allowing repetitions under ties. If \(f\) is integer-valued, all these vertices are integral.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A submodular base polytope has a greedy permutation representation of its vertices, which makes the polytope integral whenever the submodular function is integer-valued.

children.title: Submodular–Matroidal Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural overlap between submodular polyhedra and matroid-based descriptions.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stated rank axioms are equivalent to \(r\) being a matroid rank function.

notation.meaning: The subsets declared independent by r.
The matroid base polytope associated with r.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between finite matroid ranks and unit-bounded integral submodular functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(r\) is the rank function of a matroid on \(E\) if and only if \(r(\varnothing)=0\), \(r\) is nondecreasing and submodular, and \(0\leq r(S)\leq |S|\) for every \(S\subseteq E\). Under these conditions, \[\mathcal I_r=\{I\subseteq E:r(I)=|I|\}\] is the independent-set family of that matroid. Conversely, every matroid rank satisfies these conditions. Its bases are precisely the zero-one points of \[B(r)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}_{+}^{E}:x(S)\leq r(S)\text{ for all }S\subseteq E,\ x(E)=r(E)\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matroid ranks are exactly normalized, integer-valued, nondecreasing submodular functions bounded by cardinality; their base-polytope zero-one points are the matroid bases.
knowledge_statements.title: Submodular–Matroidal Correspondence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated rank-function correspondence is a theorem/characterization rather than a duality, and its equivalence and base-polytope claims lack a cited source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Elementary characterizations of submodularity and monotone submodularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two equivalences for a set function on a finite ground set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $f:2^N\to\mathbb{R}$. First, $f$ is submodular if and only if, for every $S\subseteq N\setminus\{j,k\}$ and distinct $j,k\in N$, $f(S\cup\{j\})-f(S)\ge f(S\cup\{j,k\})-f(S\cup\{k\})$. Second, $f$ is submodular and nondecreasing if and only if, for all $S,T\subseteq N$, $f(T)\le f(S)+\sum_{j\in T\setminus S}\bigl(f(S\cup\{j\})-f(S)\bigr)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set function is submodular exactly when every element's marginal value cannot increase after another distinct element is added. It is both submodular and nondecreasing exactly when its value on any set T is bounded above by its value on S plus the sum of the single-element marginal gains from S for elements of T outside S.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is submodular}\iff\text{the pairwise diminishing-returns inequalities hold},\qquad f\text{ is submodular and nondecreasing}\iff\text{the stated upper bounds hold}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Submodular Minimization–Separation–Rank Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes a submodular minimizer through a most-violated polymatroid inequality and attainment of the polymatroid rank formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:2^N\to\mathbb R\) be submodular with \(f(\varnothing)=0\), define \(k_j=f(N\setminus\{j\})-f(N)\), assume \(k\in\mathbb R_+^N\), and set \(f^*(S)=f(S)+\sum_{j\in S}k_j\). For \(S^*\subseteq N\), the following are equivalent: (i) \(S^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{S\subseteq N}f(S)\); (ii) \(x(S^*)\le f^*(S^*)\) is a most violated defining inequality of \(P(f^*)\) at \(x=k\); and (iii) \[r_{P(f^*)}(k)=f^*(S^*)+\sum_{j\in N\setminus S^*}k_j.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set minimizes the normalized submodular function exactly when its transformed polymatroid inequality is most violated at k, equivalently when it attains the rank formula at k.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{S\subseteq N}f(S)\iff x(S^*)\le f^*(S^*)\text{ is most violated at }x=k\iff r_{P(f^*)}(k)=f^*(S^*)+k(N\setminus S^*).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Greedy primal-dual solutions for polymatroid optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States explicit optimal primal and dual solutions after ordering the objective coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P(f)=\{x\in\mathbb R_+^N:\sum_{j\in S}x_j\le f(S)\ \forall S\subseteq N\}\), and order the indices so that \(c_1\ge\cdots\ge c_k>0\ge c_{k+1}\ge\cdots\ge c_n\). With \(S^j=\{1,\ldots,j\}\) and \(S^0=\varnothing\), an optimal solution of \(\max\{c^Tx:x\in P(f)\}\) is \[x_j=\begin{cases}f(S^j)-f(S^{j-1}),&1\le j\le k,\\0,&j>k.\end{cases}\] For its dual \(\min\{\sum_{S\subseteq N}f(S)y_S:\sum_{S\ni j}y_S\ge c_j\ \forall j,\ y\ge0\}\), an optimal solution is \[y_{S^j}=\begin{cases}c_j-c_{j+1},&1\le j<k,\\c_k,&j=k,\end{cases}\qquad y_S=0\text{ otherwise}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After sorting the objective coefficients and retaining their positive prefix, greedy marginal increments of the submodular function give an optimal polymatroid point; successive coefficient differences on the nested prefix sets give an optimal dual solution.
assumptions_latex: f:2^N\to\mathbb R\text{ is nondecreasing and submodular with }f(\varnothing)=0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_j=f(S^j)-f(S^{j-1})\ (1\le j\le k),\ x_j=0\ (j>k),\quad y_{S^j}=c_j-c_{j+1}\ (j<k),\ y_{S^k}=c_k,\ y_S=0\text{ otherwise, are primal-dual optimal solutions}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bounded Dual-Change Search Alternative
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Progress-or-optimality guarantee for one phase of weighted matroid intersection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Starting from the current cardinality level \(q\) and set \(S\), after at most \(n\) dual changes, either an \(s\)-\(t\) directed path is found in the associated exchange digraph or \(S\) is optimal for every cardinality bound \(q'\ge q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Within at most n dual changes, the procedure either discovers an s-to-t directed path or certifies that the current set S is optimal for every cardinality level at least q.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weighted Matroid Intersection Algorithm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal–dual augmentation algorithm using exchange-digraph shortest paths and dual changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a common independent set \(S^q\) and a weight decomposition \(c^1+c^2=c\), using \(q=0\) and \(S^q=\varnothing\) if no positive-cardinality initial solution is known. Compute \(m_1,m_2\); stop with \(S^q\) optimal for all \(q'\ge q\) when \(m_1+m_2\le0\), otherwise normalize a negative \(m_i\) by transferring its constant amount between \(c^1\) and \(c^2\). Construct \(\mathcal D_{S^q}(c^1,c^2)\). If it contains an \(s\)-\(t\) dipath, use a shortest such path to augment to an optimal \(S^{q+1}\in\mathcal F_2^{q+1}\), set \(q\leftarrow q+1\), and repeat. If no such path exists, perform the prescribed dual change; stop with \(S^q\) optimal for all \(q'\ge q\) when \(\varepsilon=m_1+m_2\), and otherwise rebuild the parameters and exchange digraph and continue.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialize a common independent set and split the weights into two components. Repeatedly test the stopping quantities and build the exchange digraph. A shortest s-to-t path produces an augmentation to the next cardinality level; absence of such a path triggers a dual change. The stated stopping tests certify optimality of the current set for every larger cardinality bound.
assumptions_latex: S^q\text{ is initialized as prescribed, or }q=0\text{ and }S^q=\varnothing
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The procedure alternates shortest-path augmentations and dual changes until it returns }S^q\text{ optimal for every }q'\ge q.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Basic constructions preserving submodularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Four sufficient constructions for submodular set functions on a common finite ground set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $N$ be finite. (a) For arbitrary $a_0\in\mathbb{R}$ and $a_j\in\mathbb{R}$, $f(S)=a_0+\sum_{j\in S}a_j$ is submodular. (b) If $f$ is submodular, then $\bar f(S)=f(N\setminus S)$ is submodular. (c) If $f$ is submodular and $k\in\mathbb{R}$, then $f'(S)=\min\{f(S),k\}$ is submodular. (d) If $f_1$ and $f_2$ are submodular, then $f_1+f_2$ is submodular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Modular set functions are submodular. Submodularity is preserved by taking the complementary-set function, truncating values above a real threshold, and adding two submodular functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: a_0+\sum_{j\in S}a_j,\quad f(N\setminus S),\quad \min\{f(S),k\},\quad\text{and}\quad f_1(S)+f_2(S)\text{ are submodular under the stated hypotheses}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Characterization by downward closure and equal maximal sums
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives sufficient conditions for a subset of the nonnegative orthant to be a polymatroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R_+^N\). Suppose (i) \(x\in P\), \(y\in\mathbb R_+^N\), and \(y\le x\) imply \(y\in P\); and (ii) for every \(a\in\mathbb R^N\), any two maximal points \(x^1,x^2\) of \(P\cap\{x\in\mathbb R_+^N:x\le a\}\) satisfy \(\sum_{j\in N}x_j^1=\sum_{j\in N}x_j^2\). Then \(P\) is a polymatroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A downward-closed subset of the nonnegative orthant is a polymatroid if, under every componentwise bound, all maximal feasible points have the same coordinate sum.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Zero-Minimum Certificate by Polymatroid Membership
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes a zero minimum of a normalized submodular function by membership and rank saturation in the transformed polymatroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:2^N\to\mathbb R\) be submodular with \(f(\varnothing)=0\), define \(k_j=f(N\setminus\{j\})-f(N)\), assume \(k\in\mathbb R_+^N\), and set \(f^*(S)=f(S)+\sum_{j\in S}k_j\). knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized submodular function has minimum zero exactly when k belongs to its transformed polymatroid, equivalently when the polymatroid rank at k equals the coordinate sum of k.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{S\subseteq N}f(S)=0\iff k\in P(f^*)\iff r_{P(f^*)}(k)=k(N).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Properties of a Submodular Rank Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cardinality bounds, hereditary full rank, and the associated-polyhedron characterization of full-rank sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let r be a submodular rank function on N with r(\varnothing)=0. Then: (i) r(A)\leq |A| for every A\subseteq N; (ii) if r(A)=|A|, then r(B)=|B| for every B\subset A; and (iii), if x^A is the incidence vector of A\subseteq N, then x^A\in P(r) if and only if r(A)=|A|.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A submodular rank function normalized at the empty set is bounded by cardinality. Full rank is inherited by every proper subset, and a set has full rank exactly when its incidence vector belongs to the associated polyhedron.
assumptions_latex: r\text{ is a submodular rank function on }N
x^A\text{ is the incidence vector of }A
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r(A)\leq |A|;\quad r(A)=|A|\Rightarrow (\forall B\subset A)\,r(B)=|B|;\quad x^A\in P(r)\iff r(A)=|A|

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A block-angular formulation has variable blocks \(x^k\in X_k\) and constraints \[A_kx^k=b_k\quad(k=1,\ldots,K),\qquad \sum_{k=1}^{K}D_kx^k=d.\] After compatible row and column permutations, its matrix is \[\begin{pmatrix}A_1&0&\cdots&0\\0&A_2&\cdots&0\\\vdots&\vdots&\ddots&\vdots\\0&0&\cdots&A_K\\D_1&D_2&\cdots&D_K\end{pmatrix}.\] The diagonal rows define independent local subsystems, while the final row block supplies all cross-block coupling. Removing the linking rows therefore decomposes the model into \(K\) independent optimization problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block-angular model consists of independent diagonal variable blocks coupled only by a common set of linking constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Block-Angular Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual block-angular formulations coupled through a shared variable block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A dual block-angular formulation has a shared vector \(y\) and local vectors \(x^k\in X_k\), with subsystem constraints \[T_ky+W_kx^k=h_k\qquad(k=1,\ldots,K).\] After compatible permutations, its matrix is \[\begin{pmatrix}T_1&W_1&0&\cdots&0\\T_2&0&W_2&\cdots&0\\\vdots&\vdots&\vdots&\ddots&\vdots\\T_K&0&0&\cdots&W_K\end{pmatrix}.\] The first column block is shared by every subsystem, whereas each remaining column block occurs in only one subsystem. Hence fixing \(y\) leaves \(K\) independent local feasible systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual block-angular model has one shared variable block appearing in every subsystem and otherwise disjoint local variables and constraints.
assumptions_latex: Variables are partitioned into shared variables \(y\) and local variables \(x^1,\ldots,x^K\).
Each subsystem has a local feasible set \(X_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Fixing \(y\) separates the model into \(K\) independent local subsystems.

knowledge_statements.title: Staircase Block Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear sequential models with nearest-neighbor stage coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A staircase block structure is obtained when stage \(t\) constraints involve only \(x_{t-1}\) and \(x_t\). After ordering variables and constraints by stage, the matrix has the form \[\begin{pmatrix}W_1&0&0&\cdots&0\\T_2&W_2&0&\cdots&0\\0&T_3&W_3&\ddots&\vdots\\\vdots&\ddots&\ddots&\ddots&0\\0&\cdots&0&T_T&W_T\end{pmatrix}.\] Thus each off-diagonal block records coupling to the immediately preceding stage, and no constraint row directly couples nonconsecutive stages. Fixing \(x_{t-1}\) isolates the stage \(t\) local constraint system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A staircase matrix orders stages so each constraint block contains only current-stage variables and, at most, variables from the immediately preceding stage.
assumptions_latex: Rows and columns are partitioned into ordered stages \(1,\ldots,T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constraint matrix is block lower-bidiagonal and permits forward stagewise evaluation once predecessor variables are fixed.

notation.meaning: The within-stage matrix at stage t.
The matrix coupling stage t to its predecessor.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Block-band quadratic structure and its splitting bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block-tridiagonal quadratic coefficient matrices as a specialization of sequential staircase block sparsity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P=\{J_1,\ldots,J_p\}\) partition the variable indices, with \(n_k=|J_k|\) and \(n=\sum_{k=1}^p n_k\). A quadratic model has band structure if every relevant matrix \(A_i\) is block tridiagonal, with diagonal blocks \(A_{i,k}\) and off-diagonal blocks \(B_{i,k}\) only between consecutive blocks \(J_k\) and \(J_{k+1}\). Then \(R_k=J_{k+1}\) for \(k<p\) and \(R_p=\varnothing\). The associated splitting scheme has block sizes \(n_1+n_2,\ldots,n_{p-1}+n_p,n_p\) and introduces at most \(\sum_{k=2}^p n_k=n-n_1\) additional variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If each quadratic coefficient matrix couples only consecutive variable blocks, the induced splitting scheme copies the next block for each nonfinal block. Its auxiliary-variable count is at most n−n₁.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P=\{J_1,\ldots,J_p\}\) is a partition of the variable indices
Every relevant \(A_i\) is block tridiagonal, with off-diagonal couplings only between \(J_k\) and \(J_{k+1}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_k=J_{k+1}\ \text{for }k<p,\quad R_p=\varnothing,\quad N_{\mathrm{additional}}\leq\sum_{k=2}^p n_k=n-n_1.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite multistage model partitions decisions as \(x=(x_1,ldots,x_T)\), with \(x_t\in X_t\), and represents the objective and constraints by stage-indexed terms whose stage \(t\) data are contained in \(\xi_{1:t}\). A canonical form is \[\min\ \sum_{t=1}^{T}c_t(\xi_{1:t})^{\mathsf T}x_t\quad\text{subject to}\quad g_t(x_{1:t},\xi_{1:t})\leq0\quad(t=1,ldots,T).\] In a sequential block architecture, dependence on earlier decisions is represented through explicit state, linking, or nonanticipativity constraints, making the stage ownership of every variable and constraint identifiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multistage model partitions variables, constraints, and revealed data by decision stage, with explicit links carrying relevant effects from earlier stages.

children.title: Interstage Coupling
children.top_down_role: Variables or constraints linking consecutive or separated stages.

knowledge_statements.title: Interstage Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nearest-neighbor linear coupling in sequential block formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a consecutive-stage linear model, interstage coupling is represented by constraints \[T_tx_{t-1}+W_tx_t=h_t\qquad(t=2,\ldots,T),\] together with an initial-stage constraint \(W_1x_1=h_1\). The block \(T_t\) contains every coefficient through which the predecessor decision \(x_{t-1}\) affects feasibility at stage \(t\); \(W_t\) contains current-stage coefficients. Consequently, setting all \(T_t=0\) makes the stage constraint systems independent, while nonzero \(T_t\) constitute the algebraic interfaces between adjacent stages.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interstage coupling consists of the linking blocks that transmit predecessor-stage decisions into current-stage constraints; removing them separates the stages.
assumptions_latex: Stage constraints are linear and couple only consecutive stage vectors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The matrices \(T_t\) are the complete algebraic interface transmitting decisions between adjacent stages.

children.title: Stagewise Information Structure
children.top_down_role: Visibility and dependency patterns associated with staged decisions.

assumptions_latex: \((\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)\) is a probability space with filtration \((\mathcal F_t)_{t=0}^{T}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasible stage decisions are adapted to \((\mathcal F_t)\), equivalently satisfying nonanticipativity across indistinguishable histories.

notation.meaning: Information available when the stage t decision is chosen.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonanticipative decisions in finite-horizon stochastic multistage models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A stagewise information structure is specified by a filtration \[\mathcal F_0\subseteq\mathcal F_1\subseteq\cdots	u0018subseteq\mathcal F_T\subseteq\mathcal F.\] A stage \(t\) decision rule is admissible only if \(x_t\) is \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable. In a finite scenario tree, this is equivalent to the nonanticipativity condition \[x_t(\omega)=x_t(\omega')\quad\text{whenever scenarios }\omega\text{ and }\omega'\text{ have identical histories through stage }t.\] Thus decisions may depend on information revealed by their decision time but not on later observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stage decisions must use only currently revealed information, equivalently taking equal values on scenarios with identical histories through that stage.
knowledge_statements.title: Stagewise Information Structure

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For variables indexed by \(V\), the primal sparsity graph is \(G=(V,E)\), where distinct vertices \(i,j\in V\) satisfy \(\{i,j\}\in E\) exactly when some constraint or nonseparable objective term depends jointly on \(x_i\) and \(x_j\). Equivalently, each expression with support \(S\subseteq V\) induces a clique on \(S\). If \(G\) has multiple connected components and no omitted global expression intersects two components, the formulation separates into independent variable subsystems indexed by those components. Graph separators identify variable sets through which the remaining subsystems interact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sparsity graph joins variables that occur jointly in a model expression; its components and separators expose independent blocks and their interfaces.
knowledge_statements.title: Sparsity-Graph Models

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-support hypergraph for a finite optimization formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) index the variables of a finite optimization model and let \(R\) index its constraints. For every \(r\in R\), define \(S_r=\{v\in V: x_v\text{ occurs nontrivially in constraint }r\}\). The sparsity hypergraph is \(H=(V,\mathcal E)\), where \(\mathcal E=\{S_r:r\in R,\ S_r\neq\varnothing\}\). Repeated supports may either be retained as labeled hyperedges \((r,S_r)\) or merged when constraint identity is irrelevant. Thus each constraint is represented by one hyperedge, preserving every higher-order variable interaction induced by that constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sparsity hypergraph has one vertex per variable and one hyperedge equal to the support of each constraint, thereby retaining higher-order interactions within constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Sparsity-Hypergraph Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the hypergraph leaf and is mathematically standard, but it has no inspectable citation. It also disagrees with its own conclusion about whether empty supports are retained: the conclusion includes every S_r, whereas the statement excludes empty S_r. A sourced version must choose one convention and use it consistently.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal interaction graph induced by constraint co-occurrence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given variable indices \(V\) and constraint supports \((S_r)_{r\in R}\), the variable-interaction graph is the simple undirected graph \(G_V=(V,E_V)\) with \(\{u,v\}\in E_V\) if and only if \(u\neq v\) and there exists \(r\in R\) such that \(\{u,v\}\subseteq S_r\). Equivalently, every hyperedge \(S_r\) of the sparsity hypergraph is replaced by a clique. Constants and objective-only interactions are excluded unless their supports are explicitly included as additional labeled rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two variable vertices are adjacent exactly when some constraint contains both variables; equivalently, every constraint support induces a clique.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given constraint indices \(R\) and their variable supports \((S_r)_{r\in R}\), the constraint-intersection graph is the simple undirected graph \(G_R=(R,E_R)\) satisfying \(\{r,s\}\in E_R\) if and only if \(r\neq s\) and \(S_r\cap S_s\neq\varnothing\). children.title: Dantzig–Wolfe Modeling Interface
children.top_down_role: Block configurations and master linking structures.

assumptions_latex: For each block \(k\), \(X_k\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_k}\) is nonempty and \(P_k=\operatorname{conv}(X_k)=\operatorname{conv}\{v^{kp}:p\in\mathcal P_k\}\).
The only cross-block constraints are \(\sum_k A_kx^k=b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing each \(x^k\in P_k\) by convex-combination variables yields the Dantzig--Wolfe master formulation.

notation.meaning: extreme-point or configuration index set for block k
master weight for configuration p of block k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite or implicitly indexed block convexification with master linking rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{\sum_k c_k^\top x^k:\sum_k A_kx^k=b,\ x^k\in P_k\}\), where \(P_k=\operatorname{conv}\{v^{kp}:p\in\mathcal P_k\}\). Substituting \(x^k=\sum_{p\in\mathcal P_k}v^{kp}\lambda_{kp}\) gives the master formulation \[\min\ \sum_k\sum_{p\in\mathcal P_k}(c_k^\top v^{kp})\lambda_{kp}\quad\text{subject to}\quad \sum_k\sum_{p\in\mathcal P_k}A_kv^{kp}\lambda_{kp}=b,\quad \sum_{p\in\mathcal P_k}\lambda_{kp}=1\ \forall k,\quad \lambda_{kp}\geq0.\] The interface exposes the block configurations and retains only linking and convexity rows in the master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each block solution is represented as a convex combination of configurations, while a master model enforces cross-block linking and one convexity equation per block.

children.title: Benders Modeling Interface
children.top_down_role: Partition of complicating variables from operational subproblem variables.

assumptions_latex: The problem is \(\min\{c^\top y+q^\top x:Ay+Bx\geq d,\ y\in Y,\ x\in\mathbb R^n\}\).
For every relevant \(y\in Y\), the continuous subproblem is either infeasible or has a finite optimum, and linear-programming duality and Farkas' lemma apply.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The operational subproblem is represented in the master by dual optimality cuts and Farkas feasibility cuts in the complicating variables \(y\).

notation.meaning: dual feasible set for optimality cuts

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical LP-dual Benders interface with free operational variables, master variables, and explicit optimality and feasibility certificates.

source_refs.locator: 4.4 Benders decomposition p. 52
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed \(y\in Y\), define \(Q(y)=\min\{q^\top x:Bx\geq d-Ay,\ x\in\mathbb R^n\}\). Let \(U=\{u\geq0:B^\top u=q\}\) and \(C=\{r\geq0:B^\top r=0\}\). Whenever the subproblem has a finite optimum, linear-programming duality gives \(Q(y)=\sup_{u\in U}u^\top(d-Ay)\), so the master may use an epigraph variable \(\theta\) and cuts \(\theta\geq u^\top(d-Ay)\) for the relevant extreme points \(u\) of \(U\). Subproblem feasibility requires \(r^\top(d-Ay)\leq0\) for every \(r\in C\), and violated inequalities generated from extreme rays of \(C\) are Benders feasibility cuts. Thus the operational variables remain confined to the subproblem while the master contains \(y\), \(\theta\), and the generated cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interface keeps complicating variables in a master problem and represents the continuous operational subproblem by dual optimality cuts and Farkas feasibility cuts.
knowledge_statements.title: Benders Modeling Interface

children.title: Lagrangian Modeling Interface
children.top_down_role: Identification of coupling constraints whose removal exposes separable structure.

assumptions_latex: The objective is separable, while coupling constraints have the form \(\sum_k A_kx^k=b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dualizing the coupling equations produces a separable Lagrangian value \(L(\lambda)=\sum_k\inf_{x^k\in X_k}(f_k(x^k)+\lambda^\top A_kx^k)-\lambda^\top b\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-coupled separable minimization and its Lagrangian decomposition.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{\sum_{k=1}^K f_k(x^k):x^k\in X_k,\ \sum_k A_kx^k=b\}\), mark the linking equation as dualizable. With multiplier \(\lambda\), the Lagrangian dual function is \[L(\lambda)=\inf_{x^k\in X_k}\left\{\sum_k f_k(x^k)+\lambda^\top\left(\sum_k A_kx^k-b\right)\right\}=\sum_k\inf_{x^k\in X_k}\{f_k(x^k)+\lambda^\top A_kx^k\}-\lambda^\top b.\] The interface therefore consists of the block sets, block objectives, coupling rows, and their multiplier domain; the dual problem is \(\sup_\lambda L(\lambda)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Marking coupling rows for dualization separates the Lagrangian evaluation into independent block problems coordinated by common multipliers.
knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Modeling Interface

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Maximum-Flow Separation of Cardinality-Restricted Subtour Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies to the stated symmetric traveling-salesman subtour-separation problem on the weighted graph defined by the current solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix node \(1\) and define \(\zeta=\min\{\sum_{e\in\delta(U)}x_e^*:3\le |U|\le |V|-3,\ 1\in U\}\). For \(j=2,\ldots,|V|-2\), let \(\zeta_j\) be the same minimum with \(\{1,\ldots,j-1\}\subset U\) and \(j\notin U\). Then \(\zeta=\min_{j=2,\ldots,|V|-2}\zeta_j\). The required inclusions can be imposed in the \(1\)-\(j\) cut problem by assigning infinite capacity to \(\{1,k\}\) for \(k=2,\ldots,j-1\), so the separation algorithm solves the corresponding maximum \(1\)-\(j\) flow problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After fixing an arbitrary node 1, the minimum eligible subtour cut is obtained from a sequence of constrained 1–j minimum cuts. Infinite-capacity edges keep the previously indexed nodes on node 1's side, and each cut problem is solved by maximum flow.
assumptions_latex: x_e^*\ge 0\text{ for edges used as capacities}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \zeta=\min_{j=2,\ldots,|V|-2}\zeta_j,\qquad\text{and the stated separation is performed by maximum }1\text{-}j\text{ flow computations.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Shrinking a Unit-Weight Edge
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the reduced weighted graph obtained by contracting an edge whose current value is one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(e=\{i,j\}\) with \(x_e^*=1\), replace \(i,j\) by a node \(l\). For each common neighbor \(k\), replace \(\{i,k\}\) and \(\{j,k\}\) by \(\{l,k\}\) with weight \(x'_{lk}=x^*_{ik}+x^*_{jk}\). Replace every other edge incident to \(i\) or \(j\) by the corresponding edge incident to \(l\), retaining its weight; all unaffected edges remain unchanged. The result is the reduced graph \(G(x')=(V',E(x'))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Contract the endpoints of a unit-valued edge. Parallel incidences to a common neighbor are combined by adding their weights, while all other incident edges are redirected to the contracted node without changing their weights.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G(x')\text{ is obtained by contracting }\{i,j\}\text{ and aggregating parallel edge weights additively.}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize with \(I_0\subseteq I\). At iteration \(t\), solve the restricted optimization problem containing only rows indexed by \(I_t\), obtaining \(x^t\). Invoke separation on \(x^t\). If it returns a violated set \(V_t\subseteq I\setminus I_t\), set \(I_{t+1}=I_t\cup V_t\) and repeat. If it certifies \(a_i^\top x^t\geq b_i\) for every \(i\in I\), stop and output \(x^t\). For a finite family, exact restricted solves, and no repeated additions, the method terminates after at most \(|I\setminus I_0|\) augmentations and the output solves the full relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve the current restricted model and add violated implicit inequalities; stop when separation certifies that no represented row is violated.

children.title: Column Generation
children.top_down_role: Implicit-variable exposure within a formulation interface.

assumptions_latex: The full finite linear program is \(\min\{\sum_{j\in J}c_jx_j:\sum_{j\in J}a_jx_j=b,\ x_j\geq0\ \forall j\in J\}\), and it has a finite optimum.
The initial restricted column set \(J_0\subseteq J\) yields a feasible restricted master, each restricted master is solved exactly, and pricing globally minimizes reduced cost over \(J\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A negative-reduced-cost column is added when one exists; if global pricing finds none, the restricted-master solution is optimal for the full linear program.

notation.meaning: dual vector for the equality rows

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(J_0\subseteq J\) so that the restricted master is feasible. At iteration \(t\), solve the restricted master over \(J_t\) and obtain an optimal primal solution and an optimal dual vector \(\pi^t\). For each \(j\in J\), define the reduced cost \(\bar c_j=c_j-(\pi^t)^\top a_j\). If global pricing returns \(j\in J\setminus J_t\) with \(\bar c_j<0\), set \(J_{t+1}=J_t\cup\{j\}\) and repeat. If pricing certifies \(\bar c_j\geq0\) for every \(j\in J\), then \(\pi^t\) is feasible for the full dual, and the restricted primal solution extended by zeros is optimal for the full linear program.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve a feasible restricted master, price every implicit nonnegative variable using the optimal dual solution, add a negative-reduced-cost column when one exists, and stop with a full-LP optimum when global pricing certifies that all reduced costs are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.title: Column Generation

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize active sets \(I_0\subseteq I\) and \(J_0\subseteq J\). At iteration \(t\), solve the restricted master on \((I_t,J_t)\), obtaining primal-dual solution \((x^t,\pi^t)\). Separation either returns violated rows \(R_t\subseteq I\setminus I_t\) or certifies full-row feasibility. Pricing either returns improving columns \(C_t\subseteq J\setminus J_t\) with negative reduced cost relative to \(\pi^t\), or certifies full-column dual feasibility. Update \(I_{t+1}=I_t\cup R_t\) and \(J_{t+1}=J_t\cup C_t\). Stop only when both certificates hold simultaneously; then \(x^t\) is feasible and optimal for the full LP. Finite exact families imply finite termination when each nonterminal iteration adds a new row or column.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(t\), solve the restricted master over rows \(I_t\subseteq I\) and columns \(J_t\subseteq J\). A valid stopping test must certify simultaneously that no omitted row in \(I\setminus I_t\) is violated by the current primal solution and that no omitted column in \(J\setminus J_t\) has improving reduced cost for an optimal restricted-master dual solution. Passing only one test is insufficient: a newly added row can change dual prices and make a previously nonimproving column improving, while a newly added column can change the primal solution and violate a previously satisfied omitted row. Hence generation must repeat after either type of addition until both certificates hold for the same solved master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Row and column generation may stop only when separation and pricing both certify the same solved restricted master; either new rows or new columns can invalidate the other certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Generation Coordination Boundaries

children.title: Lazy-Constraint Interfaces

assumptions_latex: The intended feasible set is \(F=\{x\in X:g_k(x)\le 0\text{ for every }k\in K\}\), where \(K\) may be too large to enumerate.
The separation callback is exact at every integer candidate presented for acceptance.

integer candidate submitted to the callback

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact lazy enforcement at integer candidates, distinct from optional relaxation cuts at fractional nodes.

source_refs.locator: 7.5 Using a Branch-and-Bound/Cut System p. 123

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the solver with the explicit constraints defining \(X\). Whenever it proposes an integer candidate \(\bar x\in X\), invoke a separation oracle. If the oracle returns \(k\in K\) with \(g_k(\bar x)>0\), add the lazy constraint \(g_k(x)\le 0\), reject \(\bar x\), and continue the search; if no such index exists, the candidate may be accepted. The oracle must search the complete omitted family needed to define \(F\), not merely a strengthening subset. Termination returns the best accepted incumbent together with the solver's usual optimality status. Correctness requires that lazy constraints remain globally valid and that no integer candidate is accepted without complete separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each integer candidate, exactly separate the full omitted constraint family. Reject a violator and add its valid constraint; accept only candidates certified feasible for every lazy constraint.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When the solver exposes a relaxation solution \(\bar x\in P_t\), call a cut-separation routine. The routine either returns no cut or returns coefficients \((\alpha,\beta)\) satisfying \(\alpha^\top x\le\beta\) for every \(x\in F\) and \(\alpha^\top\bar x>\beta\). In the latter case update \(P_{t+1}=P_t\cap\{x:\alpha^\top x\le\beta\}\) and reoptimize. A user cut must not remove any integer-feasible solution, including solutions outside the current node domain before branching bounds are imposed. Failure to find a cut does not certify feasibility for an omitted constraint family unless the interface is additionally specified as an exact separation oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A user-cut callback may add a globally valid inequality violated by the current relaxation point. It strengthens the relaxation but ordinarily does not certify omitted feasibility constraints.
