children.title: Node Relaxation Bounds
children.top_down_role: Relaxation-based bounds used within enumeration trees.

knowledge_statements.title: Node Relaxation Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimization-node bounds and their valid pruning test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[L_N=\inf\{c^{\mathsf T}x:x\in R_N\}.\] Since \(F_N\subseteq R_N\), relaxation monotonicity gives \[L_N\le\inf\{c^{\mathsf T}x:x\in F_N\}.\] If \(R_N=\varnothing\), then \(F_N=\varnothing\). If a feasible incumbent has value \(U\) and \(L_N\ge U\), no point represented by node \(N\) can improve that incumbent, so pruning is valid. Equality pruning assumes that another solution with objective value \(U\) need not be enumerated; enumeration of all optimal solutions requires a stricter convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxation containing the node's feasible set gives a lower bound; relaxation infeasibility or a bound no better than the incumbent permits pruning when only one optimum is required.
assumptions_latex: The problem minimizes \(c^{\mathsf T}x\) over the node-feasible set \(F_N\).
The node relaxation \(R_N\) satisfies \(F_N\subseteq R_N\), and \(U\) is the value of a feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_N=\inf_{x\in R_N}c^{\mathsf T}x\le\inf_{x\in F_N}c^{\mathsf T}x\); hence \(N\) may be pruned when \(R_N=\varnothing\) or \(L_N\ge U\), provided another solution tied at \(U\) need not be retained.

notation.meaning: Relaxation-based lower bound at node N.
Objective value of a feasible incumbent.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sufficient Conditions for Pruning an Enumeration Node

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $\mathrm{IP}^i$ be the maximization subproblem over $S^i$, with optimal value $z_{\mathrm{IP}}^i$. children.title: Implicit Enumeration Regimes
children.top_down_role: Search regimes in which large portions of the explicit solution space remain unlisted.

knowledge_statements.title: Implicit Enumeration Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite binary implicit enumeration with relaxation-based pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(\mathcal N\) with the root node and set \(U=+\infty\). Repeatedly select \(N\in\mathcal N\), remove it, and compute a valid lower bound \(L_N\). Prune \(N\) if it is infeasible or \(L_N\ge U\). Any feasible solution found while processing \(N\) may update the incumbent and \(U\). If the node is then certified resolved by a valid fathoming rule, close it; otherwise apply an exhaustive branching disjunction and insert the resulting children. Stop when \(\mathcal N=\varnothing\), and output the incumbent or declare infeasibility if none exists. Termination follows when branching never repeats an assignment and fixes at least one unresolved binary choice along every nonterminal path.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lenstra's Recursive Integer-Feasibility Algorithm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Flatness-based recursive decision procedure for integer feasibility in a full-dimensional rational polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\le b\}\) full-dimensional, first apply an algorithm returning either \(z\in P\cap\mathbb{Z}^n\) or \(d\in\mathbb{Z}^n\) with \(w_d(P)\le n(n+1)2^{n(n-1)/4}\). In the first case return Yes. In the second, set \(L=\lceil\min_{x\in P}d^\top x\rceil\) and \(U=\lfloor\max_{x\in P}d^\top x\rfloor\). If \(L>U\), return No. Otherwise, for each integer \(k\in[L,U]\), transform \(Ax\le b,\ d^\top x=k\) into an integrally equivalent system \(ADy\le b'_k\) in \(n-1\) variables and recurse; return Yes iff some recursive call returns Yes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The algorithm first finds either an integer point or a bounded-width integer direction. In the latter case it enumerates all integral hyperplane levels intersecting the polytope, converts each slice to an equivalent problem in one fewer dimension, and recursively decides whether any slice contains an integer point.
assumptions_latex: P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\le b\}\text{ is a full-dimensional polytope}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The recursive procedure returns Yes exactly when }P\cap\mathbb{Z}^n\ne\varnothing.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: General Branch-and-Bound Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic minimization search using subproblem bounds, incumbents, pruning, and branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the active list as $L=\{P(X)\}$ and, if available, an incumbent $x^*$ with value $v^*=f(x^*)$; otherwise set $v^*=+\infty$. Repeatedly select one or more active subproblems, compute a lower bound $LB_i$ for each (taking $LB_i=+\infty$ when infeasible), and fathom every subproblem with $LB_i\ge v^*$. Update the incumbent whenever a better feasible solution is found. Partition each remaining selected region $X_i$ into smaller regions and add the resulting subproblems to $L$. When $L=\varnothing$, terminate and return $x^*$ as an optimal solution of $(P)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start with the original problem as the active node and an available feasible incumbent, or an infinite incumbent value if none is known. Repeatedly select active nodes, compute lower bounds, discard infeasible nodes and nodes whose lower bound is no better than the incumbent, update the incumbent with better feasible solutions, and branch the remaining nodes into smaller regions. When no active nodes remain, return the incumbent as optimal.
assumptions_latex: LB_i\text{ is a valid lower bound for }P(X_i).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L=\varnothing\implies x^*\text{ is an optimal solution of }(P).

children.title: Pruning Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions under which weak bounds or poor branching cause excessive tree growth.

assumptions_latex: The problem is \(\min\{x:x\in\{0,1\}\}\), whose optimum is \(0\).
A feasible incumbent of value \(U=1\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Using the invalid node lower bound \(L_N=1\) prunes the root under \(L_N\ge U\) and incorrectly returns value \(1\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At the root, \(F_N=\{0,1\}\), so a valid lower bound must not exceed \(0\). Suppose instead that an erroneous relaxation or bound computation reports \(L_N=1\). With incumbent \(U=1\), the usual test \(L_N\ge U\) prunes the root, although the feasible point \(x=0\) improves the incumbent. Thus bound-based pruning is sound only when the relaxation contains \(F_N\) and its objective value is a genuine lower bound. Analogously, nonexhaustive branching can lose feasible solutions before any bound is evaluated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pruning can discard the optimum when a purported lower bound overestimates the node optimum; nonexhaustive branching creates the same loss by omission.

children.title: Cut Integration
children.top_down_role: Placement and lifecycle of generated inequalities within tree search.

assumptions_latex: At node \(N\), the relaxation \(R_N\) contains its integer-feasible set \(F_N\).
Each generated inequality is certified either globally valid or valid under the node's ancestral restrictions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Adding certified cuts preserves \(F_N\), strengthens the node bound monotonically for minimization, and remains sound when local cuts are confined to their valid subtree.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity-preserving cut-loop integration within branch-and-cut search.

source_refs.locator: 1.2.2 The Cutting Plane Method p. 11

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Solve the current node relaxation and obtain \(\bar x\). If a separator returns \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\) with \(a^{\mathsf T}\bar x>b\), verify its validity domain, add it to \(R_N\), and reoptimize; repeat until a stopping rule fires. Store a globally valid cut for reuse at any node, but store a cut valid only under ancestral restrictions locally within that subtree. For minimization, each addition replaces \(R_N\) by \(R_N\cap\{x:a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\}\), so the relaxation bound cannot decrease. If no further cut is selected and the node remains unresolved, branch or invoke another authorized search component.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch-and-cut repeatedly separates, validates, adds, and reoptimizes cuts, retaining local cuts only where valid and branching when the cut loop stops.

children.title: Solver Search Coordination

knowledge_statements.title: Solver Search Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic minimization-oriented branch-and-cut coordination with valid node bounds, incumbents, branching, and node-valid cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the active-node set with a root node representing every integer-feasible solution and set the incumbent value to \(U=+\infty\) unless a verified feasible incumbent is known. Repeatedly select an active node \(v\), solve its current relaxation to obtain a valid lower bound \(L_v\), and optionally add cuts valid for every integer-feasible solution represented by \(v\) before reoptimizing. Fathom \(v\) if its relaxation is infeasible or if \(L_v\geq U\). If an optimal relaxation solution is verified integer-feasible with value \(z<U\), set \(U:=z\) and fathom \(v\). Otherwise branch into children whose integer-feasible regions partition the integer-feasible region represented by \(v\). Any other verified feasible solution of value \(z<U\) may also update \(U:=z\). Stop with a global certificate when the active-node set is empty, or, when it is nonempty and \(U<+\infty\), when \(U-\min_v L_v\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coordinate node selection, valid cuts, incumbent updates, branching, and fathoming while preserving coverage of every unresolved integer-feasible solution. Exhausting the active nodes proves optimality or infeasibility, and a finite incumbent within the global lower-bound tolerance is epsilon-optimal.
assumptions_latex: The mixed-integer problem is a minimization problem, and the incumbent value is \(U\in\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\).
The root represents every integer-feasible solution, and throughout the search every integer-feasible solution not already dominated by the incumbent is represented by an active node.
Every processed node \(v\) is solved sufficiently to provide a valid relaxation lower bound \(L_v\), and branching children partition the integer-feasible region represented by \(v\).
Every generated cut is valid for all integer-feasible solutions represented by the node where it is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the active-node set becomes empty, a finite incumbent is globally optimal, while \(U=+\infty\) certifies infeasibility. If the active-node set is nonempty, \(U<+\infty\), and \(U-\min_v L_v\leq\varepsilon\), the incumbent is \(\varepsilon\)-optimal in objective value.

notation.meaning: valid lower bound at active node \(v\)

children.title: Presolve Interaction
children.top_down_role: Effects of model transformations on later search components.

assumptions_latex: The original mixed-integer feasible set is \(F\) and objective function is \(f\).
Presolve produces a reduced feasible set \(F'\), objective \(f'\), and a reconstruction map \(R:F'\to F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Solving the presolved problem preserves feasibility status and optimal value, and any reduced optimum reconstructs to an original optimum.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness contract for presolve transformations used before and during mixed-integer tree search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A presolve transformation is search-compatible when \(F=\varnothing\) if and only if \(F'=\varnothing\), and, whenever \(F'\neq\varnothing\), it supplies a map \(R:F'\to F\) satisfying \(f(R(y))=f'(y)\) for every \(y\in F'\) and \(\inf_{x\in F}f(x)=\inf_{y\in F'}f'(y)\). Consequently, an optimizer \(y^*\) of the reduced problem reconstructs as an optimizer \(R(y^*)\) of the original problem. During tree search, every node-specific reduction must satisfy the same conditions for that node's restricted feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid presolve reduction preserves infeasibility and optimal value and provides a reconstruction map from every reduced optimum to an original optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Presolve Interaction

children.title: Primal Heuristic Interaction
children.top_down_role: Roles of incumbent-producing heuristics within integrated search.

assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem with incumbent value \(U\).
A primal heuristic returns only solutions verified to satisfy every original constraint and integrality requirement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted heuristic solution preserves correctness, can improve the incumbent, and may only increase the set of nodes pruned by valid lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of verified primal-heuristic solutions on incumbents and bound-based pruning in minimization search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When a primal heuristic produces a verified feasible point \(\hat x\), update the incumbent by \(U:=\min\{U,f(\hat x)\}\). For every active node \(v\) with valid lower bound \(L_v\), pruning under the rule \(L_v\geq U\) remains valid because no feasible solution in that node can improve the incumbent. Failure of a heuristic to return a point changes neither bounds nor correctness. A candidate that has not been checked against the original constraints and integrality conditions cannot be used as an incumbent or as a basis for pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Verified heuristic solutions improve the incumbent and strengthen bound pruning; heuristic failure is harmless, while unverified candidates cannot justify pruning.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-dimension integer linear optimization via lattice reduction, rounding, flatness, and lower-dimensional recursion.

children.title: Dynamic Programming State Spaces
children.top_down_role: State representations for knapsack-type and structured integer programs.

assumptions_latex: Items have integer weights \(w_i\geq 0\), values \(v_i\), and capacity \(W\geq 0\).
Each item may be selected at most once.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The terminal value \(V_n(W)\) equals the optimum value of the zero-one knapsack problem.

notation.meaning: best value using the first \(i\) items with capacity \(s\)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical resource-indexed dynamic-programming state space for zero-one knapsack.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define states \((i,s)\) for \(i\in\{0,\ldots,n\}\) and \(s\in\{0,\ldots,W\}\), where \(V_i(s)\) is the maximum value obtainable from items \(1,\ldots,i\) with total weight at most \(s\). Initialize \(V_0(s)=0\). For \(i\geq1\), set \(V_i(s)=V_{i-1}(s)\) when \(s<w_i\), and otherwise set \(V_i(s)=\max\{V_{i-1}(s),V_{i-1}(s-w_i)+v_i\}\). The state records precisely the processed prefix and residual resource information needed for future decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For zero-one knapsack, a state indexed by item prefix and capacity supports an exact recurrence whose terminal value is optimal.
knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic Programming State Spaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The state representation and zero-one knapsack recurrence are precise and fit the leaf, but no source or locator is provided.

children.title: Pseudopolynomial Complexity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Runtime regimes governed by numerical magnitudes rather than encoding length alone.

assumptions_latex: The zero-one knapsack capacity \(W\) and weights \(w_i\) are nonnegative integers.
Arithmetic and comparison of table entries take constant time in the pseudopolynomial operation model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The dynamic program uses \(O(nW)\) operations and \(O(W)\) working memory, hence is pseudopolynomial rather than polynomial in binary input length.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operation and memory bounds for the capacity-indexed zero-one knapsack dynamic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Evaluating each state \((i,s)\) once for \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and \(s\in\{0,\ldots,W\}\) requires \(O(nW)\) arithmetic and comparison operations. Retaining only the previous and current rows, or updating capacities in descending order, reduces working storage to \(O(W)\). Because binary encoding contributes only \(O(\log(W+1))\) bits for the capacity, \(W\) may be exponential in the input length \(L\). Thus the bound is polynomial in numerical magnitudes but need not be polynomial in \(L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Capacity-indexed knapsack takes order nW time and W memory, which is polynomial in capacity but potentially exponential in its binary encoding length.
knowledge_statements.title: Pseudopolynomial Complexity Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The operation, storage, and binary-encoding claims are consistent and the complexity-bound kind is appropriate, but they lack a cited source with a specific locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pseudopolynomial Time and the Subset-Sum Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of pseudopolynomial running time, the subset-sum example, and the limitation of ordinary polynomial reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \text{An algorithm runs in pseudopolynomial time if its running time is polynomial in the length of the data under unary encoding. Since unary encoding represents an integer }k\text{ by }k\text{ symbols, an }O(nb)\text{-time algorithm for subset sum is pseudopolynomial. In general, }X_1\le_p X_2\text{ and pseudopolynomial solvability of }X_2\text{ do not imply pseudopolynomial solvability of }X_1.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An algorithm is pseudopolynomial when its running time is polynomial in the unary-encoded input length. Because unary encoding of b has length b, the O(nb) subset-sum algorithm is pseudopolynomial. An ordinary polynomial reduction to a pseudopolynomially solvable problem does not generally give a pseudopolynomial algorithm for the source problem.
assumptions_latex: \text{Running time is compared with input length under unary encoding.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathrm{SubsetSum}}(n,b)=O(nb)\text{ is pseudopolynomial, while }X_2\in\mathrm{PseudoP}\not\Rightarrow X_1\in\mathrm{PseudoP}\text{ for an arbitrary polynomial reduction.}

children.title: State Compression Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural limits on reducing or aggregating dynamic-programming states.

assumptions_latex: A dynamic program has states \(s\), feasible continuations \(C(s)\), and continuation values \(J(s,a)\).
Two states are merged and represented by one common compressed state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact compression is valid under continuation equivalence; merging states lacking that equivalence can change feasibility or the optimal value.

notation.meaning: set of feasible continuations from state \(s\)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness boundary for merging dynamic-programming states that share a compressed representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sufficient exactness condition for \(\phi(s)=\phi(t)\) is \(C(s)=C(t)\) and \(J(s,a)=J(t,a)\) for every \(a\in C(s)\), up to any state-independent offset explicitly retained by the compression. Under this condition, replacing \(s\) and \(t\) by one state preserves all attainable terminal values. Without it, compression may be invalid: in knapsack, merging two states with different used weights while retaining only the item index can admit a continuation exceeding capacity or discard a feasible valuable continuation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: States may be merged exactly when they have equivalent feasible continuations and continuation values; otherwise compression can alter feasibility or optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: State Compression Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, but the abstract continuation-equivalence criterion and its claimed preservation of all terminal values need a source defining the dynamic-programming framework precisely.

children.title: Encoding-Length Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Dependence of tractability claims on binary, unary, or bounded-value encodings.

assumptions_latex: A numerical parameter \(M\geq1\) is encoded in binary using \(\ell=\lceil\log_2(M+1)\rceil\) bits.
An algorithm performs \(\Theta(M^k)\) operations for fixed \(k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The operation count is exponential in the parameter's binary encoding length and therefore is not a polynomial-time bound in input length.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes dependence on a numerical magnitude from dependence on its binary representation length.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: From \(\ell=\lceil\log_2(M+1)\rceil\), one has \(2^{\ell-1}-1\leq M<2^\ell\). Hence a running time \(\Theta(M^k)\) can grow as \(2^{\Theta(k\ell)}\). It is polynomial in the numerical magnitude \(M\), but exponential in the number of bits \(\ell\) used to encode that magnitude. Consequently, a dynamic program indexed through all values \(0,\ldots,M\) is pseudopolynomial unless additional structure bounds \(M\) polynomially in the full input length.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A runtime polynomial in a parameter's value can be exponential in the bits encoding it, which explains the pseudopolynomial boundary.
knowledge_statements.title: Encoding-Length Sensitivity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The encoding-length distinction is mathematically correct and fits the leaf, but the record contains no citation with an inspectable locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Relaxation of a Maximization Integer Program
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General objective-function relaxation, allowing both feasible-set enlargement and objective majorization on the original feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the maximization problem \(z_{\mathrm{IP}}=\max\{cx:x\in S\}\), a problem \(z_R=\max\{z_R(x):x\in S_R\}\) is a relaxation if \(S\subseteq S_R\) and \(cx\le z_R(x)\) for every \(x\in S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a maximization integer program over S with objective cx, a maximization problem over S_R is a relaxation when S is contained in S_R and its relaxed objective is at least cx at every original feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\subseteq S_R\quad\text{and}\quad (\forall x\in S)\;cx\le z_R(x)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weak-Dual Bound and Unboundedness Consequence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value and feasibility implications of an abstract weak dual of a maximization integer program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let DP be a weak dual of the maximization problem IP. If DP is feasible, then \(z_{\mathrm{IP}}\le z_D\). If DP is unbounded below, then IP is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any feasible weak dual supplies an upper bound on the maximization integer-program value. If the weak-dual minimization objective is unbounded below, the integer program has no feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S_D\ne\varnothing\Rightarrow z_{\mathrm{IP}}\le z_D,\qquad z_D=-\infty\Rightarrow S=\varnothing

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weak Dual of a Maximization Integer Program
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract weak duality defined by uniform objective domination over every primal-feasible and dual-feasible pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(z_{\mathrm{IP}}=\max\{cx:x\in S\}\), a minimization problem \(z_D=\min\{z_D(u):u\in S_D\}\) is a weak dual if \(z_D(u)\ge cx\) for every \(x\in S\) and every \(u\in S_D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimization problem is a weak dual of a maximization integer program when every dual-feasible objective value is at least the objective value of every primal-feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\forall x\in S)(\forall u\in S_D)\;z_D(u)\ge cx

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consequences for a maximization integer program and any relaxation satisfying feasible-set inclusion and objective majorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let RP be a relaxation of the maximization problem IP. If RP is infeasible, then IP is infeasible. If IP is feasible, then \(z_{\mathrm{IP}}\le z_R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a valid relaxation is infeasible, the original integer program is infeasible. Whenever the original maximization problem is feasible, its optimal value does not exceed the relaxation value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (S_R=\varnothing\Rightarrow S=\varnothing)\quad\text{and}\quad(S\ne\varnothing\Rightarrow z_{\mathrm{IP}}\le z_R)

children.title: Lagrangian Relaxation
children.top_down_role: Dual relaxation based on selected complicating constraints.

assumptions_latex: The primal problem is \(p^*=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ g(x)\leq0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Lagrangian dual value \(d^*=\sup_{\lambda\geq0}q(\lambda)\) is a valid lower bound on \(p^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak Lagrangian duality for a minimization problem with relaxed inequality constraints and nonnegative multipliers.

source_refs.locator: 3.1 Lagrangian Relaxation and Dual Formulation p. 45
3.3 Lagrangian relaxation p. 24
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\lambda\geq0\), define \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^\top g(x)\) and \(q(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in X}L(x,\lambda)\). If \(x\) is primal feasible, then \(\lambda^\top g(x)\leq0\), so \(q(\lambda)\leq L(x,\lambda)\leq f(x)\). Therefore \(q(\lambda)\leq p^*\) for every admissible multiplier, and the Lagrangian dual problem \(d^*=\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m}q(\lambda)\) satisfies \(d^*\leq p^*\). Equality is not guaranteed for a nonconvex or integer primal problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualizing inequality constraints with nonnegative multipliers yields a concave dual function whose supremum is a valid lower bound, possibly with a duality gap.
knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Relaxation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subgradient stepsize guaranteeing strict distance reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step result for projected ascent on a concave Lagrangian dual function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mu^{k+1}=[\mu^k+s^kg^k]^+\), where \(g^k\) is a subgradient of the concave dual function \(q\) at a nonoptimal \(\mu^k\). For every dual optimal solution \(\mu^*\), if \(0<s^k<2\bigl(q(\mu^*)-q(\mu^k)\bigr)/\|g^k\|^2\), then \(\|\mu^{k+1}-\mu^*\|<\|\mu^k-\mu^*\|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a nonoptimal multiplier, any positive stepsize smaller than twice the current dual-value gap divided by the squared subgradient norm makes the projected subgradient iterate strictly closer to every dual optimum.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constraint-Dropping Relaxation and Its Lagrangian Extension
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Construction of a relaxation for an integer maximization problem by removing selected inequalities, together with the defining idea of adding those inequalities to the objective using multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z=\max\{c^\top x:Ax\le b,\ x\in X\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\}\). Removing the constraints \(Ax\le b\) yields \(Z'=\max\{c^\top x:x\in X\}\), which is a relaxation and satisfies \(Z'\ge Z\). A Lagrangian relaxation retains the effect of the removed constraints by adding multiplier-weighted terms for them to the objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Removing constraints from an integer maximization problem enlarges its feasible set and gives an upper-bounding relaxation. Lagrangian relaxation extends this idea by placing multiplier-weighted versions of the removed constraints in the objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Z'=\max\{c^\top x:x\in X\}\ge Z

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lagrangian Relaxation, Weak Duality, and Dual Problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: For a constrained minimization problem over a possibly discrete set \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\) and \(\mu\in\mathbb R^l\), define \(L(x,\lambda,\mu)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i(g_i(x)-b_i)+\sum_{k=1}^l\mu_k(h_k(x)-c_k)\) and \(d(\lambda,\mu)=\min_{x\in X}L(x,\lambda,\mu)\). If \(S=\{x\in X:g_i(x)\le b_i,\ h_k(x)=c_k\}\), then \(d(\lambda,\mu)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in S\). Thus the Lagrangian relaxation supplies a primal lower bound, and the dual problem is \(\max_{\lambda\ge0,\mu}d(\lambda,\mu)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative inequality multipliers and unrestricted equality multipliers define the Lagrangian. Minimizing it over X gives a lower bound for every feasible primal point, and the dual maximizes that bound over the multipliers.
assumptions_latex: S=\{x\in X:g_i(x)\le b_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m;\ h_k(x)=c_k,\ k=1,\ldots,l\}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m,\ \forall\mu\in\mathbb R^l,\ \forall x\in S,\quad d(\lambda,\mu)\le f(x)

children.title: Surrogate Relaxation
children.top_down_role: Relaxation based on weighted aggregation of constraints.

assumptions_latex: The primal problem is \(p^*=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ g(x)\leq0\}\).
The surrogate multiplier is nonzero and satisfies \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\setminus\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The surrogate optimum \(s(\lambda)\) is a valid lower bound on \(p^*\), and its supremum over admissible multipliers defines the surrogate dual bound.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative aggregation of multiple minimization constraints into one surrogate constraint.

source_refs.locator: 4.1.2 Surrogate dual search p. 99

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\setminus\{0\}\), the surrogate relaxation replaces \(g(x)\leq0\) by the single aggregated constraint \(\lambda^\top g(x)\leq0\). Its feasible set and value are \(S(\lambda)=\{x\in X:\lambda^\top g(x)\leq0\}\) and \(s(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in S(\lambda)}f(x)\). Since every primal-feasible point belongs to \(S(\lambda)\), one has \(s(\lambda)\leq p^*\). The surrogate dual value is \(s^*=\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\setminus\{0\}}s(\lambda)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A surrogate relaxation nonnegatively aggregates constraints into one inequality; minimizing over the enlarged feasible set gives a lower bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Surrogate Relaxation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Surrogate relaxation and surrogate dual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative weighted aggregation of inequality-form complicating constraints in a maximization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\mathrm{IP}(Q)\) with complicating constraints \(A^1x\le b^1\) and \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^{m_1}\), define
\[
z_{\mathrm{SD}}(\lambda)=\max\{cx:\lambda^\top A^1x\le\lambda^\top b^1,\ x\in Q\}.
\]
This is the surrogate relaxation, and its surrogate dual is
\[
z_{\mathrm{SD}}=\min_{\lambda\ge0}z_{\mathrm{SD}}(\lambda).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A surrogate relaxation replaces the complicating inequalities by one nonnegative weighted aggregate. The surrogate dual minimizes the resulting relaxation value over all nonnegative multiplier vectors.
assumptions_latex: A^1x\le b^1\text{ are the complicating constraints of }\mathrm{IP}(Q)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z_{\mathrm{SD}}(\lambda)=\max\{cx:\lambda^\top A^1x\le\lambda^\top b^1,\ x\in Q\},\qquad z_{\mathrm{SD}}=\min_{\lambda\ge0}z_{\mathrm{SD}}(\lambda).

children.title: Dual-Bound Comparison
children.top_down_role: Relative bound-strength regimes across the two relaxation families.

assumptions_latex: The same minimization problem and multiplier \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\setminus\{0\}\) define both Lagrangian and surrogate relaxations.
The relevant infima are interpreted in the extended-real sense.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every admissible \(\lambda\), \(q(\lambda)\leq s(\lambda)\leq p^*\), and consequently \(d^*\leq s^*\leq p^*\).

notation.meaning: Lagrangian, surrogate, and primal optimal values

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise and optimized lower-bound ordering for matched Lagrangian and surrogate multipliers.

source_refs.locator: 3.1 Lagrangian Relaxation and Dual Formulation p. 45; 4.1.2 Surrogate dual search p. 99

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\setminus\{0\}\). For every \(x\in S(\lambda)\), one has \(f(x)+\lambda^\top g(x)\leq f(x)\). Since the Lagrangian infimum ranges over all \(X\), while the surrogate infimum ranges over \(S(\lambda)\subseteq X\), it follows that \(q(\lambda)\leq s(\lambda)\). Both values are lower bounds on \(p^*\). Taking suprema over the common multiplier domain gives \(d^*=\sup_{\lambda\geq0}q(\lambda)\leq s^*=\sup_{\lambda\geq0,\lambda\neq0}s(\lambda)\leq p^*\), with the harmless multiplier-domain convention handled separately at \(\lambda=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For matched nonnegative multipliers, the surrogate bound dominates the Lagrangian bound, while both remain no greater than the primal optimum.

children.top_down_role: Structural regimes affecting the treatment of relaxation multipliers.

assumptions_latex: For each iterate \(\lambda^k\geq0\), an inner solver returns \(x^k\in\arg\min_{x\in X}\{f(x)+(\lambda^k)^\top g(x)\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method outputs the best computed dual bound; convergence to a dual optimum requires additional stepsize, boundedness, and attainability hypotheses.

source_refs.locator: 3.2 Dual Search Methods p. 52
3.4 Optimal Generating Multiplier and Optimal Primal-Dual Pair p. 77

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(\lambda^0\in\mathbb R_+^m\). At iteration \(k\), compute \(x^k\in\arg\min_{x\in X}\{f(x)+(\lambda^k)^\top g(x)\}\), so that \(g(x^k)\) is a supergradient of the concave function \(q\) at \(\lambda^k\). Update \(\lambda^{k+1}=\Pi_{\mathbb R_+^m}(\lambda^k+\alpha_k g(x^k))\). Retain \(\max_{0\leq j\leq k}q(\lambda^j)\) as the certified dual bound and stop under a declared iteration, stationarity, or primal-dual-gap rule. Convergence requires separately stated conditions, such as bounded supergradients and suitable diminishing stepsizes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected subgradient search repeatedly solves the Lagrangian subproblem, updates nonnegative multipliers, and retains the best computed dual lower bound.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each \(k\), substitute \(x_k=\sum_{r\in R_k}v^{kr}\lambda_{kr}\), where \(\lambda_{kr}\ge 0\) and \(\sum_{r\in R_k}\lambda_{kr}=1\). Then
\[
\min \left\{\sum_{k=1}^K\sum_{r\in R_k}c_k^{\mathsf T}v^{kr}\lambda_{kr}:\sum_{k=1}^K\sum_{r\in R_k}A_kv^{kr}\lambda_{kr}=b,\ \sum_{r\in R_k}\lambda_{kr}=1\ \forall k,\ \lambda\ge0\right\}
\]
is an extended formulation whose projection under \(x_k=\sum_rv^{kr}\lambda_{kr}\) equals the feasible region of the original block-angular linear program.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace each block vector by a convex combination of its extreme points; linking and convexity constraints then form an equivalent extended master formulation.

source_refs.locator: 4.3.2 The restricted master model p. 64

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The restricted master problem is
\[
\min \left\{\sum_{k=1}^K\sum_{r\in S_k}c_k^{\mathsf T}v^{kr}\lambda_{kr}:\sum_{k=1}^K\sum_{r\in S_k}A_kv^{kr}\lambda_{kr}=b,\ \sum_{r\in S_k}\lambda_{kr}=1\ \forall k,\ \lambda\ge0\right\}.
\]
It retains every master row but only columns indexed by \(S_k\). For minimization its feasible region is contained in that of the full master, so its optimal value cannot be smaller than the full-master optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The restricted master keeps all master constraints but only generated columns, giving a restricted approximation whose dual prices drive further column generation.

Each candidate column for block \(k\) is induced by some \(x_k\in X_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A negative optimum produces an improving column; nonnegative optima for every block certify optimality of the restricted master for the full linear master.

source_refs.locator: 4.3.1 A simple column generation method p. 42
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each block \(k\), solve the pricing problem
\[
\rho_k=\min_{x_k\in X_k}\bar c_k(x_k),\qquad \bar c_k(x_k)=(c_k-A_k^{\mathsf T}\pi)^{\mathsf T}x_k-\sigma_k.
\]
If \(\rho_k<0\), return an optimizer \(x_k^*\) and append its induced column to the restricted master. If \(\rho_k\ge0\) for every \(k\), return the certificate that no omitted column has negative reduced cost. Tolerances may replace strict comparisons, but must be applied consistently to pricing and master optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pricing minimizes reduced cost over each block. A negative value yields a new column; nonnegative values for all blocks certify full-master LP optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Pricing Subproblems

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize finite column sets \(S^0\). At iteration \(t\), solve the restricted master over \(S^t\), obtain dual multipliers \((\pi^t,\sigma^t)\), and solve every required pricing problem. If the least reduced cost satisfies \(\rho^t\ge0\), stop and output the restricted-master primal solution. Otherwise append at least one column attaining negative reduced cost and set \(S^{t+1}=S^t\cup G^t\), where \(G^t\) is the set of newly accepted columns. Stabilized or multi-column regimes may alter dual selection or \(G^t\), but not the exact stopping certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve a restricted master, price omitted columns, add improving columns, and stop when exact pricing finds none with negative reduced cost.

children.title: Benders Decomposition Family

children.title: Classical Benders Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Generated-constraint decomposition based on mathematical programming subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Classical Benders Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical linear Benders decomposition in minimization form, excluding subproblems unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U=\{u\ge0:B^{\mathsf T}u\le d\}\). For fixed \(x\in X\), if the subproblem is feasible, its finite value is \(Q(x)=\max_{u\in U}u^{\mathsf T}(b-Ax)\). Let \(R\) contain the extreme rays of the recession cone of \(U\). The Benders master is
\[
\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x+\theta:x\in X,\ \theta\ge u^{\mathsf T}(b-Ax)\ \forall u\in\operatorname{ext}(U),\ r^{\mathsf T}(b-Ax)\le0\ \forall r\in R\}.
\]
The extreme-point inequalities are optimality cuts and the extreme-ray inequalities are feasibility cuts. Under the stated assumptions, this master has the same optimal value and optimal \(x\)-solutions as the original problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When every fixed-master linear subproblem is either infeasible or has a finite optimum, dual extreme points describe its cost and dual recession rays exclude infeasible master decisions.
assumptions_latex: Consider \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x+d^{\mathsf T}y:Ax+By\ge b,\ x\in X,\ y\ge0\}\), where \(X\) is the master domain.
For every \(x\in X\), the fixed-\(x\) linear subproblem is either infeasible or has a finite attained optimum; it is never unbounded below.
The dual feasible polyhedron \(U=\{u\ge0:B^{\mathsf T}u\le d\}\) is nonempty, and linear-programming strong duality and the alternative theorem apply.
The original problem has a finite attained optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Adding all dual extreme-point and extreme-ray cuts yields an exact master representation of the original problem.

notation.meaning: dual feasible set of the fixed-master subproblem
extreme rays of the recession cone of the dual feasible set
finite value of the feasible fixed-master subproblem

children.title: Logic-Based Benders Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Generated-constraint decomposition using inference from combinatorial subproblems.

assumptions_latex: The master domain \(X\) is discrete or mixed-integer, and fixing \(x\in X\) defines a subproblem with value \(Q(x)\).
For each evaluated \(\bar x\), a valid inference procedure can derive \(B_{\bar x}(x)\le Q(x)\) for every \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the accumulated cuts represent \(Q\) exactly on all relevant master assignments and the search terminates, the returned incumbent is globally optimal.

notation.meaning: subproblem value induced by master decision x
logic-derived lower-bounding function from assignment bar x

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract minimization-form logic-based Benders principle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a relaxation containing \(x\in X\) and an epigraph variable \(\theta\). At an incumbent master assignment \(\bar x\), solve or analyze the subproblem. If it is feasible, derive a valid logic-based optimality cut \(\theta\ge B_{\bar x}(x)\) satisfying \(B_{\bar x}(x)\le Q(x)\) for all \(x\in X\), preferably with equality at \(\bar x\). If it is infeasible, derive a valid constraint excluding \(\bar x\) and any other assignments justified by the same inference. Reoptimize and repeat until the master bound meets the incumbent value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Logic-based Benders replaces LP-dual cuts with problem-specific deductions that lower-bound subproblem cost or exclude master assignments causing infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Logic-Based Benders Decomposition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The abstract logic-based Benders principle is plausible, but no source is supplied for its generalized inference cuts or termination claim. An authoritative logic-based Benders reference with a specific locator is required.

children.title: Master-Subproblem Partitioning
children.top_down_role: Placement of complicating variables and residual decisions across decomposition components.

assumptions_latex: The optimization variables can be partitioned as \((x,y)\), with \(x\in X\) retained in the master.
Fixing \(x\) leaves a well-defined subproblem \(Q(x)=\inf\{d^{\mathsf T}y:(x,y)\in F\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The partition is exact when the master can enforce the epigraph condition \(\theta\ge Q(x)\) and subproblem infeasibility for fixed \(x\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F\subseteq X\times Y\), define
\[
Q(x)=\inf\{d^{\mathsf T}y:(x,y)\in F\},
\]
using \(Q(x)=+\infty\) when no feasible \(y\) exists. A master-subproblem partition is Benders-valid if the original problem equals
\[
\inf_{x\in X}\{c^{\mathsf T}x+Q(x)\}
\]
and the selected subproblem mechanism can generate valid master constraints that enforce both \(\theta\ge Q(x)\) and exclusion of points with \(Q(x)=+\infty\). Computational usefulness additionally requires that fixing \(x\) makes the subproblem materially easier or separable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid partition retains master variables and represents the eliminated variables through an exact value function, including infeasible fixed-master decisions.

A feasibility-cut response consists of a predicate \(g(x)\le0\) such that \(Q(x)<+\infty\) implies \(g(x)\le0\); the master may safely add that inequality. A response is exact at \(\bar x\) when \(\ell(\bar x)=Q(\bar x)\), or separating when \(g(\bar x)>0\). Each response must retain the data needed to check its asserted validity class.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widehat Q(x)=\sup\{\ell(x):\ell\in\mathcal C\}\). Validity of the cuts gives only \(\widehat Q(x)\le Q(x)\). Exact Benders reformulation requires \(\widehat Q(x)=Q(x)\) on every master point relevant to optimality, together with feasibility cuts that exclude every \(x\) satisfying \(Q(x)=+\infty\). children.title: Callback Lifecycle Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Solver events, execution contexts, and permitted callback operations.

assumptions_latex: A solver emits events with documented contexts, and each callback action is permitted only in specified event contexts.
Every dynamically submitted constraint or column is globally or locally valid for the scope declared to the solver.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lifecycle preserves solver correctness only when observations and mutations obey their context, validity, locality, and reentrancy contracts.

notation.meaning: callback-visible solver state at event e
set of actions permitted in event context e

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract lifecycle contract independent of a particular solver API.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Register a callback map \(H\) before optimization. Whenever the solver emits event \(e\) with visible state \(s_e\), evaluate \(H(e,s_e)\) and return only actions in \(\mathcal A(e)\), such as submitting a valid cut, rejecting an incumbent, or requesting termination. An action carrying a constraint must declare whether its validity is global or restricted to the current node. The callback must not read unavailable solution values, invoke forbidden reentrant optimization, or retain transient solver objects beyond their documented lifetime. On termination or exception, release callback-owned state and return control according to the solver contract.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A callback may observe and modify optimization only through actions permitted at its current solver event, with explicit validity scope and object lifetime.
knowledge_statements.title: Callback Lifecycle Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Callback event availability, permitted mutations, locality, reentrancy, object lifetime, and exception behavior are solver-specific. With no documented solver API or authoritative interface source, the proposed lifecycle contract cannot be reliably reviewed.

children.title: Cut Pool Management
children.top_down_role: Storage, activation, retirement, and reuse of dynamically generated inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Pool Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity-preserving abstract cut-pool policy for branch-and-cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Store each cut \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\) in \(\mathcal P\) with its validity scope, origin, activity count, and age \(\tau(a)\). At a relaxation solution \(\bar x\), compute \(v(a,\bar x)=a^{\mathsf T}\bar x-\beta\), select only scope-compatible cuts with violation above tolerance, rank them by efficacy or orthogonality, and activate a bounded subset. Increment ages of inactive cuts, reset or reduce ages of useful cuts, and retire pool records exceeding an age or storage threshold. Retirement from \(\mathcal P\) does not by itself assert removal of an already active solver row. If the solver removes a valid active cut, the relaxation may weaken but no original feasible integer solution is excluded. A retired cut may be regenerated, and a local cut must not be reused outside its validity subtree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut pool tracks validity scope, violation, efficacy, and age. Retiring a cut can weaken a relaxation but does not invalidate the original integer model, provided local cuts are never used outside their valid subtrees.
assumptions_latex: Every candidate cut is valid for its declared global or local domain.
Violation and efficacy are evaluated against a solver state in which the cut may legally be applied.
The managed cut pool is distinguished from the solver's current set of active relaxation rows.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pool operations preserve validity when only scope-compatible valid cuts are activated; retiring or removing a cut may weaken bounds or performance but does not exclude any solution feasible for the original integer model.

notation.meaning: violation of cut a at point x
activity or age counter for cut a

children.title: Pricing Oracle Management
children.top_down_role: Coordination and reliability of dynamically invoked pricing components.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing Oracle Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact column-generation pricing for a minimization restricted master problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an initial feasible column set \(J_0\subseteq J\), set \(k=0\). Solve the restricted master over \(J_k\) and obtain a dual vector \(\pi^k\). Call a global pricing oracle to compute \(r_k=\min_{j\in J}\{c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi^k\}\) and a minimizing column \(j_k\). If \(r_k<-\varepsilon_p\), set \(J_{k+1}=J_k\cup\{j_k\}\) and repeat. Otherwise stop and return the restricted-master solution. The stopping result certifies absence of improving columns within \(\varepsilon_p\) only when the oracle solves the full pricing problem globally; an approximate oracle requires a valid error bound incorporated into the stopping test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve the restricted master and globally minimize reduced cost. Add a sufficiently negative column; otherwise stop with a pricing-tolerance certificate.
assumptions_latex: The pricing oracle ranges over the complete column set \(J\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination, \(c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi^k\ge -\varepsilon_p\) for every \(j\in J\).
review_flags: pricing-interface source and sign convention require certification

children.title: Solver-Control Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits imposed by solver state, callback safety, and object ownership.

knowledge_statements.title: Solver-Control Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness invariants for user actions that alter a mixed-integer solver search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A user control action preserves an exact-solve claim only if it maintains the solver's invariants: every global cut is valid for the original feasible set; every local cut is enforced only on its declared subtree; each submitted incumbent is independently checked against the modeled domains and constraints; and every bound used for pruning remains valid for the corresponding subproblem. Branch selection and search ordering may change exploration without changing feasibility. If the user terminates early, suppresses required processing, introduces an invalid constraint, or accepts an unchecked incumbent, the resulting status is conditional and must not be interpreted as an unconditional certificate of feasibility or optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Callbacks may steer search only while preserving feasibility, cut scope, incumbent validation, and valid bounds; otherwise the solver’s exactness certificate no longer applies.
assumptions_latex: The solver otherwise implements a correct exact mixed-integer search.
User actions occur through documented control interfaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Preservation of all stated invariants is necessary for the solver's ordinary exact-solve certificate to remain applicable.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle kind fits the solver-control leaf, but callback guarantees and the asserted necessity of independent incumbent checking are implementation-specific and potentially overbroad without authoritative solver-interface documentation.

children.title: Integrality-Tolerance Semantics
children.top_down_role: Numerical interpretation of near-integral values.

knowledge_statements.title: Integrality-Tolerance Semantics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute distance-to-lattice convention for finite integer variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an integer-index set \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and tolerance \(\varepsilon_I\ge 0\), define \(\rho_I(x)=\max_{i\in I}\operatorname{dist}(x_i,\mathbb Z)\), with \(\rho_I(x)=0\) when \(I=\varnothing\), where \(\operatorname{dist}(t,\mathbb Z)=\min_{z\in\mathbb Z}|t-z|\). A finite vector \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) is numerically integral under this convention when \(\rho_I(x)\le\varepsilon_I\). This is a solver acceptance convention, not membership in the exact lattice unless every tested distance is zero. Rounding an accepted component to a nearest integer can change other constraint residuals, so numerical integrality alone does not certify feasibility of the rounded vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vector is numerically integral when every declared integer component lies within the configured distance of an integer; with no declared integer components the test is vacuous. This is weaker than exact lattice membership.
assumptions_latex: All tested components of \(x\) are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Numerical integrality means \(\rho_I(x)\le\varepsilon_I\), not necessarily \(x_I\in\mathbb Z^{|I|}\).

notation.meaning: maximum distance of declared integer components to the integer lattice, with value zero for an empty index set

review_flags: authoritative documentation is required for solver-specific tolerance scaling

children.title: Feasibility-Tolerance Semantics
children.top_down_role: Finite-precision interpretation of constraint satisfaction.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Tolerance Semantics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaled residual convention for numerical constraint feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write every modeled constraint as \(g_j(x)\le 0\) and assign it a positive scale \(s_j\). For \(\varepsilon_F\ge0\), define the scaled feasibility residual by \(\rho_F(x)=\max_j [g_j(x)]_+/s_j\), where \([t]_+=\max\{t,0\}\). The point is numerically feasible precisely when \(\rho_F(x)\le\varepsilon_F\). Equality constraints may be represented by both inequality directions. This definition is relative to the chosen residuals and scales: it permits nonzero original-space violations and does not imply exact feasibility unless all positive residuals vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Numerical feasibility bounds every positive constraint residual after scaling; it can permit small original-space violations and is not exact feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The numerical feasibility predicate is \(\rho_F(x)\le\varepsilon_F\).
review_flags: residual normalization and row scaling vary by solver

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a coherent definition of one scaled residual convention and the content kind fits, but it must not be presented as solver tolerance semantics without a source specifying the residual normalization and scaling.

children.title: Optimality-Tolerance Semantics
children.top_down_role: Finite-precision interpretation of objective gaps and termination status.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimality-Tolerance Semantics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute-plus-relative termination test for a minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\in\mathbb R\) be the objective value of an accepted incumbent and let \(L\in\mathbb R\) be a valid global lower bound for a minimization problem, with \(L\le U\). Under the stated absolute-plus-relative convention, numerical optimality is declared when \(U-L\le\varepsilon_A+\varepsilon_R\max\{1,|U|\}\), where \(\varepsilon_A,\varepsilon_R\ge0\). This condition bounds the reported primal-dual gap under that normalization, but the tolerance test alone does not certify exact optimality. Exact optimality follows when the incumbent is exactly feasible, \(L\) is rigorous for the original problem, and the observed bounds satisfy \(U=L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For minimization, numerical termination occurs when the incumbent-minus-lower-bound gap is below the stated absolute-plus-relative threshold. Exact optimality instead requires an exactly feasible incumbent and rigorous coincident bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is the value of an accepted incumbent.
\(L\) is a valid global lower bound and \(L\le U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Numerical optimality holds when \(U-L\le\varepsilon_A+\varepsilon_R\max\{1,|U|\}\); exact optimality is certified when the required exact-feasibility and bound-validity conditions hold and \(U=L\).

notation.meaning: incumbent objective value and global lower bound

children.title: Certificate Interpretation

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Interpretation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interpretation of a tolerance-qualified mixed-integer solution certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization model, a tolerance-qualified certificate consists of a candidate \(x\), its value \(U=f(x)\), a valid lower bound \(L\), and declared tolerances. It is verifiable by recomputing the scaled constraint residual, the distance of integer components to the lattice, and the primal-dual gap. If \(\rho_F(x)\le\varepsilon_F\), \(\max_{i\in I}\operatorname{dist}(x_i,\mathbb Z)\le\varepsilon_I\), and \(U-L\le\varepsilon_A+\varepsilon_R\max\{1,|U|\}\), then the record certifies numerical feasibility, numerical integrality, and the stated gap. It does not, without exact residuals and rigorous bounds, certify exact feasibility or exact optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solver certificate supports only the feasibility, integrality, and gap predicates actually checked under its declared tolerances and bound validity.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) is independently valid for the original minimization problem.
Residual scales and all tolerances are recorded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed tests certify their numerical predicates, but exact feasibility and optimality require exact residuals, exact integrality, and rigorous zero-gap bounds.

children.title: Tolerance Interaction Regimes
children.top_down_role: Cases where multiple tolerance settings produce conflicting model interpretations.

knowledge_statements.title: Tolerance Interaction Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint acceptance requires independently checking all active numerical predicates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_{\varepsilon_F}\), \(I_{\varepsilon_I}\), and \(O_{\varepsilon_A,\varepsilon_R}\) denote the sets of solver records satisfying the declared feasibility, integrality, and optimality-gap tests. A record receives the combined numerical status only when it lies in \(F_{\varepsilon_F}\cap I_{\varepsilon_I}\cap O_{\varepsilon_A,\varepsilon_R}\). In general, none of these predicates implies either of the others. Rounding a point represented by a record in \(I_{\varepsilon_I}\) can move it outside \(F_{\varepsilon_F}\). Moreover, if a tolerance-feasible incumbent is not exactly feasible, its objective value need not be a valid primal upper bound for the original exact minimization problem, so its reported gap does not by itself certify exact optimality. The tolerances must therefore be interpreted jointly for the same model and scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasibility, integrality, and optimality-gap tolerances impose separate tests. Combined numerical acceptance requires all three, while rounding and tolerated infeasibility can affect feasibility and the validity of the reported gap for the exact problem.
assumptions_latex: All three predicates refer to the same model instance and scaling.
The reported bounds and incumbent value use the same objective convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Combined numerical acceptance is membership in \(F_{\varepsilon_F}\cap I_{\varepsilon_I}\cap O_{\varepsilon_A,\varepsilon_R}\), and this status does not alone certify exact feasibility or exact optimality.

notation.meaning: solver records satisfying the numerical feasibility test
solver records satisfying the numerical integrality test
solver records satisfying the numerical gap test

children.title: Native Discrete-Construct Semantics

knowledge_statements.title: Native Discrete-Construct Semantics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible-set semantics of native indicators, ordered sets, and finite-domain declarations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A native discrete declaration denotes a feasible set before any internal reformulation. An indicator \(z=1\Rightarrow g(x)\le0\) denotes \(\{(x,z):z\in\{0,1\},\ z=0\text{ or }g(x)\le0\}\). An SOS1 declaration on \((x_i)_{i\in S}\) permits at most one nonzero member; an SOS2 declaration with a fixed ordering permits nonzeros only at at most two adjacent positions. A discontinuous-domain declaration \(x\in\bigcup_{k=1}^m D_k\) denotes membership in that union. Any solver-generated reformulation is semantically correct only when its projection onto the declared variables equals the corresponding set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Native constructs directly define disjunctive feasible sets; any hidden reformulation must project exactly to the declared indicator, ordered-set, or union semantics.
assumptions_latex: The SOS2 ordering is fixed and unambiguous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A correct internal formulation has projection exactly equal to the feasible set denoted by the native declaration.

notation.meaning: component domains of a discontinuous union

children.title: Big-M Bound Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Validity, strength, and numerical problems caused by missing or unsuitable bounds.

children.title: Invalidly Small Big-M Values
children.top_down_role: Conditional representations that exclude intended feasible solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Invalidly Small Big-M Values
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A too-small coefficient destroys equivalence of a standard on-off constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(0<M<U\) and consider the intended on-off set \(S=\{(x,y):0\le x\le U,\ y\in\{0,1\},\ y=0\Rightarrow x=0\}\). The usual big-M inequality \(x\le My\), together with the same bounds and binary restriction, yields \(S_M\). For every \(x\in(M,U]\), the point \((x,1)\) belongs to \(S\) but not to \(S_M\). Hence \(S_M\subsetneq S\): choosing a valid activation bound below \(U\) removes intended feasible solutions and can change feasibility and the optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an on-off variable bounded by U, using M below U excludes valid active solutions with x between M and U.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The big-M formulation satisfies \(S_M\subsetneq S\).

notation.meaning: set produced by the chosen big-M inequality
valid upper bound on the active variable

children.title: Excessively Large Big-M Values
children.top_down_role: Conditional representations with weak relaxations and poor scaling.

knowledge_statements.title: Excessively Large Big-M Values
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Valid but oversized coefficients weaken relaxation and amplify scaling disparities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the on-off set with \(0\le x\le U\), \(y\in\{0,1\}\), and \(x\le My\), every \(M\ge U\) is logically valid. After relaxing \(y\in[0,1]\), however, the point \((x,y)=(U,U/M)\) is feasible. The integer hull satisfies the stronger inequality \(x\le Uy\), which this point violates by \(U-U^2/M\) whenever \(M>U\). As \(M/U\to\infty\), the relaxation permits full activation \(x=U\) with \(y\to0\), while the coefficient ratio grows. Thus validity persists, but relaxation strength and numerical scaling deteriorate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any M at least U is valid, but oversized M permits nearly zero relaxed activation at full x, weakening the relaxation and worsening scaling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(M>U\), the linear relaxation strictly contains the integer hull and includes \((U,U/M)\).

children.title: Implicit, Missing, or Infinite Bounds
children.top_down_role: Reformulations depending on unavailable or unrepresented finite bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Implicit, Missing, or Infinite Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite big-M reformulation requires a finite, represented bound on inactive violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(y=0\Rightarrow a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\) over a base set \(X\), represented by \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b+My\). Exactness requires \(M\ge M^*\), where \(M^*=\sup_{x\in X}(a^{\mathsf T}x-b)\). If \(M^*=+\infty\), no finite \(M\) makes the representation valid. If \(M^*<\infty\) but the bounds defining it are absent from the solver model or unavailable to the reformulation, validity cannot be established from the represented data. Substituting an arbitrary finite default can therefore exclude intended points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite big-M reformulation needs a finite bound on the inactive constraint’s maximum violation; infinite or unavailable bounds make finite-M validity impossible to establish.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is the intended base feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A finite exact coefficient exists only if \(M^*<+\infty\), and validity requires \(M\ge M^*\).

notation.meaning: base feasible set for continuous variables

children.title: Data-Dependent Bound Instability
children.top_down_role: Formulation quality changing sharply across instances because derived bounds are unstable.

knowledge_statements.title: Data-Dependent Bound Instability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Instance-dependent valid bounds can destroy uniform coefficient tightness or finite reformulability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For instances indexed by \(\theta\), let \(M^*(\theta)=\sup_{x\in X(\theta)}(a(\theta)^{\mathsf T}x-b(\theta))\) be the smallest valid coefficient for the implication reformulation whenever this value is finite. Suppose a modeling procedure selects \(M(\theta)\ge M^*(\theta)>0\). If \(M(\theta)/M^*(\theta)\) is unbounded over a family of instances, then the selected coefficients are not uniformly tight relative to the smallest valid coefficients. This fact alone does not imply a particular integrality-gap or numerical-conditioning bound without further structural assumptions. If arbitrarily small data perturbations can change \(M^*(\theta)\) from a finite value to \(+\infty\), then availability of a finite exact big-M reformulation is unstable across that instance family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If selected valid coefficients become arbitrarily larger than the tight instance-dependent coefficients, coefficient tightness is not uniform, although a specific relaxation-gap claim needs more structure. If nearby instances require an infinite coefficient, finite reformulability is itself unstable.
assumptions_latex: Each finite selected coefficient satisfies \(M(\theta)\ge M^*(\theta)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Unbounded \(M(\theta)/M^*(\theta)\) precludes uniform coefficient tightness, while \(M^*(\theta)=+\infty\) precludes a finite exact big-M coefficient for that instance.

notation.meaning: smallest valid instance-dependent coefficient when finite
coefficient selected by the modeling procedure
